name: East Valley Christian Fellowship - El Cajon Campus
reviewSummary:
I am the Youth Director here at East Valley Christian Fellowship, and I am so grateful that this church has become our home. My husband and I have been attending since 2023, and it has been amazing to watch the church continue to grow while still maintaining such a genuine, family atmosphere.

The people here truly care about one another and are sincerely pursuing a deeper relationship with Christ. No one pretends to be perfect, but there is a real desire to grow, learn, and become disciples of Jesus. This church has walked with our family through some of the biggest moments of our lives. They welcomed us with open arms from the very beginning, celebrated with us when we found out we were expecting our son, and have continued to support and love our family as we grow.

Being part of the youth ministry for our junior high and high school students has been such an honor. These are real teens facing real struggles, questions, and challenges, and our goal is to help guide them through life using the truth of God’s Word. We want them to put on the armor of God, turn theology into action, and become strong disciples of Christ who genuinely know Him.

One of the things I love most about East Valley is that there truly is a place for everyone. We have programs for toddlers, kids, teens, men, and women, along with Bible studies, fellowship opportunities, outreach ministries, and more.

If you are looking for a smaller, family-style church where people will genuinely know you, care for you, and grow alongside you in Christ, I highly recommend East Valley Christian Fellowship. I’ve been attending this church as both a member and worship leader for the last five years, and through every blessing and every trial, the Lord has used this church family to shape and strengthen my walk with Christ. Serving under such a faithful pastor and alongside a loving, Christ-centered community has taught me so much over the years. I can honestly say I’m a better Christian and servant today because of the consistent teaching, discipleship, encouragement, and care I’ve received here week after week.

From Tuesday Bible study, Wednesday midweek service, Thursday men’s Bible study, monthly Saturday men’s breakfasts, and Sunday service with fellowship afterward, this church places a deep emphasis on the Word of God — reading it, studying it, living it out, and encouraging one another through it. There is a genuine desire within this body to grow in wisdom, pursue holiness, love one another well, and live lives that honor and glorify Christ.

Over the years, I’ve been able to grow in my understanding of Scripture and sound doctrine while also being part of a church that believes the Holy Spirit is still active and moving today. I’ve witnessed lives transformed, gifts cultivated, and people lovingly discipled through authentic biblical community.

I’ve watched this church grow simply through word of mouth and through what I truly believe is the hand of God bringing people together to grow in truth, love, and service. Having been part of many churches and denominations throughout my life, I can confidently say that Pastor Jason has consistently lived above reproach — loving, serving, listening, and always willing to give biblical counsel with humility, wisdom, and care.

Watching each ministry begin and continue to flourish has been an incredible journey to witness. Being part of this church has grounded me more deeply in Scripture, strengthened my faith, helped me grow in the fruit of the Spirit, and continually encouraged me to pursue a life that is pleasing to God. My family has been coming here for almost 1 year and we really enjoy Sunday service. Something that is so wonderful is the different days I can come and pray or study. The women's ministry led by Michelle is amazing I learn so much and the ladies are so open to sharing, learning, and praying. My family has found a solid church home to serve in. 24 years this church has been amazing to me and my family! I highly recommend you check it out 10am on Sundays 6pm on Wednesdays!! East valley Christian fellowship is a great church Pastor Jason is a great pastor we go by the word of God and the Bible.. it's a very close-knit family...

The Life Group classes are great and there's something  for everyone!  They start @ 9 am every Sunday.  The music ministry is awesome.  Young and not-so-young will love!! We have been so impressed by the childrens and youth department and all they offer our children. Pastor Stuart's messages come directly from scripture and are always applicable to our lives. If you are looking for a church home I would highly suggest giving Eastern Shore Baptist a visit.

name: Eastland Church - Lexington Campus
reviewSummary:
My wife and I had been attending Southland for years starting in college and like most of its attendees enjoyed it. Somewhere along the line we found ourselves sitting with different people every Sunday and we started to feel like we were lacking a sense of community - something that we have been chasing ever since we got married. We left Southland and found a smaller church via some friends who also previously attended Southland, but still felt that the community aspect wasn't what we wanted. Fast forward to about 2 years ago, my wife woke up Sunday morning and said "I'm going to go try Eastland, I heard that they have a new pastor."

When she got back from service, she said not only did the pastor spend time talking to her learning who she was and why her husband wasn't with her (we have 2 kids so I stayed back to tend to them), but also explained the vision of the church and what they believe in (something we never experienced within Southland or the other church we attended). I went to my first service with my wife and 2 children and after dropping off the kids in the nursery, which by the way was the most welcoming group of staff members I've ever come across, we quickly sat ourselves in the front row of the sanctuary. Needless to say, new folks in the front row is a big deal - we were promptly met with smiles, hand shakes, and "we're so happy you are here."

What stood out to me most was that all the people that we interacted with were not pushy. I felt as though every comment made to us was genuine and the place just felt warm, like we were genuinely meant to attend church here.

What we like most about Eastland:

1. Honest pastor - he tells it how it is, good or bad, and loves you regardless
2. Super cool staff - good mix of young/middle-aged/older folks regularly contributing either by volunteering or being on staff directly in various aspects.
3. The message is true to the word - no boiled down generic message. Pastor Jared gets straight to the point and does such a good job at making his message relatable every single week. Then he doubles down and brings back previous sermons to really put a bow on what it means to be a Christian in todays world.
4. My kids ENJOY going to church. They are 6 and 3 and it's not difficult to get them out the door in the mornings on Sunday - the Eastland staff do such a great job at making sure all the kids are having fun while also reinforcing core Christian values and beliefs.
5. We felt welcome as soon as we walked in the door; truly “Come as you are” community. We have come in tshirts and shorts, we have come in slacks and dresses, hair done or wet hair right out of the shower, heavy hearts and light hearts; struggling or content; seriously come as you are!
6. Members ask personal questions and follow-up with you at later dates - they don't forget the stories you share/hardships that you are going through.
7. While small, the congregation is starting to widen its age gap and grow (younger families showing up every week!)
8. The music is NOT a rock show - Lorie puts together wonderful arrangements every week that compliment Pastor Jared's sermon for that week.

If you're looking for a smaller, dedicated, Christian family, please consider going to Eastland. Church doesn't feel like a chore to us anymore and we attribute that to the community that they have built over the past few years. We feel lucky to have found Eastland and love the direction and improvements that have been made over the last couple years. I have been coming to Eastland over 11 years now. I got engaged in the gym and have had all my kids dedicated here. What I love most are the people- we care about each other and live life together. My husband runs the Upward program and we love to help the community have a safe place to play basketball and share the love of Jesus. Come check us out at Eastland. I have been attending Eastland Church for the last 10 years, and I am so grateful for each person in this Church family. I have found a community that cares about my teens, prays for them, and supports them in whatever they are going through. I have had the honor of serving Eastland Church in the PreK and seeing my kids now serving as well. It is a joy to have a place where they can go and have fun and ask questions and seek Jesus. I hope you come and visit Eastland and get to know some of the amazing people I have gotten to know over the years. You won't regret visiting Eastland this Sunday! Pastor Jared tells it in the most positive and understanding for everyone. Love our church family. I love this church I have truly felt an amazing community here and made friends that will last a lifetime

name: Eastown Church - San Ramon Campus
reviewSummary: I love my 5th year attending Eastown Church. It's a welcoming, warm and great worship/teaching place to be!!! Thanks to Pastors: Clint Dupin and Mrs. Michaell Garcia Dupin for their dedication to truly show God's heart towards all. A small, but mighty local church that truly lives out their mission of loving local. My husband and I have been attending Eastown for a few months now and have taken next steps in serving and immersing ourselves within this community. If you're looking for a place that will welcome you and support you in your faith journey, come and check out Eastown. I looked at this church when it first opened at the request of former neighbors who knew these “Pastors.”  I’ve followed this organization and I would not put my family in this place or under the care of this pastoral team.  Yes, they appear really nice, friendly and loving to the world; but that is because they are worldly too.  This organization is afraid to teach the Bible in truth of God’s word, fearing it might offend someone.  In doing so, they seek followers and growth instead of God and they do not realize this error.  They sound so just, citing their fight against systemic racism on their website, but fail to realize all worldly problems are overcome by Jesus alone.  Racism is hatred for the color of one’s skin and systems can’t hate, people do.  People who don’t understand we are all brothers and sisters and descendants of Adam.  They teach that Heaven is a real place but so is hell, and that’s why Jesus spoke more about it.  So you have to teach both, because how much would you have to hate a person to not warn them of the consequences of not putting their faith in Jesus alone.  Because it is in faith alone that we are saved.  Jesus came in truth and grace (John 1:14, 17) but churches like this only teach grace because truth offends all.  They miss out on the glory that comes when you accept the truth, that is we are all sinners who have fallen short and we are all in need of the only savior, Christ Jesus.  God’s only son from heaven who alone provides the only way to heaven thru faith in Him alone, because of the work He alone, performed on the cross.  I hope churches like this change and become bold in their faith.  I hope they change and begin to follow the requirements for being a Pastor that the Bible clearly outlines in 1 Timothy and that they come understand Jesus’ warning in Matthew 7:21-23 and in his letters to six of the seven churches of Revelation were warnings to churches and people who claimed Christ. Very warm and inviting. Each person that you shock hand with were engaged in meeting you and welcoming you. The sermon relevant. The band was wonderful. The best and funniest kids church ever!

name: Eastside Christian Church - Anaheim (Platinum Triangle) Campus
reviewSummary: I have not tried taking my ESA Dog people tell me she’s not really a service dog, but she is a service dog because it says right on my ESA paper that I am handicapped and she has to help me with my handicap and that’s not the only handicap I have but anyway the only other place that ever turned her away was one of the doctor offices. I’ve had her into a couple of different hospitals and nursing home and they loved her. I don’t always take her with me everywhere I go one time one doctor’s office told me I could not have her in there because I don’t have a special patch on her little vest. She’s a little pedigree Shih Tzu and she’s very well behaved and if she does. Or something like that, I would just take her out Eastside Regeneration was so healing for me when I went. Sadly, I have not gone back but I plan to. I miss everyone there, and this truly was such a safe place for me when I attended. I even had the opportunity of volunteering at one point. I hope to be back in God's timing and I highly recommend the regeneration program for physical disabilities, mental health, sexual addiction, and addiction. It is truly one of a kind program. Blessings. This church has mine and my kids whole heart. You can feel the Holy Spirit everytime you come in or hear a message online. We have recently moved and I watch online . I have not found a church where you can feel God as loud as you can in this church . Thank you for all you do Eastside Pastor Gene is so funny. I was atheist/lukewarm and this Church led me home to Jesus. I was baptized in 6th grade on my birthday and they showed me so much love and care. They also protect your stuff in the bathrooms when you're getting baptized. I love this Church. This Church saved my life 15 years ago...I love the people who all make it feel like HOME. The Worship music touches my soul and the Sermon... 9 out of 10 times it relates to me and my life..I'm always amazed by the Compassion and Love I see poured in and out of this church and all its locations...Anaheim, Park Rapids, Bellflower, Redlands, Las Vegas, Irvine....One of the best things that happened during pandemic was Online Church was started and we were still able to worship and hear the message..I'm so grateful to be apart of this amazing Church and it's community...

name: Eastside Church - Marietta Campus
reviewSummary:
I am a church neighbor of many decades, not a member. But I feel I must share that this church does not care for its community, nor growth of its congregation. As evidenced by the church’s attempt to build a for-profit, 3 story, 95 apartment, expensive senior housing on their current parking areas, in among 1950s/1960s 1 story established residences.
Its a shame, but over time I have seen this church evolve from caring for their neighbors to a whatever the church wants attitude. First they closed off Lucky Dr (paid for by Cobb taxpayers) to connect their disjointed campus. Then they built a huge rec center (the neighbors did not want) saying it would be for all, church mbrs and non-church mbrs, with direct neighbors having free access. This too has changed to a no access rec center, except a small exercise room up 3 flights of stairs after coming in an exterior door that is often flooded inside/outside. And finally, they have a new, beautiful LOCKED playground any child would love to play on, only allowing access on limited days/times. The past leaders of this church built a wonderful playground with access to everyone, which current leadership did not keep up.
In closing, these a just the few but significant issues I’ve seen that I feel anyone seeking a caring, church family might want to be aware of.
A sincere thank you for your time.
Amy Kent There was a native plants sale in the church parking lot today. They offered a wide variety of healthy plants - natives that can be tough to find at your typical big box retail store. Thank you to The church for allowing this Amazing church always with incredible staff and members Eastside has a phenominal rec center, which is open to the public. Includes a full size basketball court (6 goals) and full weight room. When you first go, they will give you a card with 7 free visits so you can try it out before you commit. If you want to become a member, it's $150 for the year.

Aside from being way cheaper than any chain facility you could go to, there are open gym times each week when groups come and play regularly. The most popular time is weekday mornings around 6 AM. Typically Monday, Wednesday and Friday, there are between 8-12 guys who play for a couple of hours. It's a great opportunity to get a couple games in before work/school.

The facilities here are great and the staff is really enjoyable to talk with each time I come. If you're looking for a spot to get in some good hoops (with good competition) for a great price, you can't beat this spot. I highly recommend. They have a very strong spiritual presence unlike many churches today that Cross is always there for you to see. Too many churches have thrown the cross out with the trash and now we're doing new age make everybody happy. This place is not a ashamed to use the Lord's name and praise and to bring him up at every opportunity. You want to make a Carpenter smile visit Eastside.

name: Eastside Covenant Church - Tucson Campus
reviewSummary: We have been attending ECC for about a year and a half and I have never felt more at home at a church. The congregation is small and welcoming with a wonderful youth group (surprisingly large amount of kids attend ECC). The services are changed up weekly, not just a sermon each week, so that you feel more involved and learn from one another. Even my kids look forward to the service each week! And there's awesome fellowship after the service with great snacks to get to know one another. Extremely welcoming. My first time there I had so many people welcome me and treat me like part of their family. At the end of the service there is always food and drinks for you to enjoy while you mingle. They do their best to make sure there is something for everyone. The facility is always clean, and they recently painted and updated the look. I would definitely recommend this church's it's a fantastic atmosphere. After looking for a church to feel welcome and safe to wrestle with faith and religion this small community of wonderful humans has embraced our family and created a safe space. I drive from all the way across town to attend this surprisingly progressive (for the Eastside), but still very true to the Bible church home. Christ centered worship with a variety of service styles.  Traditional to volunteer discussions and reflection with praise and hymns to ground us. Multigenerational loving caring congregation. After being part of a large church it's nice to be part of a family. ECC is like a family of people sharing a belief in Christ and doing our best to live that belief. And by family we have people as young as two and as old as 90 joining us in worship and while we are small we share Jesus love to our community.

name: Eastwood Christian Church - Louisville Campus
reviewSummary:
Have been going there for many, many years.  They have lot of Older congregation, wonderful ministers, organist etc.
This church really makes me
feel welcome & has the old time religion that I grew up with. I've been a member since 1969.  I loved the church then and I love it now. The pastor bill. Did such am amazing job. At teaching. Left. Me in a good spot Not spent much time here, but beautiful both inside and out.

name: Eastwood Christian Church - Nashville Campus
reviewSummary: This congregation is thriving in a time when many churches are closing. It is filled with kind, caring, and loving people. We strive to be a congregation living by Jesus's example and accepting ALL people. We don't all agree--and don't try to. Theologically diverse. Politically diverse. Who said you can't talk about politics or religion? We can. And do. Thoughtful people, willing to listen to each other and care about each other. Differences accepted. Celebrated! Open and Affirming, which among Disciples of Christ means we welcome all lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgendered and questioning people. We say and mean: All means ALL! And that includes people who don't identify as Christian but want to belong to a caring, accepting community. We are serious about social justice and outreach ministries. Come see. You'll be welcomed! Growing open and affirming congregation with young Korean minister(fabulous preacher), wife and 3 adorable children.  Variety of musical talent in the congregation. This is a wonderful community that lives by the motto “All means all.” The teachings of Jesus as represented in the gospels leads Eastwood Christian Church to be a place where all are welcome. Eastwood truly welcomes AND includes ALL. No exceptions. A loving community with GREAT messages and music every Sunday.

name: Ebenezer Baptist Church - Atlanta Campus
reviewSummary:
There are photo shoots and then there is THE photo shoot that leaves a lasting impression on you.

The Civil Rights Trail Photo Shoot @ebenezer_atl Heritage Sanctuary was just that. Being inside this historic church felt like being surrounded by legacy, faith, courage and the powerful echoes of history all at once. Beautiful welcoming congratulation!
-Brought my friends from Italy to hv the real Atlanta experience with worship and a visit to the Martin Luther King Jr Memorial. An eye opening and inspiring time 🥰👏👏🙏 I visited Ebenezer Baptist Church and the Martin Luther King Jr. Center for Nonviolent Social Change, and it was such a powerful and moving experience. 🙏🏾✨

Being in the church where Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. preached, seeing the memorial, and walking through the exhibits filled my heart with reflection, gratitude, and inspiration. This place is a beautiful reminder of faith, love, courage, and the power of peace.

I left feeling blessed, inspired, and grateful for the opportunity to witness such an important part of history. ❤️ After an amazing day spent at the John Lewis Institute "Good Trouble" Summit (Emory University Goizueta Business School)...

We were dropping by the King Center, in order to pay our respects on the 4th.

Little did we know we would catch the tail end of the service and then get to witness the wreath raising on Ebenezer Baptist Church.

The whole experience was absolutely overwhelming and I'm so glad the timing worked out.

I could not recommend this venue enough.  Everyone is incredibly gracious and the historic nature of the building speaks for itself.  An absolute must-see if you're in the Atlanta area! We did the tour. Love the guys who shared the history. Very informative and he made it interesting amd was respectful. Only downside is I couldn't really hear the speech at the beginning but that was because other people were talking during the tour.

name: Ecclesia Christian Fellowship - San Bernardino Campus
reviewSummary: I have been visiting this church for more than a year. Always with a message from other  visiting or in house ministers who brought a great word. I happened to go a few Sundays ago and the Pastor preach a POWERFUL word so rich and educational for me in tithing. OMG. I literally had to stop taking notes!!! He PREACHED without all of the hoopla. He laid it all out with power and grace. Bible study on Sunday works for me. I went back the following Sunday and it was him bringing fire again.   I went t to a women’s ministry event. It was lovely. The leaders were approachable and the service was on time and flowed. The Pastors wife was the speaker. Excellent word. Very good word driven church who are serious about people. I feel good sowing seeds here. Amen. Great church helps its community with food and events for families and community love the people that workk here there not only helpful but friendly and full of praise Brought somebody here to collect food as I've been doing for nearly two years and overall haven't had any bad experiences until recently, as the same person I normally bring to this church was gathering food I was in dire need of a restroom and came inside to use it. As I was heading to the restroom what appeared to be a staff (female, presumably African-American, taller) greeted me in what appeared to be a polite and respectable manner but was under the assumption that I was there to gather food and directed me to where the food was being distributed. Out of concern that I would be denied access to the restroom I did not wish to state that I was here to help somebody else collect food and asked if I can use the restroom without stating why I was there, she allowed me to use the restroom which was greatly appreciated but upon leaving the restroom and attempting to return to my car to wait on who I brought that same staff directed me to where the food was yet again. To avoid potentially causing a scene I went in the direction she pointed and began to look for the person I brought, that same staff further directed me to where the food was after she saw that I was walking in another direction I guess assuming that I didn't know where I was going and starts to speak to me in a manner that I found unnecessary. As an attempt to return to my car I made it known to another staff person (also female, presumably African-American, wearing prescription glasses) that was signing people in and who spoke to me in a more ridiculous manner that I am looking for somebody and quickly walked away to return to my car. Though I made a similar statement the exact statement that I wished to make was "Excuse me, I am looking for somebody but I do not see her. Thanks." but I was afraid that I would start trouble by saying that, while I recognize that I had the option of staying in my car or fetching a restroom elsewhere both of these staff that I encountered appeared to be incompetent when it comes to speaking to people in a sensible manner (addressing me as "sweetie" and "mama") and assumed that all people who came were looking to gather food. This was not the most pleasant experience and I do not wish to return here at least not in-person, this incident occurred approximately on: Wednesday, January 21, 2026 My husband and I were looking for a new church, we thought it would be nice since I came on Saturday with my aunt and parents to a line dancing class everyone was very friendly. It was not the case Sunday, we had a gentleman come in and tell us about the family room which was nice we have our 7 month old baby but he’s been going to church since he was 6 weeks old the music doesn’t bug him and he generally falls asleep or just sits in our laps. When I was outside a usher approached my husband about moving our stroller mind you we are in a back row against a wall where there are 3 empty rows in front of us basically telling him to move the stroller. We chose the back to not be a bother to anyone and the stroller literally wasn’t in the way it was against the wall. Then when I came in and we were sitting another usher came and told us about the family room I was like I know thank you. I enjoy praise and worship so I wanted to enjoy it with everyone. About 7 minutes later another person comes and tells us about this room we already are highly aware of, I told her I know thank you. We took that as our cue to go. My son wasn’t crying, screaming, or shouting just existing. Apparently, it’s a problem to exist as a baby. Didn’t even listen to the sermon. I sang on my churches praise team right after giving birth and the baby wasn’t a problem as an infant or as a 6 month old. Just doing too much. I have been attending that shirt since it's been on date street. Pastor Joshua Beckley is awesome and a bible teaching Pastor. Come by and check us out. Won't be disappointed. Amen

name: Ecclesia Houston - Downtown Campus - Houston Campus
reviewSummary:
I was involved in this church community for over 10 years, primarily through kids ministry and consistent volunteering. I don’t regret the relationships or time spent there, but I am no longer part of the congregation and am at peace with that decision.

Over time, several concerns accumulated that led to a shift in how I viewed the church. What once felt like a grounded, community-oriented environment gradually began to feel more curated and performance-driven. Earlier leadership under individuals like Kelly B, Steven, and Mike felt more stable and authentic. In recent years, the high turnover and cultural changes have been difficult to overlook.

One area that consistently stood out was the church’s social culture around alcohol. Many volunteer and women’s events centered on bars, breweries, wine tastings, and similar environments. As someone who does not drink, it increasingly felt like an environment where full inclusion was not always considered, particularly for individuals who may be in recovery or simply choose not to participate.

I also had ongoing concerns regarding leadership culture, particularly surrounding Pastor Chris. Over time, I heard multiple concerning accounts from individuals connected to staff. While I cannot verify those claims firsthand, the overall lack of transparency contributed to a sense of unease.

In addition, the church has taken a deliberately non-committal public stance on LGBTQ-related issues. While it presents itself as broadly welcoming, responses on doctrine and practice tend to be carefully worded and ambiguous. From my perspective, this has created a lack of clarity that feels intentional.

There were also financial decisions that raised questions for me, including the ownership of a beach property that is described as being used for retreats, while regular tithing remains a core expectation of members.

Ultimately, the point at which I decided to step away came when the church announced a 21/22-year-old as a pastor. I do not question her personally, but from a professional standpoint, I believe pastoral leadership carries expectations of maturity, experience, and demonstrated judgment over time. That decision reinforced my broader concerns about leadership direction.

I am not leaving from a place of anger. I am grateful for the people I met and the years I spent there. However, the church has changed significantly from what it once was, and for me, stepping away was the right long-term decision. Great experience. Welcoming environment. Understated worship (which is a good sign in an age of performanceism). Pastor felt genuine and real. All it took was one curious visit and I instantly signed up to become a Ecclesian. Little by little they're are helping to change our community for the better. This church is very nonjudmental and relaxing. Everyone is accepted here! Very kid friendly also! Haven't had the opportunity as of yet to see your facility i will Wednesday the 15th Good coffee, great fellowship, and powerful message, every time.  This church understands and lives the Christian mission.   I have volunteered there for their regular bbq meals for the unhoused and their weekly shower ministry.  I hope to be able to do more.

name: Echo Life Church - Pensacola Campus
reviewSummary:
Came here looking for a bold, Bible-based church with real conviction, left disappointed. They had a woman come up claiming to be one of the pastors/leaders which is clearly not biblical. Then they promoted a “merch drop” during service like it’s a streetwear brand. If you’re serious about Scripture and want a church that isn’t trying to be trendy, this probably isn’t it. Echo Life Church has been such a blessing for me and my family. We first visited in May, just a week after Easter, and it immediately felt different in the best way. After being away from church for over 10 years, it’s refreshing to be somewhere that doesn’t pressure you but lets you reconnect with God at your own pace.

The pastors’ messages are always heartfelt and easy to relate to. The kids’ program is amazing, the staff are kind, and the coffee shop is such a great touch. Echo Life has helped me grow closer to God in a way that feels real and personal. I’m so grateful for this church and the community we’ve found here. Wow! This was our first time at Echo Life Church! It just happened to be their 7th Year Celebration! We really enjoyed seeing their grassroots slide presentation and how they have become who they are today! Amazing testimony to faithfulness and determination 🙌 👏 🙏 ❤️ ✨️
Pastor Joe had a great sermon and Pastor Suzannah, his wife, was one of the energetic Music  Praise Team members!
They have 2 services- 9 a.m. & 10:45 a.m. We are going to participate in their Steps program next week after the last service to learn more about the church and how to serve!

Update! Now it's July and I can't say enough wonderful things about Echo Life Church! They have expanded to 3 services, since I started attending 5 months ago! There is 8 a.m., 9:45, and 11:30! We go to the 9:45 and it's packed out! I serve as a Greeter at 8 a.m. and that service is quite full too! But, don't be discouraged by that! There's room for everyone!!! Pastors Joe and Suzanna are doing an absolutely wonderful job! 👏 The service starts with wonderful live music that changes members, so everyone who wants to serve can! I love the energy and words to the lyrics on 3 screens! Who doesn't want to not praise the Lord with great worship 🙌 music? Believe me! If you and your family and friends, are searching for a happier life with Jesus, Echo Life Church is an absolutely awesome place to start! They have a great place for your kids at Echo Life Children's Church too! Enjoy a nice cup of coffee before and after the service too! Bring it into the service too! Our city is ready for a revival, like the message from Pastor Joe Driver today, who incorporated film clips from the "Jesus Revolution" and "The Chosen" today! We'll have 2 more Movie Summer Sundays- July 14 & 21, 2024! We even have bagged popcorn 🍿 and sodas, so y'all join us! You won't be disappointed!!! Come on Pensacola!!!! This church will put the fresh wind in your sails! The team of people here go above and beyond the church norm. My wife and I attended over a dozen other churches in Pensacola before finding Echo Life. While life took us back to the Midwest a couple of years later, we still watch online every Sunday. I simply can't recommend enough for you to try this church out!
All the best, -Alex This church is led by an absolute amazing group of pastors who genuinely care about everybody has an individual no matter how much or how big the church will grow. They will continually work to get to know you. This The first time in this church I was invited by a friend and upon walking in I was welcomed with nothing but hospitality and warmth. It definitely made me feel like I was already a part of the community. Echo Life Church is definitely an impact I will never forget I will always be grateful for In my life as it has allowed me to build my faith on levels I did not know existed!

Give this church a visit!!

name: Eden Prairie Assembly of God
reviewSummary:
I left this church for many reasons. I will return if a new pastor comes in but it seems the new pastor wants to vote to make the pastor not replaceable like they used to do voting every 3 years. Wonderful pastor and family, new in the last 3 years, great annointed expository preaching. Highly recommend this church. Come as you are you are welcomed and this church is growing. See you soon! I've been looking for a new church home for a while and tried EPAG recently. I was warmly welcomed. I love the size of the church: not too big, not too small. The music was beautiful and so was the sermon! I was getting excited that this may be "it," but then I was dismayed when a gentleman wrapped up the service by saying something along the lines of that men should love their wives (fine) and in turn, women should respect their husbands (... are you for real?). That was a complete turn off for me. It's 2020. Women and men should love and respect each other as EQUALS and the impression I got was the whole "old world" way of thinking (women should "serve" their husbands). Since I decided to visit on a whim, I didn't take a close look at their philosophy and realized that it caters to a more conservative crowd. I doubt LGBT+ are welcome here though I could be wrong... I suggest you review their beliefs listed on their website to see if you agree with them before going as they seem to take a very literal approach to the Bible ("lake of fire" type of speak...). If that's how you roll, then go for it but if you're more progressive/inclusive I'd look elsewhere. They served a lovely breakfast and took the time to get to know me. The members were very kind and friendly. I have been going here for awhile. The worship is good and the preaching is sound and challenges you. They have good children's ministry and youth group. They have some small groups but could use more. There is a little something for everyone to learn, grow, and share in community. Very few churches that I have visited would get such a rave review. THe service starts out with two or three upbeat songs "warm-up" as the pastor put it. Then the sermon that was engaging, real, and was funny. Then they ask you to stay for at least two songs afterward. The musicians and singers were so anointed, I am a grown man and had tears I was so moved by His presence in the worship. DISCLOSURE: I only visited there once. But I do definitley plan on going again.

name: Edgefield Church - Nashville Campus
reviewSummary:
I’ve been a lay-member of this church since 2011. Its leadership cares about its members and cares much about the gospel. I remain a member because the fruit of love and grace is evident in this church.

It’s a great congregation, a lovely building, and solid teaching. The music tends to be traditional hymns, psalms, etc. Nothing showy. The church leadership eschews the Christian nationalism currently endemic to evangelicals.

Edgefield Church was a result of a merger between historic Edgefield Baptist Church and Trinity Church (where I was a member) in 2020.

You would be welcome at Edgefield. Come visit sometime. We left membership of this church because we felt that, under the current policies, our children and others within the church were unsafe due to the policy regarding offenders against children.

I believe that extending cheap grace to these offenders who are either currently on the registry, those who have been removed, or those who have not yet been prosecuted, harms children and abuse survivors.  Bonhoeffer rightly said, “Leniency to the dishonest is cruelty to those they injure.”

I would like to see the elders of this church extend careful grace instead of cheap grace, exercising wisdom and discernment. An offender should never have been allowed to use the same bathroom facilities as children. I don’t think it’s appropriate to praise an offender without qualification or encourage parents to get to know offenders against children. Evidence of dishonesty on the behalf of offenders should result in immediate permanent exclusion from the church. The risk of legal liability should never prevent a church from investigating whether historical abuse happened.

The elder in charge of children’s ministries said to me that “offenders are in a vulnerable position”. This is backward: children and sexual abuse survivors are vulnerable to offenders. A repentant offender would act similarly to the good thief on the cross who said, “we are suffering justly”, rather than appearing to be victimized by the consequences of their actions.

There are many faithful Christians attending this church. For their sake, we hope that the elders will write and follow robust policies, expediently, with the aim of protecting children and abuse survivors.  I would invite the elders to post their policies on their website, as many churches do, and leave a link as a reply here, so readers of this review can rest assured that the issue has been adequately addressed. It is never too late to do the right thing and allow the good teaching this church has to prosper. I started in this church when I was first born I’m now 75 I have fond memories of going to church with my grandparents my great grandparents and my parents my great grandfather if the veins was on the board of deacons told his stroke in 1960 but he listen to the service for the next 20 years every Sunday history of this church I hope you continue for another 100 years A beautiful building to have Christmas Eve in Stunning 1800s church a much see

name: Edgewater Church of Clear Lake - League City Campus
reviewSummary: Looking for a church that takes a deep dive into what it means to explore your faith and truly understand the grace given to you? This ministry takes an approach from the roots up, delivering a message rooted in biblical and historical context that gives one a more profound understanding of scripture. Pastor Thad has an annointing over his teaching that is palpable. The worship service beforehand will absolutely bring you to tears. God has blessed this church and I have never experienced anything like it before. I expect this ministry to grow and grow. What a place! The band is awesome! Thad is inspiring when he speaks! I like it here! They need a much bigger church! I know they like being a small church, but God let's you know when you must reach out further. You just have to expand when you have something special. If they stay themselves they have to have a bigger church! No arrogance! How great that is! You would think they would be arrogant with how fantastic the entire service is, but these people are real and very original! I like it here! The first time in decades that I have gone to church 3 times in a row. That says a lot for me! Amazing and anointed service. Praise and Worship is amazing. The Pastor delivers a life changing message regularly I love my church. If you are looking for a deeper understanding of the Spirit and a greater relationship with the Lord, this is the place for you. This is a Spirit-filled church and I love it. We have Wednesday night Bible study, 3 Sunday morning services, a prayer night once a month and we take communion. Can't say enough good things about the church, Pastor, and staff. Beautiful & just the right size, amazing teaching, and warm & welcoming. Definitely a place to learn AND understand about all things biblical. It feels like I get to learn a secret every week!

name: Edification Fellowship Worship - Chandler Campus
reviewSummary:
I don’t really subscribe to a particular “religion”; I am spiritual but not very particular to a certain group.. I never want to go in anywhere by myself for the first time anyway. I am right where I need to be today, & for today, that was enough.

name: Edify Church - Citrus Heights Campus

Just the right mix of music/message etc. Its my Church Home and wonderful members down to earth. The name means Butterfly in Spanish. Food Ministry, Good people A friendly  church welcoming  been my church ⛪  home for  me, my mom and aunt since 2018

name: Edmond Church of Christ - Edmond Campus
reviewSummary:
I wrote the review below 2 months ago.  Today, I must praise the Edmond Church of Christ as they reconsidered their decision and agreed to have my friends husband honored at the church after all.  It was a lovely service with military honor guards and a relatively large audience.  My friend was extremely delighted that the church reversed their original decision and this is helping her get through her grief in loosing her beloved Monty.

Thank you Kevin Raynor for your open heart and courage to make this right.

—————

My friend’s husband was a regular member, a tither, a veteran and volunteer for years at Edmond Church of Christ until he got ill and went into a nursing home.  Sadly, he passed this week and the family wanted to have his memorial service at this church.  When my friend asked pastor Kevin Raynor to arrange the service, he denied her request citing “it’s been awhile since he was attending and no one would remember him, so no, we won’t be able to accommodate your request“.

Wait….  what!  How disappointing is that!  Both my friend and her husband were veterans and served this church for years. So I guess his wife will have to hold his memorial service for her family and friends in her living room.

We have found the Church of Christ to be extremely righteous and hypocritical.  I guess they want your time and money while you’re living, but once you get old, they ignore veterans and dedicated members when you‘re gone.  This is just another example.

Save your soul and stay away from this church! Wonderful family of Christians to worship the true words of God with.  Will attend again as we travel thru this area. I love this congregation so much. Everyone there is so kind and welcoming, especially the youth group. I've been attending this church since 2015 and have been involved in a lot. They have so many mission trips and service opportunities. I have seen God work through this congregation. Thank you teacher Phil Sanders for the word of the  bible and the singing so beautiful and praise Jesus for all of you for your faithfulness each week. Sunday July 30,2023 truly  miss Phyllis b. I've attended Edmond Church of Christ since 1997. I've found it to be a warm, loving, friendly group of people, with dedicated leadership. It's been a blessing to me and my entire family.

name: Edmond Faith Bible Church - Edmond Campus
reviewSummary:
Love this church so much. Amazing sermons and amazing people. All of the sermons leave me feeling convicted which is what every church should be doing.
Get here early for parking! I’ve been going to FBC since kindergarten no, since I was a  daycare kid, and now I’m a sophomore and every single person I’ve talked to are genuinely the kindest people I’ve met, I just want to give a public thank you to all of our teachers and pastors for being welcoming and kind to everyone. I have no idea what the day to day body life of this church looks like. Whether it’s a place of healing and grace or legalism and rules, I know nothing of. I can only leave my first impressions.

Obviously it’s a church of means with a beautiful building. But there was more.

The music……. how lovely to hear modern worship music so well done AND with theologically sound words.  The musician and worshipper in me was blessed.  I’m always thrilled to see drums and praise teams that aren’t on the cutting edge of 1992. And I appreciate a safe space to raise my hands in worship if the Holy Spirit so leads.

The teaching….. a very sweet blend of well prepared exposition of the text along with excellent sound doctrine and theology.  And with the beautiful encouragement of a very personal and thriving relationship with Jesus woven in.  I appreciated Pastor Jay teaching that a relationship with God is not just intellectual, but experiential. It was more than just stuffy intellectualism and knowledge. There was exhortation and inspiration to genuinely know Jesus because He is worth knowing.

So thank you for a great visit to a traveler who was looking to worship while away from home.  I’ll see you all in heaven someday! Just started going to Edmond faith Bible church. Situated on the East side of Coltrane it is a large church that started small and has been built on to. The pastor really digs into the scripture and delivers an amazing service. If you have a teenage daughter wanting to join the youth group program, I strongly suggest going somewhere else. The youth leaders will mainly pay attention to the kids who have grown up in Faith Bible and the kids in the groups won’t expand their groups or reach out to new people/ people who are alone. The leaders and kids in the youth program will ignore you until you tell them you’re struggling to find a reason to live. This has happened to multiple people in this program. The worship leader had a conversation with the high school and middle school girls about “being modest” but they told us that we couldn’t wear skirts/ shorts and we couldn’t wear tank top, so instead of tell the boys to keep it in their pants they told the girls what to wear in 90 degree weather in summer in Oklahoma. A church it isn’t a a building! It’s the people! This church doesn’t show that they care for new followers of Christ or new people of the church.

name: EHills Church - Aurora Campus
reviewSummary:
The strongest traits of this church: sermons. They are providing top-notch sermons that you don’t get to hear often in other churches. It’s very relatable, life-application focused, with a bit of head-tripping involved, which I enjoy a lot. A liberating experience, especially if you are a Christian.

I could see why some people feel this church is focused on growth and some may feel conflicted about that, but I found many people naturally want to come after getting to know this church.

Their sermon and worship are very professional. For some, it’s “too professional,” but what’s wrong with that? I found that’s something this church can offer. And it’s delivered by a pastor from South Africa who experienced the hood, not someone who has always been sitting on the high seat. It’s awesome.

Their worship style is very contemporary, which I also prefer compared to conservative worship. Very relaxed and not snobby. You don’t need to dress up when you walk in here. And yes, their childcare is another top-notch. There’re many educators among SE Aurora residents and many of them volunteers here.

I don’t know the personality of the congregation yet, but I highly recommend visiting here, especially if you are seeking a church in the neighborhood. Hey there!

I just had to share how absolutely wonderful E Hill Church is. Seriously, I'm overflowing with appreciation for that place! Their drive up food bank is so helpful to a lot of people.The folks who volunteer there? They're truly something special – incredibly kind, super helpful, and genuinely lovely people. Every single time I've interacted with them, they've gone above and beyond.

Honestly, if anyone asks me about a great church community, E Hill Church is the first place I recommend. It’s such a welcoming and supportive environment, and I genuinely believe anyone would feel at home there.

It's actually hard to put into words just how grateful I am for everything they do. On a personal note, they've been incredibly supportive and made such a positive difference for some of my family members too, who absolutely adore being a part of it all. It really speaks volumes about the amazing spirit they have. I absolutely love this church and the church family. The sermons are so relatable to my every day life. The paster is also incredible. May God continue to bless you and your family and the whole church body. We found our new home. Thank you to Alissa for welcoming us and being so great to us!

Alpha group is fantastic and so happy to have Brandon as our leader, meeting great people that care, and having a relationship with Christ A church leader stated that gay people do not align with their core beliefs.
