Fellowship Christian Church - Santa Clarita Campus
reviewSummary: [object Object]

name: Fellowship Church
reviewSummary: Led by Ed Young, known for highly creative and visual sermon series. The vibe is modern and can be flashy. Attracts a wide demographic looking for engaging, relevant communication.

name: Fellowship Church - Antioch Campus
reviewSummary:
I am so thankful for the kindness and generosity of the church. The church culture, people, and services are great.
This is a place where I was able to find God and get closer to Him. The pastors and people are great. I've been blessed to start friendships here. Join a FREEDOM Small Group, you will be a different person. This church was, at one point, a meaningful and transformative experience for me. Ultimately, the church chose to part ways with me; while I acknowledge their right to do so, the decision felt unilateral, and in reflection, what once seemed like minor concerns became much more significant.

I experienced inconsistencies in communication—being told one thing by security or leadership, only for a different outcome to follow, along with delayed or unfulfilled follow-ups. There was also a noticeable guardedness around who could be approached and how conversations were handled, which made the environment feel less open than expected.

At times, certain interpersonal boundaries, particularly across genders, felt more restrictive than empowering. I also observed the presence of strong political or geopolitical perspectives within the messaging that may not resonate with everyone.

While the services are highly produced and engaging, they can at times feel more performative than reflective. There is also a strong emphasis on involvement—groups, serving, participation—which, while presented as optional, can carry a degree of social pressure.

I also had interactions that felt, at times, intimidating. Overall, the environment felt welcoming on the surface, but carried an underlying tension that made me cautious about stepping outside of expectations.
My experience included both meaningful moments and notable concerns. I share this so others can approach with awareness, trust their instincts, and maintain their own boundaries. I live in Alabama and have followed what God is doing through this church and its pastors for years. Was finally close enough to the area to visit today! I loved hearing vision and values clearly stated just as I expected!

If you are in the Bay Area and looking for a church, you’ve found it! Best church in the bay awesome engaging pastors .The sweetest and welcoming people.You really feel at home I love 🤍my church.I highly recommend you come to visit. The stupid speed bumps broke my bike now me and my family don’t have a fast way to move around my city anymore. They pack the Walmart parking Sunday’s. Playing loud music and make it impossible to get through the parking lot safely. It disgusts me me every time I see the building that they promote violence and negativity on the community.

name: Fellowship Church - Dallas Campus
reviewSummary:
The 4/26 Sunday service was deeply disturbing. Instead of offering anything resembling spiritual guidance, the sermon leaned into blatant anti-Islam, anti-LGBTQ, and anti-Palestinian rhetoric. It was shocking to see a pastor use the pulpit to demean entire groups of people, and even more troubling to hear parts of the audience applaud it.

A place that claims to represent faith should not be promoting division, hostility, and ignorance. This was not thoughtful discourse or theological reflection; it was outright disparagement (and insane). I would strongly warn anyone seeking a respectful, inclusive environment to look elsewhere. I’ve attended Fellowship in Dallas a few times before and always appreciated the worship and warm welcome, but today’s experience was disappointing.

I brought a new friend hoping for a great service, but the sermon focused almost entirely on money and financial goals. It felt unbalanced and very off-putting. We left about 25 minutes in, while the pastor was still focused on the topic.

Today’s service felt like a financial pitch and not a message from God. I’m concerned about how a first-time visitor might perceive faith from this message. A church always in Downtown Dallas is always very hectic to find a parking spot or too much traffic I love the word of God I just don't like the fact of where it's located They really make you feel wanted, comfortable and worthy. I love the service EVERY TIME. I’ve been attending Fellowship and even served at the Grapevine campus. Currently, I attend services at the Dallas campus. My experience at Grapevine was challenging it led me to take a break because I didn’t want to accept that a church environment could feel like that. At the time, I made excuses for the people, but ultimately, the people are the church.

Since then, I’ve moved and began attending the Dallas campus. Unfortunately, I’ve experienced the same kind of disheartening interactions there. One moment that stands out happened on Mother’s Day. I shared part of my story with a young lady, I won’t mention her name, but she wore blue and had dark hair. I won’t go into detail, but I’ll say this: I’d rather have someone see or hear me suffering and do something, than witness it and remain silent.

To me, if I’m going to be a sheep in a flock, I want to be under a shepherd who weeps with his people, prays for them, reads and lives the Word, and is willing to fight the enemy on their behalf. I don’t want to be led by someone who watches people struggle and does nothing; someone more concerned with preaching a sermon than caring for the hearts of the people they serve.

From these experiences, I’ve realized where my disconnect lies with both campuses. I’ve given Fellowship chance after chance, but it’s time for me to move on.

name: Fellowship Church - Fort Worth Campus - Fort Worth Campus
reviewSummary:
Best Church around come check it out we have Bible Study for women and men. Leadership events and an amazing kids program. Great church and great people out there. I attended a couple of Sundays and a Wednesday night and I was hoping to go back more because our first day was a surprise. The way they welcomed new people and engaging was amazing.
There was a lunch, get together and just getting to know each other moment.

The only downside was that my son refused going back. I suspect he didn’t have a positive experience at the kids ministry but regardless it’s a church that actually makes you feel a good place to worship.

Not a lot of churches have that level of commitment to welcoming and networking with fellow members. I went for the Christmas Eve service and it was great! They were all friendly and smiling and saying hi as we walked in the door and then they pointed me to the “VIP table” where they gave me and my friend a gift bag and got to know us a little bit. Then they directed us to some other people who showed us our seat. It made me feel better that they showed us where to sit so we didn’t have to wonder around looking for a spot. And I never felt lost because there was always someone there to help! The worship is very lively which I like a lot!! Then this week one of the ladies called me to see how I felt about the experience and invited me to a women’s group she leads. They did well! This campus does not see or value mid-life singles. As a woman in my 40s, I am not able to join their Bible study groups. They offer two groups, 1 for singles up to 35 years old and 1 for married people. I asked them about this. They said I was welcome to join a small group that was just women. It wasn’t the same as a Bible study group, and why am I not given the opportunity to study the Bible with both men and women to get different perspectives? Simply because I’m single and in my 40s? It seems yes, because if you are single and under 35 it's okay to be in a co-ed study group. The information desk told me maybe they weren’t a good fit for me if that’s what I was looking for because in their experience, coed Singles Group create “trouble” (but I guess only after a certain age since they did have an under 35 co-ed group! SMH) Ultimately, I did not feel welcome, seen or remotely cared about. We went here for adventure and my son loved it. The message was easy to follow for him in bible study. The only thing I personally did not like a long with many other parents. It was recorded from Grapevine location live so the Big Show was on TV not in person. They church is big enough to be able to perform live, in my opinion.

name: Fellowship Church - Frisco Campus - Frisco Campus
reviewSummary:
I live in New Jersey and love visiting my daughter. I recently attended the Easter service on Saturday and enjoyed the egg hunt with my grandsons and I had such a  beautiful experience. The music and service brought tears to my eyes. I was very moved and look forward to watching services online.  I am thrilled my grandchildren are attending the classes and my grandson who is 4 told me Jesus lives in his heart. I would like to thank all the teachers who have taught my grandson. Alice Garrett Sacca As one of the few churches open during the pandemic, this Modern Christian Church experience makes anyone feel safe and right at home! They are welcoming from the second you pull into the lot all the way to your seat. The special kids programs with their first-rate production with age appropriate material, had my kids excited to return! Creative messages, top notch music, friendly volunteers and opportunities to get involved make this a perfect place for us to call our new church home! It’s been a while since I last attended Fellowship Church in Grapevine, especially after moving out to another location close to my college that I was attending at the time. Now that I’ve relocated to Frisco, my parents and I decided to visit the Frisco campus—and I’m so glad we did. The same spirit of warmth, powerful worship, and Christ-centered teaching that I remember was present here too. It truly felt like coming home. Grateful to reconnect with the Fellowship family in this new season of life! The best. All real Christians will love their time here.

Great messages from Pastors Ed, Lisa & Sam I am, as well as the others.
And the worship music is sensational & emotional. We were greeted warmly from the parking lot to the sanctuary.  There was Special parking for newcomers with our own personal escort into the church where we were welcomed again with an information packet and welcome bag with pastor, Ed Young's book (awesome), free coffee from the specialty coffee shop, and don't get me started on the AMAZING worship music!  So, grateful we came.  Thank you Nate, for inspiring my husband to get Baptized!

name: Fellowship Church - Rome Campus
reviewSummary: Fellowship Church is a warm and welcoming church in Rome, Georgia with a heart for families, young adults, single adults, college students, students, and kids. The worship is meaningful, the Bible teaching is clear, and the church does a great job helping people connect through children’s ministry, student ministry, college ministry, Connect Groups, and discipleship. It feels like a place where people are noticed, welcomed, and encouraged to grow in their faith. If you are searching for a family friendly church in Rome, GA, or a church with strong kids ministry, student ministry, young adult community, and gospel centered teaching, Fellowship is a great place to visit. Awesome congregation!!! Very welcoming to all people. I have not attended Church services at Fellowship, but I am active in their Prayer Shawl ministry. This group of fine women crochet shawls, and blankets for cancer patients, homeless people, or people in need. We also make hats and blankets for neonatal units, and for preemies who don't make it. Great group of women doing service for God. Friendly and welcoming, and I love the music! Our new pastor is really great and we have enjoyed welcoming them to our family! If you are looking for a church home, give Fellowship a try! They allow my daughter's school to hold their Christmas musical here every year. They are wonderful people.

name: Fellowship City Church - Chagrin Campus - Chagrin Falls / Bainbridge Campus

Been a member here since 2005. Have always felt welcomed when you walk in the door.  Love the fellowship and teachings.  The praise and worship is fantastic and you can really feel the Holy Spirit moving. Definitely worth checking out if you are in the neighborhood. Wonderful non-denominational church!
I have been going here since I was born, quite literally.

reviewSummary: I loved 🥰 to be in City Church ⛪️ last Sunday… Because I was able to see the love ❤️ of God through my brothers and sisters. I bless this beautiful Ministry!!! name: Fellowship Community Church - Aurora Campus
reviewSummary:
Fellowship Community Church is a warm and welcoming place with a strong sense of community. The atmosphere is friendly, the people are kind, and the services are meaningful and uplifting. I truly appreciate the welcoming environment and the genuine care shown to everyone who attends. Highly recommended! Great multi-generational church.  Friendly congregation. The staff, deacons, and volunteers are working very hard to make everyone feel welcome. My family and I (2 adults, 2 kids) have been attending for a few months and we all love it! The Christmas service was the best we ever attended. Highly recommended for seasoned Christians as well as new (or inquiring) believers. I'm now on my fourth visit and you most definitely feel God in this place.  Lovely people, great music and excellent pastors who definitely give current messages from the Bible.  I love it here.  They also are doing great community outreach work and have a lot of get together for women and separate men's opportunities.
I haven't been comfortable in a church for many, many years, but I finally found a home church where God is always present. Worship team is bringing it!  Consistently each Sunday the song selection is spot on and the talent brings it home.
Gospel based sermons are thoughtful and informative.  Christ is explained as well as glorified.   Bible based sermons are always my favorite I have been a member of Fellowship Community Church for a long while now.  My husband passed away in Jauuary, and we are having his service at the church. Pastor Rick is a great person and loves the Lord. He is a great person you can talk to about the Lord.
I'm so glad he is the pastor of this church. Thank you for all that you do for the Lord.
Eva

name: Fellowship Congregational Church UCC - Tulsa Campus
reviewSummary:
Good AA meeting here, most days at noon and other times, check your Meeting Guide app for details. All are welcome. A progressive church with many outreach programs and a very friendly congregation. It takes the phrase "open and affirming" as a way to live out their mission. All are truly welcome and not required to change to fit a set of rules. Refreshing. An 'open and affirming' congregation of the United Church of Christ. Congregation and its leaders are strong proponents of full inclusion for LGBTQ persons. Progressive message from clergy, taking the Bible seriously, but not literally. "No matter who you are,  or where you are on life's journey, you're welcome here."

Disclaimer - I am an authorized minister in the same denomination, although I do not serve this congregation. I   I am a member of the church. This is the best church I’ve ever attended. There is no condemnation, no judgment, and no one isn’t welcome. They have an emphasis on social justice and you do what you can when you can. The Church is so welcoming and the people are so kind. I don't attend but I do pass by twice a week and I just wanted to commend whoever is making the marquee messages.

name: Fellowship Covenant Church - Arvada Campus
reviewSummary:
Been coming to this church for 3 months now and it is so very very amazing. I Love How everyone is so Welcoming and friendly. The pastor is Amazing with his sermons he Explains everything so Everyone can understand. I am Going to Continue coming to this Church and I want to get more Involved. Terrific church. I visit regularly for the Bible Breakfast brotherhood meeting twice a month. I would consider regular attendance for church services, but it's a long haul from where we live in Saudi Aurora!
If you are near Arvada, give it a look What a wonderful church to visit! People were so warm and inviting we felt very comfortable just being visitor for the day. Sermon was wonderful and biblical. We really enjoyed our visit here! The first time we entered this church, we felt we were home. Pastor Brad and his congregation are truly connected to the Lord.  His sermons and prayers come from the heart and are Biblical.  We were welcomed with open arms when we entered the church and continue to feel the love and kindness of Pastor Brad and his congregation.  Barb and Charlie Hanes Great community. Biblical and friendly. Amazing place of worship. Also the leadership and staff are very caring, come out and visit us! I'll be there as long as I can 😁

name: Fellowship Dallas
reviewSummary: Noted for its 'Teaching Team' approach and 'Expository' style. Reviews highlight a 'warm' and 'Grace-centered' atmosphere. It feels like a 'Bible Church' but with a strong emphasis on community diversity.

name: Fellowship Dallas - Dallas Campus
reviewSummary: Excellent service.  So many times the instrumentation is so loud you can't really understand the praise team singers or the other folks in the pews. This service was the exception to that kind of experience.  Really liked the way communion was offered and done. The sermon was relevant and only 45 minutes long.  My only wish is for an alter call. Great worship and sermon that was biblically based and easy to apply in our lives! This is so important these days. Very welcoming and the lobby and worship center were beautiful, so nice. I've heard good things about their small groups too! We'll be back! This is such a wonderful, warm, and welcoming church. As a Dallas newbie, i wanted to find a place of worship that i can call home and I've found it! The pastor provides such amazing and inspirational service, the worship team is phenomenal, and i just love how all the staff is just so helpful and kind. Shout out to Kelly who helps get you connected and find just what you need at Fellowship. Loving the services! The church goes are not dress' in business more lack back atmosphere blue jeans and any shirt. Some women wear a dress not all. Most of people were friendly greeted  me every where though out the church I felt welcome to the family. Country band on the background had Christmas trees and chimney on the wall burning a fire of course not real fire. Colorful burning. Outside had police patroling the parking lot safety measures etc. Welcome as are seen one ole boy with flip flops had a nice looking hot girlfriend. Im not to judge just observed what I saw. This is a bible church in the middle of Dallas. The church is in a modern building and the service is contemporary with a band, lead singers and back-up singers. The pastor delivering the message is outgoing, and I have found the messages and bible references relevant. If you don't bring a bible, no worries as they have the verses on the monitors. People here are very friendly but not "in your face" friendly. I didn't feel intimidated by members mobbing me before or after the service about becoming a member. They provide free coffee before and after the service, on the second floor, and you can take it into the sanctuary during the service. Or bring your own from home or Starbucks! People are generally dressed in "church casual," and everyone seems comfortable here. You come into the building on the first floor, but the entrance to the sanctuary is on the second floor. They have elevators and escalators for those that need extra mobility assistance. They have a large parking lot and a parking garage available. Their location immediately off Central Expressway makes it easy to access from most parts of Dallas. They only have one service on Sunday. It starts at 10a and goes until 11:15-11:30 depending on if there is a baptism or communion that day. If you are looking for bible church, I highly recommend!

name: Fellowship In Christ Church - Carmel Campus
Fellowship Nashville - Nashville Campus
reviewSummary:
Finding Fellowship Nashville was truly a blessing for my wife and me after our move to Nashville. After hopping from church to church, we stumbled upon a gem that has become our spiritual home. What sets Fellowship Nashville apart is its unwavering commitment to community. From the moment we stepped through the doors, we were welcomed with open arms into a warm and supportive family of believers.

The pastors at Fellowship Nashville are exceptional in their ability to preach the gospel with clarity and passion. Every sermon is firmly rooted in biblical truth, guiding us deeper into our faith journey and inspiring us to live out our beliefs in our daily lives. It's evident that this is a Bible-centered church where the gospel is at the heart of everything they do.

But what truly sets Fellowship Nashville apart is the sense of belonging and fellowship. Whether it's through small groups, sports leagues, men’s night, women’s night, community outreach programs, or simply sharing a meal together. It's a place where relationships are nurtured, burdens are shared, and joys are celebrated.

In Fellowship Nashville, we've found not just a church, but a family—a supportive community where we can grow in our faith and journey alongside others who share our love for Christ. If you're seeking a church home where you can experience authentic community and be nourished by the Word of God, look no further than Fellowship Nashville. Fellowship Nashville is about being gospel centered, caring for each other and the world around us.  Theologically sound, verse by verse teaching.  A community of believers who seek the Lord and do life together.  For the city, in the city, seeking a city above.  I love this church! Fellowship Nashville has been a huge blessing to our lives. The leaders and the members are living out Gospel-centered lives, and together make up a Gospel-centered community where God works powerfully. When we first arrived, they immediately invited us to a small group, and we met some of our closest friends in that group and have been participating in that group ever since! The pastors care for the individual, and teach the Word with personal humility as well as confidence in the power and truth of Scripture. We are so grateful for our experience at Fellowship Nashville! Fellowship Nashville has been such a blessing in my life! The pastoral team loves the Lord and seeks to know him, and make him known to the Fellowship Nashville community and beyond. I leave church every Sunday with a greater understanding of the Bible and feeling encouraged to live for Christ in every way. They don’t shy away from uncomfortable scripture, but prayerfully invite the Lord to speak truth through his word. Fellowship Nashville has been such a breath of fresh air for church community. From the moment my husband and two kids walked in, we have felt like we’ve known the people there our entire lives. It is an atmosphere of love, kindness, and acceptance. The expository teaching guarantees being deep in God’s Word each week and the people there truly exemplify the hands and feet of Jesus in the most genuine way. I am so incredibly grateful to have found Fellowship Nashville.

name: Fellowship Of Believers Church - Sarasota Campus
reviewSummary:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Fellowship of Believers Church is a truly welcoming and Christ-centered church. The teaching is biblical, heartfelt, and practical, making it easy to apply God’s Word to everyday life. The worship is uplifting, and the sense of community is genuine—you feel like family from the moment you walk in. The pastors and members clearly love the Lord and care deeply for people. If you’re looking for a church that teaches truth, loves well, and lives out the Gospel, Fellowship of Believers Church is a wonderful place to call home. ✝️ Fellowship of Believers Church is truly a place where the presence of God is felt the moment you walk through the doors. The worship is powerful, the preaching is filled with truth and the Holy Spirit, and the atmosphere is full of genuine love, faith, and unity. This is not just another church service — it’s a place where lives are transformed, hearts are healed, and people are drawn closer to Jesus. You can tell this ministry is led with sincerity, passion, and a deep desire to glorify God. I’m incredibly thankful for this church family and highly recommend it to anyone hungry for a real encounter with God. Vibrant church with great music, a desire to honor God, and LOTS of of young families. Rather than a strict 1-hour service, they relax in God's Presence and give opportunity for anyone in the congregation to say what they're hearing/experiencing. Very unique and refreshing. The sermon was very good, delivered in a very non-preachy way. My wife, son and I are very thankful to have found Fellowship of Believers. I personally have encountered more of His Holy Spirit and am seeing transformation, becoming closer with my Lord Christ Jesus since attending. Everyone that we have met has been genuine, lovely people. They have a great children's ministry. They have been around for many years and have NO DEBT (praise God)! The pastors are being led by the Holy Spirit and there is a unique framework of accountability whereas the leadership is comprised of three God-fearing married couples leading the direction of the church. I appreciate this compared to other churches, whereas one person may have too much power and influence, they are all being held accountable according to His Word and Holy Spirit. Fellowship of Believers freely worships but is also very rooted in scripture, which I also value, while also practicing the gifts of the spirit without being off-putting, that uplift others. I also very much love that church service may be different every Sunday, being several hours long or shorter, it depends on what His leadings are. There is also just one service, so you have the opportunity to meet everyone when you attend. Church should be this way and not a formula. Full stop. Perhaps most importantly, there are many multigenerational families that attend here, which is a great blessing to be around to see such true wealth (thriving families) especially coming from a broken family and choosing to break generational bondage and seeking to emulate this within my own growing family. We are so thankful to be a part of Fellowship of Believers and hope God can use us to make a difference for His kingdom here. The morning service is usually from 10 a.m., but people come in advance, chat, talk, get acquainted, drink coffee, you have a very friendly, hospitable atmosphere. I really like the unofficial, free, homely atmosphere in this place and good, friendly and kind people of different ages. There is a continuity of generations and there is no spirit of legalism in the ministry, you can pray and go ahead, even to children who praise Jesus during the glorification. If someone has a need, a minister, spiritual guardians and worshippers approach them, they are offered to pray together without coercion, and the Holy Spirit always acts in different ways, not according to the template. There is a very good children's service. I would also like to have a translation into Spanish, Russian or Ukrainian.
Thank God for you!

name: Fellowship of Champions - Spring Campus
reviewSummary:
Excellent church, friendly people, pastor is great with expository preaching and teaching, great youth ministry and special events to connect and support the local community! Home groups meet every other week for more personalized time for Bible study and prayer and personal attention to your needs (and great lunches!) Good for the whole family to worship and get support from each other.  Excellent music ministry for each service.  Come and visit and worship with us! My wife and I just joined FOC after attending for several months. The community is very warm and welcoming, and the preaching is expositional (so hard to find these days). On our first Sunday, the Senior Pastor spent time talking to us, several people introduced themselves to us and invited us to sit with them (both young and old), and we were invited to visit a small group after the service. My family and I have been attending this church for 5 months and I know this is the church for us. They have a wonderful staff often reaching out to visitors and members so they may feel welcomed. This doesn't feel like a super church, but instead a more personal church. The pastor preaches from the bible and doesn't sway from the truth, even though the subject matter can be difficult due to the times and generations. He greets everyone before church and makes himself readily available after the service. Their child care is outstanding, and I feel very comfortable having my son stay with them during the service. God led me to this small church in Spring, in October 2013. MY very first day here, was like a big warm hug. I was greeted at the door, hugged a few times, welcomed to sit with members as they talked with me. Everyone was so friendly - and genuine! Genuinely caring and sincere. I've never seen anything like it in any church I have been to.

I joined a home group of theirs my first Sunday. I love this church so much, that - now that my husband and I are looking for a bigger place to call home - staying within close distance to this church is an absolute factor and must. I never want to leave. I pray they add more services in the long run and more ways to be fed. We email each other, get a weekly newsletter, mission opportunities, prayer team, fantastic worship team and live music, a truly wise and gifted pastor that makes the Word just come alive every time I hear him preach, a wonderful children's program and Mothers Day Out and - coming soon - Vacation Bible School! It's free but spots are limited so register now to get your kids a spot!

Everyone here is my second family. I absolutely adore each one of them - but am shy so I don't talk to many hahaha. I am working on that. And hey you get free donuts and coffee before service! Yay! Y'all really should come. It will do wonders for your walk with the Lord, and bless you and your family in more ways than you could ever imagine. We also fell in love with the small, tight-knit community and clear passion for God’s Truth. This place quickly and easily felt like home for us.

name: Fellowship of the Rockies - Colorado Springs Campus
reviewSummary:
We rented a home by this church for 10 months and were told they would not renew because the property was church-owned and they wanted to turn it into another ministry. We accepted that, despite it putting our family of five in a very difficult position in an already tough housing market.

I think this is well worth your time to visit Firepoint.

name: First Baptist Church - Dallas Campus
reviewSummary:
Very friendly people attend this church. I love pastor jeffress you're so kind and knowledgeable. Plenty of things to do there to learn about the Lord and get ready for the day that he comes for us 💕🙏🙏❤️💕 this is the first mega church that I’ve visited in Dallas. The service is amazing, and the campus is clean and nice. The people here are just amazing too. I love the college & career group, they’re so nice!!! I would love to come back when I’m here in Dallas. God is good! Had the opportunity to visit with my family on Easter Sunday.  It was a short walk from the hotel on a beautiful Resurrection day.
The main entrance is stunning.  Fountains choreographed to praise and worship music filled my eyes and ears.  We took pictures, of course, in front of the fountains and made our way in to the service.  If you are a first time visitor you will have no problem getting around.  There are volunteers posted throughout to give you precise direction. Such a sweet spirit is in this place.  We had came expecting, and from the opening of the Orchestra to the invitation we knew that the Holy Spirit was in this place.
We took time after the service to walk around, through the old auditorium, and around the church.  Thank you all for making our Easter Sunday a special one to remember. This morning I visited First Baptist Downtown, solo dad with four children, ages 13 months through 12 years. We were traveling, and I intentionally brought my kids so my older ones, who are very musically inclined, could experience the orchestra and corporate worship in person. We sat exactly where we were directed, in the back right section designated for parents with children- near the exit in case we needed to step out.

My 1-year-old was making soft baby cooing noises. Not crying. Not screaming. Not disrupting anyone. Just the normal sounds of a one-year-old existing. To be clear, if a child is screaming, crying, or truly disrupting the service that's different. I would not keep a genuinely disruptive child in the sanctuary, because I respect the worship experience of others. But soft baby coos are not disruption. They are life. And a church that cannot make room for life risks losing it.

Mid-message, we were approached by Mark with security, who informed us that we would not be allowed to remain in the sanctuary because of the baby’s cooing. We were escorted out and directed to a small room with a television feed. No orchestra. No corporate worship. No shared atmosphere. Just a screen.

If I wanted my children to watch church on TV, we would have stayed in our hotel room.

Mark was not rude, but he was not warm either. And the decision itself speaks louder than demeanor. Jesus said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.” (Matthew 19:14). It is worth asking honestly: would the first-century church, whose members walked with Christ Himself, have escorted a father and his children out of worship for baby coos?

Families who bring young children into the sanctuary are investing in spiritual formation. Those small sounds are not distractions. They are signs of life, proof that the next generation is present.

After leaving mid-service, we went to Clyde Warren Park. My children were welcomed there. No one treated their presence as an inconvenience. We enjoyed fellowship, and reflected together in a place that felt more open to families than the "sanctuary" we had just left.

If this is official policy, church leadership should seriously reconsider it. Policies that elevate silence above presence will not protect a church’s future, they will empty it.

The Church is meant to be the fellowship of believers, gathered together, worshiping together, and sharing the gospel across generations. It is supposed to be a place where families are formed in faith, not filtered out.

If this is not official policy, then those representing your church need to better reflect the heart of Christ.

We will not be returning. When a public park is more welcoming to children than the gathered Church, something has gone deeply wrong. A huge church with several buildings and many ministries. This church does so much for people in Dallas and around the world. It is neat to see how the new architecture goes around and preserves the original building of the church. It has church services on Sunday at 9:15 and 10:50 am and disciplemaking groups at 5:30 pm as well as throughout the week.

reviewSummary: “Biblical teaching to guide you to spiritual maturity” couldnt be more true. Love this church and the congregation After 4 years of searching, I have finally found a church where the people are real, welcoming, and warm. If you are looking for a church that preaches out of the Bible and the people are warm and friendly. This is the place for you. The Pastor is ABSOLUTELY RUDE.  I had a TERRIBLE experience at this church. They need to do better introducing people to Christ. The secretary was even rude. It doesn’t make any sense. Their approach to representing Christ is Terrible from my perspective. Your first introduction shouldn’t be are you a Christian and what does your church teach you. Unbelievable My kids and I are on a weekend trip and decided to find a church Sunday morning. I looked online for a church that preached expositorily and this church came up. We decided to visit and when we walked in the door it just sounded heavenly. The church was packed but the kind greeter found us a seat near the front middle since my kids like to be able to see. The worship songs were so Christ focused. It was amazing being able to hear the congregation singing all the words was just wonderful! The message was well given and also very Christ focused. Then I got to noticing that there had not been an announcement about children's church and even though my children always stay with me most other children at most other churches go to children's church but at this church all the children stayed with their families which was just beautiful. They were quiet and listened which is what should be happening in churches. Children fall away from the church because they literally never sit in a sermon, but this church is different in that area. Furthermore, I noticed that most of the women and girls were wearing dresses and skirts that were decent and not sensual. This was such a beautiful breath of fresh air. Thank you for what you're doing, you're obviously doing a great job with it.  I hate that we live three and a half hours away! May God get all the glory from your efforts! I have my undergrad in Religious Studies and my MDiv in Global Studies, so I have heard quite a few sermons by different individuals.  Without a doubt I love listening to Dr. Davis preach the Word of God!  I have been listening to his series he did on Mark and every morning I listen to the sermon and I find myself meditating on the sermon and Scripture all day.  I wish I lived close enough to go to this Church.

name: First Baptist Church - Huntersville - Huntersville Campus
reviewSummary:
I have referred a young lady  to come to Lydia’s Prom Closet to search for a dress for her senior prom. I stopped by to check it out for myself. I received a warm welcome when I entered the room. There were so many dresses, shoes, purses, and accessories. Everything was hung and presented so beautifully! It was a wonderful experience from the moment I arrived until I walked out the door. After reading the negative review posted by a former employee I felt compelled to tell my story regarding FBCH. My wife and I started attending this church in 2019 shortly after moving to Huntersville. This was right before the pandemic so initially it was a struggle to get to know folks but we pressed on and have found this to be a warm and inviting atmosphere. It is a very community centered organization providing services like Lydia's Loft, Prom Closet and summer Saturday breakfasts. There are multiple opportunities for bible study and to find an area where your talents can be used to serve others. I was previously a long time member of Myers Park Baptist Church in Charlotte, arguably one of the most liberal churches around when it comes to social justice. I can assure anyone that I would not join a church that I felt had racist tendency. All I can say is come find out for yourself. Think twice before going to this church because if you are from a different race other than Caucasian you will not be treated the same by a lot of people (read between the lines).

I am doing my own review because I gave a thumbs up for another review that described exactly what I’m talking about and for some reason you cannot see that review anymore.

So please be aware of this when you are choosing a church. And remember racism can be anywhere in this world, it doesn’t matter if it’s pastors, or in the pews or in public life… it can be anywhere. Our daughter has gone here for 2 years now and the teachers are phenomenal!!! Donna has ran the school for over 25 years now and has the biggest heart. I trust my child’s safety so much everyday when I drop her off and will be bringing my other daughter here when she’s old enough! Love this school! The congregation is warm and loving. The support I received after my brother's murder helped  carry me thru a horrible experience.

name: First Baptist Church - Montgomery Campus
reviewSummary:
If you want a good Southern church Vibe without being in church all day long this is the church for you not only is the people friendly and make you feel welcome they are loving and supportive and make you feel the spirit of the Lord in the house definitely stop by and visit this church Extremely friendly and welcoming. A lot of historical valu here. A must see for visitors from Canada. Very nice Sunday service. Thank you Mr Davis for sharing your story. At perhaps the lowest point in my life I sought refuge and sanctuary here so I could pray and reflect. It was 7m on May 29 and the church was closed, yet when I called a woman answered and invited me in around back. She introduced me to Pastor Morris who read well my hearts cares and concerns and sat with me and talked of the heart's resolve and God presence guiding us through life’s trials. I was there for a couple hours and in our last conversation he asked “Well blake let me ask you again since you can’t backtrack (because life won’t allow you to go back the way you came), where you headed?” I thought he was talking about geography and it wasn’t until July that he’d been talking about the direction of my life and the condition of my soul.

I’ve prayed several times a day since then and have taught biblical passages as English Literature lessons. Where am I headed? Back to Montgomery and Pastor Morris  to  surrender my life and soul to Christ this Sunday July 21, 2019 It was closed but still worth a visit. Beautiful old church in downtown Montgomery that my family attended for generations. Friendly and welcoming, it brought back so many memories.

reviewSummary:

name: First Baptist Church of Alabaster - Alabaster Campus
reviewSummary:
This church has become a family to me. They have served our family in hard times and celebrated our joys with us. They have discipled my children and teenagers in the faith and given them lifelong relationships to encourage them as they walk it out. They all look forward to church activities. The church is solidly founded on the gospel and rooted in the Word. It has been wonderful to see the Spirit move here. Unfortunately my wife and I had several bad experiences at this church while looking for a new home church. We attended 4 services in March and April of 2021. Probably the worst experience was our fist time there. We had a 16 month old at the time, and he tended to be a distraction during preaching. After the singing I took him into the lobby when he got restless. While I entertained him quietly, the older usher indicated to me that I should take my son all the way outside. It was raining that day. Not a little rainy, a full on down poor. He wanted me to take my 16 month old son out into the rain. I firmly declined and we stayed in the lobby. Unfortunately our experiences after didn't improve much.
My limited assessment of this church is that it's an older congregation not open to new young couples. While they apparently had children's classes no one seemed interested in giving us information. We tried to make it clear that we were new and the information received was nothing. We have since been happily attending at Westwood Baptist. Visiting First Baptist Church of Alabaster from a long time membership in a Mega Church, I loved it! I found it to be a comfortable welcoming environment with a small town feel. The praise band / music was beautiful, the sanctuary was just the right size. The Pastor is not only very knowledgeable with scripture but delivered a message of truth that we could all follow along with in our bibles. He has a great sense of humor and able to keep everyone's attention. I like the fact that he makes himself available at the door on the way out to shake your hand and talk / pray, what ever you need. I would recommend this church. Great church for singles and families. Brother Steve always has great sermons(preaches from the Bible). Daniel always has great music specials lined up from the choir which sings with One Voice. Amber is wonderful with kids and youth programs and she rocks all the many fun things she sets up to do with them. Kids choirs, youth band and worship. Summer camps, VBS, and special programs during the summer. I'm jealous of all the stuff the senior adults get to do! Great food closet ministry. This church is home. Still greeted like the first time we came with hugs and love! Loved the pastor very sweet and always a great message

name: First Baptist Church of Austin - Austin Campus
reviewSummary:
First, I want to say that my experience at FBC Austin was good. It didn't have quite everything I was looking for but there are still good qualities. While I will remain anonymous and I will be honest in my review, I'll also keep it constructive and respectful. I do NOT intend to be hateful or mean spirited at all. I attended for a few months in 2025. Everyone there including the staff, was  friendly and always welcoming. I am a gay man so that is important in a church. Follow up with visitors is pretty solid; I had several different people follow up the first week I visited after I completed a visitors card. I appreciate the fact the church overall is welcoming to the LGTBQIA+ community. The pastor, Griff, is terrific, friendly and very approachable, and his sermons are the highlight of worship (no one paid me to say that, it's true), and the associate pastor, Carrie Houston, is one of the most genuine, caring people - she's a true asset to the staff. A few constructive items: 1) Diversity. Diversity in its staff - there are no people of color on its staff. A church like this could benefit from different perspectives. On the plus side, FBC still heavily ministers to white, straight families. On the downside, FBC still heavily ministers to white, straight families. For a downtown, urban church, it's still overwhelmingly caucasian & straight. The number of people of color in a given service could be counted on one hand. 2) LGTBQIA+. I will say this, I appreciate the fact there are people from my community on staff & involved in the church. However, at the time I attended, there were NO small group or any offerings at all for the LGTBQIA+ community. Honestly, that's not great for an urban church like this. They sent me to a lent small group and all the people in it were wonderful - but also all white & straight. I'm also hesitant to say this, while I also appreciate the fact the music minister is gay - I could sense his focus is music (nothing wrong w/that) - his role outside of music seems awkward. There was a "yes, I'm gay but I only lead the music here" type of vibe (no one's fault-just an observation). This brings me to my next point. 3) The worship music. I grew up Southern Baptist. I've seen churches divided over music. I'm not the most musical person and have rarely, if ever, complained about the music in any of the churches I've been a part of, I've just gone with the flow - but I have to say the music wasn't for me. The musical style at FBC could best described as very, ultra traditional - all hymns, dirges, readings, chants etc. There's nothing inherently wrong with that, and the music minister is considerably gifted (and he does a great job at leading worship), but for a downtown, urban church that strives to reach a diverse crowd, its approach seems a little odd and unappealing. Again, I've never complained about the music at all and honestly I feel a little bad about saying it. I don't have a specific solution - perhaps a more streamlined, contemporary musical approach could help. Overall, there's a great group of people at FBC and it is ministering to people, so I commend them for that and wish them nothing but the best. It wasn't quite for me, but it might be for someone else (especially if you have a family and want them in a welcoming environment). God Bless the folks at FBC Austin, I pray nothing but great things for you. Churches have strengths and weaknesses, just as people do. But having been a part of nine Christian churches during a long lifetime of job-related moves, I’ve never attended one I loved more than this one, after 15 years here. What makes it unique is that the staff and the congregation strive for authenticity (not lip-service) in expressing their faith—and aren’t afraid of confronting doubts, because searching for deeper insights about how to live out Jesus’ teaching is the goal. It’s truly the kindest and most Christ-centered church I’ve ever known. And anyone looking for a choir or handbell group to join couldn’t do better. I also love that the children’s ministry is vibrant and helps knit the whole community together! This "Church" has unique Architecture which is worth experiencing, however that is the only reason to make the stop if you are passing through and I would recommend steering clear if you are looking for a Christ centered Church as I felt the need to get up and leave multiple times during the service. First Austin is a group of vibrant, caring, open people seeking to follow Jesus and care for each other and their surrounding community. The choirs are great, too! UPDATE: I stand by my review, despite the response. Though some may view my review as an attack, I wrote this review to let others about my experiences at FBC. Had the leadership practiced what they wrote below when we attended, we probably would still be there. Unfortunately, despite being members for a long time, we did not feel welcome anymore, so we left. (I would point out that, if you are having trouble attracting people, you need to look at the culture, teachers and leadership of the church and you will find your answer). As most people know, just like jobs, people leave bad managers.

When we found our new church home, I had to unlearn lessons I had been taught while at this place. For example, you do not have to be baptized to go to heaven. Baptism is a public proclamation of faith.

Our current church has instilled in us that you stand by what the Bible teaches, even when it doesn't conform to the whims of society. All Jesus followers must view the culture through the lens of the Bible, and not the other way round.

I saw the recent news article, which reminded me of this "church". I grew up going to "church" here. I use quotes because it became apparent they were not Bible based. This is a political club, masquerading as a church. There is a reason they hemmorage members and are unable to attract new people. We go elsewhere now, and are much happier being in a church that teaches Biblical principles and lessons.

Side note: I remember when they were thinking of building that parking garage. It was a waste of money then and my opinion still stands. Look elsewhere for a church that will teach you about God. This is not the place.

name: First Baptist Church of Denver - Denver Campus
reviewSummary: I rent parking from them and I have had multiple issues with them that have yet to be addressed. Constantly, they are blocking off rows of spaces in their rental lot for churchgoers, leaving the rest of us who live or work in the area (who pay for parking!) frustrated. Services are both morning and night so I do have this problem often. One church employee on Easter told me there was nothing he could do about parking and initially laughed in my face when I asked for help. Incredibly hurtful as I approached him with friendliness. I have complained and they never dignified my voicemail with a call back. There was also an issue with their invoicing one month that led to me getting a $40 parking ticket. They did resolve this, but it is something to note. Very disappointing and be wary of getting a parking permit from here. Went June 20th, 2026 to see a Polish guitarist, the room was 90°F. Very uncomfortable, and unpleasantly hot room. Many people left before performance was over because of the heat. AVOID We weren't able to stay for service due to our flight, but met some absolutely amazing membera who gave us a tour of their beautiful sanctuary. Would absolutely recommend coming for a service, hearing the organ and worship music, or popping into their library or small group sessions!! My organization has been a tenant and partner with the church for over 8 years and has the greatest respect for the church and its pastor, Brian Henderson. The church was one of the first hosts of the Safe Outdoor Spaces in Denver for homeless women and this is such a great indication of how dedicated it is to filling its mission. The church has become a wonderful home for several excellent nonprofits and we so appreciate this space and culture of caring for community. Nothing biblical going on here, but if you want a God of your own imagination, want to be justified in doing what is right in your own eyes, and want your ears tickles then this place is for you. Sola scriptural rightly divided is the only way.

name: First Baptist Church Of Duluth - Duluth Campus
reviewSummary:
I would like to say that our family was very well received in this church. It is the most multicultural church I have ever seen. The ESL coordinated by MS. Cindy help us to improve our English. Pr. Mark is a vocation of God and his words have always brought me comfort and exhortation. The church is based on faith in Christ Jesus, baptism and the Lord's Supper. A traditional church adapted to the modern world. The children have a great safe and Christian environment, guided by Ms. Young. The weekday Preschool is amazing!! I would definitely recommend this church! 🙏🏼❤️ Multi cultural worship center, with exceptional preaching and bible study, translation facilities in Korean and Spanish
All ages are well catered for both during bible study and main service Although I really appreciate this church that reaches out to people who are in need, the ESL director was RUDE to me.

I went to ESL classes on Wednesdays, because I wanted to make immigrant friends like myself. She aggressively asked me “WHY are you here? How old are you? What age did you move here? Are you born here? the second generation?”

She might have thought that I don’t need an ESL class, based on my English level. But like many other immigrants, I struggle with my English as well.

I didn’t feel welcomed, n felt interrogated by her. I didn’t come here after a few times I tried. First impressions of FBC Duluth: they are multicultural, multigenerational, and welcoming to first time guests. The worship service was bright and engaging. There are many families here and a ministry area to pour into each age group. 5/5! The way everyone is welcoming in this church is amazing.  We went to VBS and sports camp for the first time this year.  I have been looking for a home church that specializes in missions locally and abroad. I am so glad I found this bible based church.

name: First Baptist Church of Gahanna - Gahanna Campus
reviewSummary:
Have you ever prayed to find a church, and a calling was to a church you have been many times before? So you finally give in and attend, then find that the Lord is there and doing mighty works on a small scale. This is the church for everyone. No fancy show here. Only expository sermons from the scriptures and nothing but love from everyone. Leadership is very sound and although human doing an amazing job. They understand the people are the church. "We are the Church" not the buildings walls that surround us. My wife and I found ourselves at this church after others just didn't seem to hit the spot. The best part about FBC Gahanna is the ability of pastor Wally to speak and stay engaging during the sermon. On any given Sunday, the message was theologically solid, biblical, and much more meaningful than you'll find at your average modern protestant church. The church body here is a very genuine and welcoming group of people, and I highly recommend giving this church a chance if you're looking for a place to be each Sunday.

Many churches today give a feeling of community without offering quality discipling, and pastor Wally offers very good counseling and biblical perspective while trying to further the knowledge of those he's been called to pastor. His purpose is truly to shepherd, and he takes that role very seriously. Just visited for a Wednesday night Bible study. I really enjoyed it. I wish y'all well. I pray God gives you workers for the harvest. One man plant,one man water, but God gives the increase. Thank you for being so welcoming to a stranger. God bless you all. I prayed about finding a home church when I moved to the area. I felt led to FBC of Gahanna. I began attending the first Sunday in April (2019) and have attended ever since.   It is the most friendly, family feel and welcoming, Bible based church I've ever attended.  This is truly "my home".  It's come as you are.  Whether you're in a dress, suit, blue jeans or shorts, all are Welcomed.

They have great Sunday school classes for all ages;  weekly activities for children and various groups for adults (some that meet weekly, others on a once per month basis).

Come join in.... you'll love it here! We have been attending FBC for a few months now and have found the people to be warm and welcoming and the teaching to be biblically sound and relevant.  Since coming to Ohio 3 years ago we have struggled to find a place we can call our church home.  I am confident that not only will FBC be our new church home but also our new church family.  :-)

name: First Baptist Church of Garden Grove - Garden Grove Campus
reviewSummary:
Wonderful Church! Pastor Wade is amazing in proclaiming the true Gospel every time he teaches. Great Sermons and simply great congregation. We just joined this church not too long ago and both my fiance and me are really blessed to be part of this church Very friendly Church!! Lovely stained glass windows along one whole side of church with life of Jesus. Only negative - guitar music only as have no organ or piano player presently. I had been attending another nearby church with great Vietnamese pastor and great pipe organ but people not friendly. Fabulous Hispanic ministry.  👏 Beautiful church architecture; no doubt from Garden Grove's distant rural past. Be respectful of churchgoers on Sunday if you are there to photograph the church and surrounding structures. This Church welcome us and our Mission in Pakistan. Pastor Wade preaches  the word of God faithfully.
Generous and are a super nice congregation.  We are grateful.

name: First Baptist Church of Glendale - Glendale Campus
reviewSummary: I’ve had nothing but positive experiences with this church. I feel very welcomed by the staff and congregation, and they treat every newcomer as part of the family. I often come and sing with the church choir, and the choral and instrumental music is always varied and engaging. The church itself is expansive and beautiful, with a spacious sanctuary and side chapel, as well as areas for events. If you’re looking for a new church to call home, you’ve found it. Joined this church in 2018 and attended for an entire year, giving of my time, energies, and excessive money in service. In the very beginning I experienced snide remarks by other members, and even refusal to shake my hand from another member, condescending treatment by the secretary, rudeness and shunning by the family members of the choir director, who never participated in any other planned activities or events except choir, and the ABSOLUTE WORST - a clique environment created by the "first lady" where, if one was accepted into the clique, apparently good for them, but if not accepted, all shunning, scorn and wrath was rendered onto the one who was not accepted in..I am one of the latter category. There was an obvious personality problem as this woman made blatant statements to a room full  in her short-lived ladies class such as "I don't care if any of you like me...I have the Lord and Bella...that's all I need" (Didn't even include her husband, the pastor) And " If any of you think by being married to the pastor, it has 'rubbed off' on me, you're wrong."  ZERO reason from anyone in the room to deserve that kind of intimidation, but it happened in all sorts of scenarios on a regular basis. I experienced bizarre things like her grabbing a plate out of my hands at a luncheon, impatiently shouting at me "WHAT IS IT YOU WANT???" when I was making a decision of foods I wanted from the luncheon table, and numerous other outbursts and childish behavior. She even made condescending comments about my accessories such as handbags as if it were indignant jealousy. I finally ceased attending services, and as a retaliation toward me after I explained to the pastor in a heartfelt email why I was no longer in attendance, he conducted a bait-and-switch campaign to get me to submit an application for one of the duplex rentals   the church oversees, (I had sold my house several months prior and began inquiring with interest to lease one of the properties). It became full circle when I was denied the apartment, and now I am convinced it was the pastor's wife that demanded the duplex not be rented to me from the very first time I expressed interest. (Believe me, there were a number of clues along the way; I simply tried to give the benefit of the doubt, and tried to dismiss them) I further believe that anyone unfortunate enough to believe the charade that goes on consistently at this beautiful old building is in for a complete and utter shock...that is, unless.  one happens to become accepted into the clique that is thriving, alive and well within the walls. The recent post of the person indicating there're a lot of "SHADY PEOPLE THAT WORK HERE" and "THEY ARE THE "EXACT OPPOSITE" of who they portray themselves to be...is hauntingly correct and right on. I don't know who this reviewer is, but I trust every word conveyed, because I am personal witness to it, as well. As Jesus warned...there will be FALSE PROPHETS, and my eyes are opened to that prolific reality. this is a lovely church with a beautiful sanctuary, kind and knowledgeable staff, and a particularly wonderful music program! I'm not remotely Christian, but I still felt welcomed by the friendly congregation and enjoyed the services I attended. The concert with the APU Men's Chorale and Bel Canto Women's Choir was awesome. Worship and the message that morning was a amazing, too. This is church is a gem waiting to be rediscovered by it's city. It's a nice place listing an concert.

name: First Baptist Church Of Indianapolis - Indianapolis Campus
reviewSummary: First Baptist brings traditional teachings of the church into the modern day, focusing on hope and love in these dark times. A congregation welcoming for all cultures, LGBTQIA+, and all ages. It's a lovely place. Beautiful church on northwest corner of 86th Street at College Avenue. Welcoming congregation. Traditional Sunday worship service, with nice mix of new and classic songs and hymns. Instructional Sunday School classes, as well as other activities throughout the week. First Karen Baptist Church congregation also meets here on Sunday afternoons, and often contributes music to the morning service. Me and my family got woken up to a red head caucasian guy with glasses about 5”6 and kicked us out of their parking lot because we were connected to their electricity from the building for heat for our kids to stay warm we’re homeless living in our vehicle. The guy took one look at my husband and seen that he is black and started disrespecting him as we thought that they were a Christian church. They tried to take our extension cord as my husband went to go tell him and he threatened us by telling us if he seen us again that he was going to call the police and have him locked up for no reason. He is also the same person that seen us a few days before and called the police and the police seen us and our children in the vehicle doing nothing but staying warm and minding our business. I have diabetes, my husband has Crohn’s disease and I have 3 disabled children and it’s sad how people profile before they know who you are or going threw. I am full blood Puerto Rican, my husband is black and Puerto Rican which makes our children mixed as well. We been trying to get ahold of Evan the preacher at the church to get help and to see if they had resources but I guess churches are not the same like how they use to be. I just wanted to share how things are these days while we are trying to get up on our feet trying to find resources and help. Just wish we were not profiled and judged but god does not judge his children here on earth but sad how now a days people are quick to judge you before they know you. Does anyone remember what it says in the Bible to come as you are and you will not be judged.!! Just saying!! Stay away from politics,  this is a Church of God. I don't want to go to God's Church and hear the arguments of political parties. This is the first time in my life I got up and walked out in the middle of a service. First Baptist has wonderful sports leagues.   The coaches are great using positive reinforcement.

name: First Baptist Church of Jacksonville - Jacksonville (Downtown) Campus
reviewSummary:
I have friends who live in the area, and this is the church I visit when I am in town. I love this church, and I always look forward to going! Every week, we are led in truth-filled, God-honoring worship and get to experience musical excellence at the same time. I'm also involved with the Student Worship ministry, and it's such a great opportunity for students to learn more about worship and have fun with music. If you're looking for a church home in the Jacksonville area, come visit First Baptist! A time was had celebrated end of the school year luncheon served by JSO STAFF food was delicious & the recognition was beautiful (crossingguards) lifestyle 5 to 30 yrs wow what and amazing achievement

They had sleigh-rides, live orchestra, and even snow in Jacksonville!

name: First Baptist Church of Las Cruces - Miranda Campus
First Baptist Church of Lithia Springs - Lithia Springs Campus
reviewSummary:
FBCLS is truly a place to belong. The presence of the Lord is evident, from the moment you come in, to the moment you leave. Pastor Jeremy’s messages are biblically rooted and Christ centered. The congregation is very warm and welcoming. The church has various ministries that seek to bring glory to God and help you grow in your walk with Christ. They also have ESL classes, a beautiful prayer room and a great gym for various sports and activities. My nephew absolutely loves Children’s Church. My parents weren’t regular in-person church attendees, but now they are raising their grandson, and his excitement for God and his love for learning about Jesus inspired them to start attending church regularly.

That, in turn, motivated me to visit. At my nephew’s insistence and persistence, I came—and I’m so grateful I did.

Today, I am blessed to attend church every Sunday with my parents, my nephew, and my spouse.

It just goes to show that Children’s Ministry matters. Whether you have children in your home or not, a child can be the reason an entire family walks through the church doors.

In our case, one little boy’s love for Jesus brought four adults to church every week.

A child’s love for Jesus is contagious. Never underestimate the impact God can make through the faith of a child. ❤️

:

name: First Baptist Church of Mandeville - Mandeville Campus
reviewSummary:
Been a member for 30 years, and I love my church family. So many memories of significant life events for our family and other families. This church and its members have helped me grow close to God and navigate life’s struggles. I can’t imagine how we would have made it without our church family. We’re not perfect, but God is working on that 😍 This church has been a tremendous blessing to my family. From the moment we walked through the doors, we felt genuinely welcomed and accepted. I appreciate the diversity of the congregation, which reflects the unity of the body of Christ. Most importantly, the teaching is biblically sound, Christ-centered, and grounded in God’s Word. First Baptist Church of Mandeville has truly become a place that feels like home. The church offers incredible youth programs that genuinely invest in students and help them grow in their faith while building meaningful friendships.
One of the things I love most is the wide variety of Life Groups available for people in every stage and walk of life. No matter your age or background, there’s a welcoming community where you can connect, grow, and belong.
The church also does an amazing job hosting fun churchwide events throughout the year that bring everyone together in fellowship. Beyond that, there are so many opportunities to serve and get involved, making it easy to build relationships and make a difference.
If you’re looking for a church that is welcoming, Christ-centered, community-focused, and passionate about discipleship, I highly recommend First Baptist Church of Mandeville! This church has an amazing hometown, family feel. Such a genuine, loving church family & sound biblical teaching. Amazing children & youth programs that are fun while actually teaching kids the word of God in depth. Great place to worship & call your church home! Church family is the best. Lots of relocation families for making new friends in a new area.  Jesus loving, Bible preaching, awesome worship time, and great small groups for all ages. Offers a wonderful weekday preschool too!

name: First Baptist Church of Monterey - Monterey Campus
reviewSummary: Immensely loving congregation. Very welcoming to newcomers, especially service members. Clear and thoughtful biblical exposition from the pulpit each Sunday. What we wanted was a church that was community friendly meaning they would greet and talk to us and get to know each you know life outside of church, a church that utilized expository preaching meaning to break down the scripture in its correct or accurate context, and a church that is filled with the Holy Spirit, meaning I’m not just hopping up and down filled with emotion 😭but instead filled with conviction, peace, hope, love.  Every time we leave I find that I’m not just filled with this artificial fire or strange fire but the conviction of the Holy Spirit and recognizing my deep dependency of Him!!! This church has filled our prerequisites for a faithful church to the Lord. It makes it more personal that it’s small as well!! I love this church and we have made this our church home!! We especially love that even though the military asks many FBCM congregants to move frequently, Pastors Josh, Eugene, and the elders encourage those in service to become members anyway. The men's, women's, and young adult ministries are so fun and a wonderful way to gather and connect throughout the week. Excited for summer VBS this July! Our church community has shown my little family much love and service in the past year and we are so grateful for God's presence in this church. The  Church is truly a wonderful place! My husband and I, being new to California and the Monterey area, have been warmly embraced by this community. We absolutely adore the expository preaching and are deeply touched by the humility and kindness of everyone here. It’s been a joy to meet such welcoming and loving people. This church is based firmly on God's word. Wonderful place to worship!

name: First Baptist Church of Pasadena - Pasadena Campus
reviewSummary:
I went there on Easter with my son and his fiance. We started with a brunch, an assortment of scrumptious food brought in by parishioners. We were accompanied by a mariachi band. What a wonderful idea. Celebrating the resurrection of Christ with the happiest music on earth. The pastors were all available and mingled with us before the service. What a wonderful church, people and pastoral staff! FBC is truly special and unique. I came here on my search for churches to be married at. My mom said my great grandma was a member of the church and she remembered it being really beautiful, so I was curious and thought it would be a sentimental touch to my wedding. Mom was right. The church was a bit more contemporary on the outside than I was looking for (I like the old gothic look), but looks can be deceiving!! The inside was just gorgeous!! There is a large gated patio with a water fountain that leads you to the side entrance. The main entrance is breathtaking. There are 2 parallel runways lined with a red carpet leading up to the altar. The windows are all beautiful stained glass windows letting in colorful light. There are giant iron chandeliers and a massive organ and cross at the altar. Needless to say, THIS was it! I met with Marcie and then Cindie the wedding coordinator. Let me say, these 2 ladies are simply angels. They both were so incredibly patient, kind, understanding and helpful every step of the way. I went multiple times prior to the wedding and we emailed and texted often. Again, they are truly angels and I felt so blessed to have them for this process. Words cannot express my gratitude. My wedding was not typical, and I was happy to know that the church was accepting of my non-traditional dress color, my very tattooed bridesmaid and our use of a reverend who was our dear friend marrying us. Our wedding was very challenging, not because of the church, but because of Covid, my hair stylist gone rogue and a venue that was in constant crisis. I felt like everything was going wrong, and many times when I would be upset, the only comfort I had was the church, Cindie and Marcie. I would like to also mention Paul who is INCREDIBLY talented!! He is their musician and can play everything from the organ, to the piano and harp. I told him what songs we wanted-again, none of which are traditional-and he played it all perfectly!! The ceremony was my favorite part of the day and I will cherish that part of our wedding always.  If you are thinking of having your wedding here-DO IT!! The First Baptist Church of Pasadena is a beautiful historical structure. The facilities and grounds look very well taken care of. The Sanctuary is gorgeous, it's close to City hall and within walking distance of many hotels in the Old Town area of Pasadena. First Baptist Church of Pasadena is an elegant, beautiful, spiritual church that I go to attend classical concerts ! Lovely pastor. Great God inspired scripture based teachings. Friendly and diverse (ages, races, schools of thought) congregation. Worship music is very approachable mix of contemporary with some traditional roots.

You'll be hard pressed to find a better church. Oh and the building itself is beautiful too.
