name: First Christian Church - Pomona / Claremont Campus
reviewSummary:
Unbelievable architecture! It's a huge arch (boat) inside. A human fete! Seats are hard to sit on...need new pillow cussions...especially for an opera performance of hours. Gave me a royal back-ache.
Beautiful stage for the performance. Delightful...and a good community outreach program.
Grounds are a bloom with gorgeous flowers...very well maintained. Worth the trip to see.
Large capacity parking lot...well lit...beacons us. I am a first-time mom to a beautiful three-year-old. I started taking my daughter to First Christian Church Child Development Center shortly after she turned 1. I was nervous and anxious and had no idea what to expect. The staff all put me at ease, assured me of their open door policy, that I could pop-in and check on my little girl whenever I wanted and listened to my list as long as my arm of things to do to care for my child. The school feeds my daughter breakfast and lunch, which takes so much pressure off of my shoulders on having to prepare and pack her food every day. As a parent community, we donate snacks for the classroom and other small things that the kids would enjoy or the teachers can utilize, it really does take a village!

Over the years, we have now seen some new faces as with any school and have been honored with a new Director, Cristina. She is organized and motivated, ensures there is consistency with all of the children and their routines, which we all know as parents, is very important. She has set-up an online app for parents to be able to communicate at any time of the day with the teachers, as well as be able to see what activities and meals your child had that day. It has created total transparency with the school, the teachers are happy and loving and Cristina is working hard towards continual improvement at the school What more could I ask for when trusting the care of my daughter with someone else. As parents, we were very apprehensive looking for a daycare for our 3 year old daughter, each us took different years off from work to stay home  with her. With that being said, I learned about the daycare facility from a colleague. I went for a visit and signed my daughter up the very next week. It has been over a year later, my daughter absolutely loves going and loves her friends and teachers so much. We feel at ease taking her to daycare, I have no worries with her there. I know she is being well cared for and that she is having fun and learning. We have 5 other older children and we have never like a daycare like this before. We are very happy with everyone here. Truly, sincerely happy. Plus, we get updates through out the month of what is going on, plus pictures. Plus the daycare always does something fun each month with the kids, whether it is a picnic, bringing in a magician, mobile aquarium, etc. The staff is great from Ms. TK, Ms. Liliana, Ms. Kami, plus the Director is very approachable. My daughter has been going to this daycare since she was 3 months old. She will turn 3 in March 2020. I absolutely love the staff and Cristina the director. Since Cristina took over as the director (1-2years ago), I have seen an improvement with the staff, security, cleanliness, and curriculum. She also implemented the online Kinderlime app that allows parents to view pictures of their kids throughout the day, eat/sleep/potty schedule, activities and will message you with important info about your child or about what is going on with the center.

She is seen everywhere around the center making sure everything is ran smoothly, fixing things, cutting branches that interfere with the playground area, plunging a toilet like today, volunteering with parents on a weekend to improve the daycare, fundraising  for a new playground, working on stricter security measures, etc. This woman unstoppable. A force to be reckoned with.

My daughter had Lidia as an infant (treated my daughter like her own, but does not work there any longer), had Ms. Brenda / Ms. Taylor & Ms. Lilliana (My dream team) when she was 1-2yrs old. My daughter Loves these ladies, especially Ms. Taylor. She currently has Ms. Kammy, whom is the BEST for this age group. She is great with the kids. My daughter has learned so much in her classroom. She is very professional, very friendly, patient, a great communicator with the kids and parents.
Highly recommend this daycare. I wouldn’t take my daughter here if I didn’t recommend this daycare. Absolutely Love this School! The Director and Teachers are ALL amazing with the kids. Treat them as if they are their own! My Son love his "Ms.Kammy"! The curriculum is fantastic. I cant deny that half on my sons Genius-ness comes from this school for certain! Thats why the name is "First Christian" because not matter who you are they should always be your FIRST choice!

The people are friendly, Pastor Bill is passionate about the Word of God, and the environment is welcoming. If there is a church you’re looking for, the FCCC is the one of the best places to attend. The first time I walked in I felt that I was at home and have been going ever since then. Everyone is welcome and treated with kindness and respect. This church and the members are amazing! Very welcoming and friendly environment. Have been attending this church for several years now with my family and would recommend it to anyone looking for a church to call home and hear the word of God! reviewSummary: I do not regularly attend this church, but I've gone a couple times for their ashes to go on Ash Wednesday, and I just really appreciate soooo much that they offer this. Thank you so much for offering this for all of the people with hectic schedules who aren't able to make it to mass.  It really means a lot. I have attended First Christian Church of Tucson for 14 years. This is an open and affirming congregation. We practice open membership and communion. Our church supports important community service organizations such as the community food bank. Our facility houses two other congregations that worship here as well as the Desert Spring preschool. No matter where you are on life's journey, you will feel welcome here. First Christian Church of Tucson, which has a denominational affiliation with the Christian Church (Disciples of Christ), is a loving and caring church.  Several years ago the church proudly celebrated its 100th year anniversary in Tucson.  It has been recognized as a leader for social causes in the community.  Several organizations such as Habitat for Humanity and Humane Borders found their roots in this church. I came to this church 10 years ago from another Disciples of Christ church in Ohio and like that church, I find this church to be warm, welcoming and spiritually comforting.  If you are looking for church home this is a good place to start. I came to First Christian Church when my husband was ill and I was struggling to believe that God loved me, and I learned there that God loves me and I do not need to do anything to earn that love.  First Christian and God's love has transformed me in that I want to spread God's love with others and so I work with people who have a mental health challenge to help them recover.  If you are looking for a church that truly cares about people and wants people to experience God's gracious love, come to First Christian Church.  Sometimes it is confused with another church with a similar name, but the two churches are very different.  People at First Christian are encouraged to think and discover for themselves how to relate to God.  It is the first church I've ever attended that encouraged me to think and to question. reviewSummary:

I drive by this church a few times a week and my heart aches. I believe the leaders of the congregation want to create an inclusive atmosphere, but they are doing more harm than good.

Scripture makes clear to us that God made both men and women in His image.

"So God created man in his own image, in the image of God he created him; male and female he created them." Genesis 1:27

He didn't make a mistake when He made you a man or woman. The Bible tells us in Psalm 139:14 that you are wonderfully made.

God's Word also tells us how homosexuality of any kind is a sin and an unclean spirit. It enters a person through trauma or as a familial spirit.

If anyone is claiming to be a Christian church, but they do not follow what the Bible instructs then they are just a building with a sign.

Leviticus 18:22 Leviticus 20:13 1 Corinthians 6:9-11 Romans 1:26-27 Jude 1:7 1 Timothy 1:10 and so many more verses

We all struggle with our past. We all struggle with sin. You are not alone. The problem is when we start calling good evil and evil good. When we start contorting the Bible to say what we want or what makes us comfortable, we avoid the growth that needs to happen to heal.

Jesus loves you and wants a personal relationship with you. I know you are hurting, I know you are confused and I know you feel like an outcast. Ask Jesus to come into your heart, wash you clean of all sin, give you a new heart and to begin your healing.

Your desire to be a part of a church family is beautiful, healthy and it's only the beginning of your journey. Find one that aligns with the truth that the Holy Spirit wants to speak into your life. May God convict the congregation of First Christian, so that they once again turn back to Him. If you want to truly experience the love of God, check this place out. It's one of the few churches I've been to that had representatives of every age, sex, gender, race, or sexuality. They actually have fun in their worship, which many other churches could learn from. Finally, a church that truly cares less about who you are on the outside and focuses instead on cultivating the light you already carry within. Genuine honesty, zero hypocrisy. Come as you are actually means something here. In the end, Jesus is our judge — not imperfect humans.

name: First Christian Church of Augusta - Augusta Campus
reviewSummary:
Walking along Greene Street, with its long line of monuments, memorials, and those quiet pockets of shade that make Augusta's historic core feel so lived‑in, it's almost impossible not to be pulled toward the First Christian Church. The red brick, the tall white steeple, the way the building anchors the corner at Seventh and Greene. It all has that unmistakable presence of a congregation that has shaped the city for nearly two centuries. The historical marker out front gives you the essentials, but the deeper story adds even more texture to what you see when you stand there.

The current sanctuary, completed in 1875, reflects a blend of Romanesque Revival and Gothic Revival architecture, a combination that gives the building its distinctive profile. The soaring 168‑foot steeple still rises above the surrounding blocks. Even after a fire destroyed the earlier sanctuary in 1870, parts of that structure were incorporated into the new building, a quiet architectural continuity that ties the modern church to its nineteenth‑century roots. Restoration work began in 1989, part of a long effort to preserve both the building and the congregation's place in Augusta's civic landscape.

The marker reads, "The Christian Church (Disciples of Christ) began in Kentucky in the early years of the nineteenth century. Dr. Daniel Hook and Captain and Mrs. Edward Campfield established Augusta's First Christian Church in 1835, despite great suspicion and negativity from more established Protestant denominations. Philanthropist Emily Tubman aided the fledgling congregation by donating the first building (later Tubman High School for girls), convincing Georgia lawyer James S. Lamar to study and to become the church's pastor in 1852, and donating new buildings for the church's relocation to Greene and McIntosh Streets in 1874. Restoration of the structure began in 1989."

It is marker number 121-9 and it was erected in 2005 by the Georgia Historical Society and the Congregation of First Christian Church (Disciples of Christ). This church family is just what we as Christians need for fighting against the evils of this this world.

name: First Christian Church of Fort Lauderdale - Fort Lauderdale Campus
reviewSummary:
The First Christian Church of Ft Lauderdale was started by Maude Bollinger and Ruth Repp who offered Sunday school classes on Repp's front porch to the Ft Lauderdale community which was only 143 people at that time. Church services were held at several locations in Ft. Lauderdale including the old Fort Lauderdale Sentinel building.

In 1925, a benefactor donated land for a church at the corner of Southeast 13th Street and Southeast Third Avenue on the site of a former rock pit. Lumber to build the church arrived on Sept. 16, 1926. The very next day the Hurricane of 1926 destroyed the church records, lumber, the tent they were working out of, and all of their equipment. Two children and two adult members of the congregation lost their lives. The church rose from this devastating loss and completed the church building in 1927. A later expanded building incorporates the original church structure.

I love a historic church and I was able to check out First Christian Church of Ft Lauderdale during a tag sale. They held the sale in their basement! I was amazed that there was a building with an actual basement in South Florida. The congregation was so warm and welcoming and I got invited to church service by Katherine. This church is gorgeous and you can feel the history within its walls. Church services are held every Sunday at 10:45. everytime my family is down here we love to go to this church. Great vibes. Great teaching Wednesday night bible study at 8pm is awesome! If I lived in Fort Lauderdale I would be attending this church. Old school Pastor who also serves on the worship team (as I do) and loves Jesus. Loved the stained glass windows and the word and the anointed. If we move here, this is out church where I will help find someone for video!

Phil
Jesus Lives This is, as I understand it, the second oldest continually operating church in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. It was founded in 1911 and continues today as a place where people from all walks of life worship God.

Although the church was once a formal member of the Disciples of Christ denomination, it has been an independent, non-denominational church for the last fifteen years or more. It is organized in the same manner as the churches in the Book of Acts and is elder led.

There is a sweet spirit among its congregation and, upon entering, you can feel the love of God. The multi-ethnic, international membership is a picture of South Florida. What sets them apart is their joyful, loving praise of Jesus Christ.

Sunday School starts at 9:30 a.m. and the church service follows at 10:45 a.m. with a live band leading praise and worship, a sermon from God's Word and communion. After the service, everyone retires to the basement Fellowship Hall for coffee and fellowship. It's a great opportunity to meet your fellow Christians and experience the move of God's Holy Spirit!

Come and join us. Let us worship the Lord, our God, together.

name: First Christian Church of Napa - Napa Campus
reviewSummary:
I moved to Napa in 2013 and left a church that I didn't think could be replaced. I was right, I tried and tried many different churches throughout the years and none made me feel like I belonged. Fast forward to 2021. The pandemic left its mark on so many people and so many ideals (especially around the church and gathering). I knew I needed help so in May of 2021 I decided to check out the Celebrate Recovery(C/R) at First Christian Church (FCC) on Tues. nights. I truly felt welcomed and decided that I wanted to keep attending C/R. I was invited to another church in the area for Sunday worship by someone that I had met in a phone conversation so I went to this church the next Sunday. No one greeted me, and I had to introduce myself and tell them I was new before someone came to lead me around and talk to me. Not a problem for me but if I was a shy new Christian, I know that I would have left. I did mention this to that pastor just because I think it was important for them to know. First impressions really do matter. I decided that the next Sunday I would try FCC. I loved the C/R, and many of the people there were regular attendees at FCC so I figured it was definitely worth the effort. When I got to FCC Sunday morning I was greeted by a very sweet and smiling Connections Ministry Leader who gave me a gift and set me up with connections to the church. The worship was amazing, the kids and family ministry was so terrific and truly caring, the Pastor was so "on Point" and the congregation was open and friendly. Like any family though, they are not perfect, but they try their best to love like Jesus and truly that is all that matters to me. We are all beautifully broken and when we can fit in a place where that is accepted, where we feel we can heal and not have to live up to some "perfect" standard,   then we are able to let Jesus heal us. I truly feel this is a place of healing and love. From the C/R to the Sunday sermons it is all about Jesus and fellowship. Thank you FCC for being faithful and honest to our Lord and Savior Jesus! I will never find a church to replace the one I left in 2013 but I found a church in FCC that is as honest and caring in their faith as my old home church. I am very happy to call FCC my home church. Are they perfect? No. Is any human or establishment? No. Do they love well? Yes, and that is truly all that matters to me. I have visited First Church three times consecutively. Worship services are beautiful! The Congregation is warm and welcoming, Senior Pastor Allen (prefers the use of his first name),  sermons; which by the way feels like a one on one personal conversation, display his keen knowledge of God's Word and delivers to the listeners historical biblical and culture back ground, as he spoon feeds deep theological doctrine. Having carefully dissected each biblical verse referenced in his sermon, which are also displayed on a large screen for parishioners review; Pastor Allen compares today's secular culture and Christian living throughout his conclusion. Check it out, if you want to freely worship, and enjoy the music ministry, Easy listening, comfortable atmosphere for the Body of Christ to experience The Holy Spirit. No Pretenses, just Followers of Christ trying to understand how to live the life they sing about.
Much Love,

name: First Church of Christ Scientist - Berkeley Campus
reviewSummary:
The Christian Science church in Berkeley by Maybeck is a stunning example of early 20th-century architecture. Designed by renowned architect Bernard Ralph Maybeck (1862 - 1957), the church is a masterpiece of the Arts and Crafts movement.

Designed and built at the cost of around $60,000 of 1910 money, the exterior of the church is characterized by its striking Craftsman, Gothic and Romanesque style architecture with mature Wisteria vines which give the building an unusual and inviting feel. The building with respect to its materials was rather unusual and innovative for its time.

Inside, the church is equally impressive. The soaring nave crossing is supported by a series of wooden trusses in the form of a Greek Cross which create a sense of grandeur and space. The stained and textured glass are particularly noteworthy, in contrast against the modified, industrial sash windows.

A striking feature of the church is the working Austin organ, which is located in a choir loft above the altar and the only one of its kind in the US. There is also an amazing interior, planted courtyard that is not viewable from the street. This courtyard is a must-see.

Overall, the Christian Science church in Berkeley by Maybeck is a true masterpiece of architecture and worthy of a visit. Its combination of warm materials, intricate details, and soaring spaces make it a truly unique and inspiring place of worship. The Church offers a free tour on the first Sunday of every month at about noon. One of Bernard Maybeck's masterpieces.  Like the UC Berkeley faculty club building, the real treat is waiting for you inside.  Try to go on the tour offered free on the first Sunday of the month, if you can.  In the late winter, the church is enveloped in wisteria.  Wonderful to see. I am not a believer of any. This slave tool will come back to haunt you. How can it be? I have never witnessed life return to someone that died. I know. I am no classification idiot to become. I can't be labeled. You can. May you find peace in your God. I don't have any. And if you find your lord and savior, let it be known I looked, I knocked, I expected. They did not answer, no door to open, I am not a child of the most high. I am not the son of man. I am without cause and broken because of. May you all be judged for my suffering with the judge you have taught. The website says that the doors are open, but when I visited on a Saturday, the whole church was closed :(

I studied this building in my architecture history class and know the interior well. It is too bad that I couldn’t experience it for myself A gorgeous building designed by ground-breaking architect Bernard Maybeck. It's a City of Berkeley landmarked site.

We look forward to the Sunday sermon because unlike other churches we have been around the world(we have lived in different countries because of work and the reason why we have been exposed to different evangelical churches)is that Ronnie teaches not only about the Love of God. He teaches without filtering the fact that God has nothing to do with the unrepentant. He teaches about what God does not tolerate. The teaching is not about the modern way of introducing God/Jesus. Where God is painted as all-loving, all-tolerant. In a world full of pain, confusion, and fake gospels my family appreciates a solid teaching without filtering the fierce God of the Bible. The heart of the church is the pastor because he serves the message. We will for sure miss him. Despite his coming retirement, we welcome the new Pastor with gratitude and joy. 🙏🏼

name: First Community Church - North Campus - Upper Arlington / Northwest Columbus Campus
reviewSummary:
Everyone is welcome in this church. The spaces, people, worship and clergy are warm and respectful. I was able to worship without being badgered to join. The music is as spiritual and up lifting as the messages and liturgy. Go there! You will be delighted in your time spent. I really appreciated the words and music of the hymns pposted on line today!  i can't drive to chuch and really want to still be a part.  Being able to see the hyms made it so much better.  Thanks!
Lindy Kehrle I have attended several large public events at the North Campus of First Community Church during the past several years.

I had been a member of First Community Church [during the 1970s] at a time when there had been only one location [three buildings that now are called the South Campus]; during the early 1990s, First Community Church built the North Campus and now has worship services at both the South Campus and the North Campus.

The facilities of the North Campus had been wonderful; the one drawback to that location [at least on February 25, 2018] had been the near-impossibility of finding the entrance to the parking lot [a left turn from northbound Dublin Rd. about 500 feet north of Fishinger Rd.].

My Uber driver had passed the church without having found an entrance to the parking lot and then had turned onto the next street to the north of the church but had been unable to find a different way to enter the parking lot from that street; eventually, we did successfully find the entrance to the parking lot. Nice church, fun to meet people near Old Hilliard and Upper Arlington. Great preaching, great snacks, good baby sitting. Teaches a good Holy Gospel. Nice church with a great service. Really enjoyed going there for Christmas mass. The building itself can hold lots of people!

name: First Community Church - Tuscaloosa Campus
reviewSummary: Enjoy the Veterans Day services. The pastor did a correlation between veterans in a Biblical passage out of the Bible great job I’m sure like many, you feel sometimes the Pastor is speaking directly to you that was me during the sermon this morning. Minister Gordon spoke about Being like Christ; through the week. A great place to visit.  I look forward to returning soon. Have a great time learning about God Love My Church

name: First Community South - Columbus Campus
reviewSummary:
My husband and I were married at First Community Church in June and it was absolutely perfect. Jill was amazing to work with and made sure that every detail was taken care of and that everyone knew what they needed to do. The Church is beautiful, and I appreciated that they welcomed non members to have their ceremony there. The ceremony was exactly what we wanted and we feel lucky to have had our wedding here. Wonderful Christian people who provide wonderful food and home items to get me through the month. So grateful for this place Sidewalks on First Avenue are treacherous.

No effort was made to clear them after any of the recent snow.  So dangerous.

Worst sidewalks in our community. This Church is phenomenal! You get so much here. Not just produce. And they even manage to put nice treats in there as well. Very well organized, and then you are Blessed. We were married here. Disappointed it was not open

name: First Congregational Christian - Birmingham Campus
reviewSummary: The repass was really nice!!!!! Thanks so much. Wonderful.

reviewSummary:
Right now the church is closed down because of the CV19 (virus ). When they  were open they would welcome you with open arms hand shakes,a special WELCOME greetings for first time and returning visitors. Even though  the doors are closed the messages are still delivered .The members receive emails with updated announcements and time of service ,Sunday school etc.
A GREAT MEMBERSHIP TO BE A PART OF AND SUPPORT.
GGC A very special place with wonderful people! Come and visit us. We welcome all with open arms. Service is on Sundays at 11:00. It's a perfect place to praise the Lord. Great service

name: First Congregational Church - Colorado Springs Campus
reviewSummary:
Very disgraceful to Christians around the world. Jesus never made or said anything mistakenly. How you feel about your sexuality is up to you, but don’t put your human desires and feelings in the church as it does not align with Christ. Yes nobody is perfect, everybody is imperfect in different ways. But don’t OK and welcome the sin of the world to the place where you seek to be forgiven of it. Warm and welcoming
A breath of fresh air
And great music We haven't been inside of a church in many years. We recently visited First Congregational and enjoyed the  worship service.   Music and message were worshipful and positive and pointed toward a caring creator wanting to touch the lives of others through this church. The church appears to have a wide range of ages and friendly people.  My first  impression from our visit is the church supports  or provides a wide range of  agencies, services  providing assistance and care around  Colorado Springs.  Positive place. I heard about your banner. I would like to know if there is a find in place to donate to a new one? I'm a pagan, but believe in your kindness and love for others, and would like to participate in making sure you're able to express it. Please let me know if you have a gofundme! A sanctuary of kindness- filled with caring members that are deeply connected to Colorado Springs’ progressive past.  My wife and I were married here way back in 1999- it has been a deeply meaningful landmark in our spiritual journey.

name: First Congregational Church - Columbus Campus
reviewSummary: I went to this Church for Christmas 2025 and my god. The inside is other worldly. I showed up to volunteer Christmas morning,but I wasn't aware of prior registration. I did however stay a couple of hours to help out. I met some great people,good conversations with the staff working. Also it warmed my heart to give back,I met some nice people who were there for the dinner. I definitely look forward to helping out this coming Christmas. I've always signed up on the website for a few jobs . I look forward to seeing everyone again. Be blessed.... Experience God and enjoy learning about Christ's love for everyone.  The stained glass rocks! They won't let you bring any food out of the place and if you get caught they tell you to leave. Just went to the Christmas dinner that they had from 11 to 3 p.m. . Got there at 11 took them two and a half hours to get me down there to the dining hall to eat. It is a long wait. This church is BEAUTIFUL!  I think they have a place for the homeless to sleep at night.. Stop by and see the church.. Talk to the homeless.  See how you can offer help. Now..you know what I think would be a GREAT idea?  Ok so..look.. did you know that you don't HAVE to go to church to know how to live like Jesus lives?  He is kinda like those footprints in the sand when you thought you were walking alone.  Well.. so.. most of my homeless friends know EXACTLY what I'm talking about so.. I don't think Sunday school is necessary for them..it's for those busy people who forgot about God's school before life made them so busy.. I'm pretty sure my homeless friends can just go fishing.. and I bet I know a few places that will donate fishing poles, some hooks and a bobber if you don't prefer fishing on the bottom at that free park.  But... I mean those doors to GODS CHURCH should be OPEN!!!! I know a few people who can throw on a Security Guard jacket to protect the people.. but if you're a true believer.. you really don't need protection from anyone on earth.. Now...if you could kindly spread the word to ALL denominations and in EVERY language.. it would be a whole lot easier and faster than me having to do that before I get to go fishing because honestly.. I can't take a vacation as long as my homeless friends have to sleep in the rain, snow, heat.. you know how hard it is to wash dirt off your hands when it's freezing outside and there's no warm water? I may have walked a few miles in their shoes.. You know how some religions wash their feet?  I'm pretty sure Jesus was homeless.. and maybe nobody took him in so he just died to show you all how much you meant to him no matter what.. well ..if the churches won't even let the homeless people in..just bull doze those churches down and start with the next generation.. teach them how to plant grass and herbs so they don't have to steal them like they tried to at that WalMart I visited the other day... and live wild with the animals of the earth and only eat what's necessary to keep your body fueled.. We don't need to keep churches just because they're pretty or "historic" .. buildings are not more important than people .

name: First Congregational Church - Hudson Campus
reviewSummary:
Sunday service wise this place is fantastic. 3 SUN morning times. You always leave feeling re-invigorated.

Daycare wise this is one of the best childcare locations in the area. The teachers all care so much and have a deep passion for each kiddo. My son has been here for 6 months and we can already see a marked improvement in his overall development. Which due to the pandemic was lacking some.

Cheers 1st Con Warm and inviting. Great semi-mix of contemporary and tradition service style. The huge pipe organ in the chapel is almost as beautiful as it is played. The good Reverend Peter Wiley is a nice fella and a gifted preacher. Unfortunately, they have a problem with special needs on their journey.   Steve H. has a problem with autistic/aspberger  teens.  Also, speaks down to female parents. Wherever you are on your journey. You may find spirituality and true love of Christ elsewhere. This church made me feel awful. Beautiful Historical church.    Historical Pipe organ played every Sunday.  It's worth a visit or two or three. I don't go to this church, I bring someone to it. I must say, if you are looking for a home church, this is a very Christian place!!! And they work amazing with children, and the place if FULL of children! Love!

name: First Congregational Church - Riverside Campus
reviewSummary:
My wife and I were attending a Candlelight String Quartet concert-Vivaldi's Four Seasons  The First Congregational Church-Riversude, CA .

It was the first time going to this venue and we wanted to see if sitting in woiden pews for 60 minutes was going to be uncomfortable or not.

I'm very glad to report the pews all have cushions on them. It made sitting on the wooden church pews comfortable.

The venue itself is intimate and seen to suit this classical music concert. There are 16 rows of pews, so the musicians are closer to evettyone than at other Candlelight  venues.

The sound acoustics in this church venue was great for this concert.  The church with all of the candkes (battery operated) just added another level of anbiance to this concert.

My wife & I look forward to attending more Candlelight concerts at this church venue. Absolutely amazing went to see Juan Gabriel tribute. Such a beautiful performance by the violinists the cello and the viola player . Will have to do another candlelight tribute concert to another band n like the Beatles . Can’t wait !!!! I booked tickets for our 48th wedding Anniversary. As fans of Fleetwood Mac, we were not disappointed! The talented young musicians really did their homework. Simply Amazing! Hands down one of the most beautiful concerts I’ve ever attended. The music was so moving that I found myself tearing up more than once. The arrangements were incredibly thoughtful and did a stunning job honoring the original artists (Queen and Abba) while allowing the string musicians to truly shine.

The candlelit setting elevated the entire experience — intimate, elegant, and unforgettable. Even if you don’t typically listen to classical music or string ensembles, this is the perfect introduction. It’s accessible, emotional, and absolutely captivating.

My only complaint? It ended too soon. The hour flew by, and I genuinely could have listened all night. Highly recommend — I will absolutely attend again. This church has been just what Ive needed for my spiritual health. With a young growing family the welcoming atmosphere has been great and surprisingly accommodating. The open and affirming message and community engagement is a breath of fresh air. I think it's the perfect blend of traditional worship with progressive ideas and theology.

name: First Congregational Church of Akron - Akron Campus
reviewSummary: My host Alex went above and beyond for my daughter’s prom send off. The establishment is very big and clean and can accommodate anything you need. Would highly recommend and we will be back soon Great Church! The staff were very helpful during a recent visit I had for a recording gig. Very resourceful and kind. I'm not religious but this church is so welcoming! Their food pantry is great too It is extremely disgusting the way the congregation is acting today. I'm extremely disappointed in this church. They say they are godly and accepting of everyone but then treats security like absolute garbage. That is very ungodly behavior to someone that was there to serve and protect you. All of you should be ashamed of your behavior today. It was extremely uncalled for. I went to this church for the very first time today and used their food pantry services.  I will be honest with you, I have never met a nicer group of people.  Each and every person was just lovely to me, taking me by the hand and showing me how everything worked.  They made me feel right at home.  They were all just so helpful, kind and well, just plain wonderful.  The generosity of spirit in the people I encountered today at their food pantry was just beyond amazing.  I was so thankful.  Thank you to all of the fantastic people volunteering at their food pantry for your kindnesses.

name: First Congregational Church of Alameda - Alameda Campus
reviewSummary:
Warm, inviting community. Beautiful church, lovely music, thought-provoking sermons that relate to the present day with historical context.  Open and affirming. Focused on social justice. All are welcome! Some ten years ago, I was looking for a church that follows a Christian path while holding respect for other paths and found United Church of Christ.  We started coming occasionally and enjoyed the thoughtful sermons, the beauty and artistry of the sanctuary and the warmth of the congregants.  But what really clinched it for me is that my daughter, then about 4 years old, starting asking when we could go back to church again.  There was a feeling and a spirit there that really attracted her, and we saw that as a very good sign.  This has become a wonderful spiritual home for our whole family. This is a beautiful old church that balances the traditions of their colonial roots with thoughtful, contemporary relevance to worship in the 21st century. This multi-generational congregation welcomes all and offers much to families, couples and singles without regard to race, gender or sexual orientation. The First Congregational Church of Alameda (FCCA) is a congregation where God truly is still speaking. They achieve what seems elusive to so many other churches: a vibrant, innovative, yet respectful, balance of deeply traditional Congregational roots and dynamic contemporary theology. The result is warm welcoming worship that's well crafted, fresh and authentic.

Their life giving use of new worship arts, beyond just great music, all rise out of the morning's worship theme, such as: well choreographed liturgical dance; deeply theologically biblio-drama; visual artists create altars and other elements of the sacred space; evocative bulletin covers made in house; and technology and digital media, when used, successfully avoid the contemporary trap of using clip art to make easy, sentimental Christian scenes.

The congregation is truly kind & welcoming and their work in social justice is progressive and exemplary. And their children's program::: they've got more children than they can fit on the chancel stairs ! Also I hear, a great supportive question-embracing youth program...

These examples must be just part of why FCCA is a growing & exciting story of Love Embodied in the East Bay.

Unequivocally 5 Stars !! I do Jazzercise on Saturdays there at the church.Thankful to the Church for accommodating us!

name: First Congregational Church of Anaheim Chapel - Anaheim Campus
reviewSummary:
Great place for fellowship and worshiping the Lord. Attending Church is really inspiring. I enjoy attending here very much on Mondays.
Dinner is awesome and after we receive the word of Jesus  in Church which is fulfilling, singing the music and hearing the testimonies of how great Jesus is  having faith and believing in him can and does change lives thank you Jesus. Attended church here, the pastor and people are great! If you are looking for a church home a great place to be! The grounds are also magnificent! The perfect place for a wedding! The best HomeTown Church in the world!!!!
Friendly people Friendly Church.. Beautiful Church
Godly people ❤️❤️❤️

name: First Congregational Church of Auburn - Auburn Campus
reviewSummary: First Congregational Church of Auburn is a warm and welcoming church. Pastor Dan embodies the love of Christ; Love for all, in all walks of life. Pastor Dan's sermons will touch your heart with his delightful mix of humor and empathy. Pastor Dan has a true understanding of the human condition and what it means to love one another. Love is all. As a new family in the area, finding 1CC was a genuine gift from God.  Here we found a community who lives the message of Jesus by welcoming the stranger, loving one another, and bringing justice, healing, and love to a broken world.  Reverend Dan's messages are always poignant, relevant and related to whatever issues our world is facing.  By pointing us to the truth of God's unending love for not only us, but all people on Earth, we are reminded of the Divine Love that Jesus came to teach of and are filled with hope that there is goodness in this world.  We also greatly enjoy meeting other young families through this community and benefit greatly from the supportive children's program. GREAT: friendly people, dynamic Pastor, terrific message, wonderful music, SO welcoming. All-congregation breakfast once a month is awesome - A+++ cooks! This church is very welcoming to all.  No matter your race, gender or the color of your skin or hair.  And our pastor Dan Spacek, feeds us on Sunday in ways we understand and ways that relate to us in these current days. The best church I have ever been to.  The entire congregation is so welcoming to all.  They are like family and the pastor will move you with his message every time.

name: First Congregational Church of Berkeley - Berkeley Campus
reviewSummary:
Concert at the church was AMAZING! The parking lot was not free, a man demanded $15. This seems to be an ongoing situation. But every thing rose is nice and very clean!
LGBTQ

The performances were AMAZING! In the evening of Dec. 21st, 2025, I was here for a Voices of Music performance.  Parked at the church parking lot, approached by a person demanding 10 dollars for parking.  The person had no credentials, and when I was trying to scan the QR code on the parking stall, the person started yelling, "I am here, you pay me.  If you don't like it, you can leave."  The person was quite agitated, and out of safety concerns, I left.  I hope that troubled person is not affiliated with the church.  The Telegraph Channing Garage charges 4 dollars flat rate for evenings, which is one block away. I love this church! This place of worship welcomes the full participation of every sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, race, nationality, ability, and age in worship. 🌈

This community loves Jesus, but is also open to those who are spiritually curious or questioning their faith. They are also deeply involved in the community and social justice efforts (anti-racism work, hunger programs, environmental justice, etc.)

Service is at 10 am (in-person and live-streamed), and they have communion on the first Sunday of the month (open to all). I can't recommend this church enough! Love the space. I was privileged to see Alice Walker and Angela Davis there...I'm still star struck!!😍 This is a fine venue for musical performances, with nice acoustics and seat layout. Every seat but those in the back of the balcony is a good one. It competes with two truly excellent venues for the affections of Cal Performances concert-goers, so is rarely considered a favorite, but it is a great place to see a concert.

name: First Congregational Church of Burlington, UCC
reviewSummary: We moved here from Cincinnati 8 years ago and looked at quite a few churches.  We found our home at First Congregational Church.  It is welcoming, open, affirming, peace and social justice focused and a Christ following community.  Our children love the children and youth programming, the music and worship experiences are phenomenal and church staff are amazing!  We love the numerous opportunities to serve and be in community as adults. Our family has been coming to this church since 2009, and it has become our community.  This is an Open and Affirming congregation, which is important to me, and all really are welcome here.  The preaching is both thought and prayer provoking and always spurs meaningful discussion together as a family.  I am a more loving and kind human for my relationships and time spent with this community. This church and all it stands for had been part of my life since I was a baby. For various reasons, I stopped attending but, was able to revisit recently. The inside is classically gorgeous. The minister speaks from her heart and goes well beyond the expected in helping and speaking with you. I highly recommend a visit. This church is very involved in making the community better through mission, social justice, etc.  Great worship experience from preaching to music to welcoming members.  Looking for a place to be involved?  Try us out! Stiff, not as friendly as Metodist church next door, less homeless friendly in posability sshop

name: First Congregational Church of Columbus - Main Campus
First Congregational Church of Long Beach, UCC - Long Beach Campus
reviewSummary:
Interesting place. We came for a concert and the sound was impeccable. Seats are horrible for an hour and a half performance. After visiting 3 times,  I can say this church is a unique breath of fresh air and activity.  They are living into the call to care for one another and the greater community. The activities really have something for everyone - book groups, Bible Studies, musical theater, paddling, food drives, and even a drag show trivia event!  This church has clearly worked to live into the idea that all really are welcome. Beautiful historic place..Great woodworking artistry inside the Great brick edifice
.Century plus in age..Grand pipe organ.  Parking only Jesus could die for.  Bring ur skates or scooter
Happy Easter. Rejoice in the Lord Church buildings should be utilized during non-worship times. However, this is not the best venue for concerts. The columns on the first floor obstruct views. The acoustics require amplification. Progressive church and welcoming to all. The sound of the organ is amazing.    When the morning light hits the windows is a sight to behold.

name: First Congregational Church of Los Angeles - Los Angeles (Downtown) Campus
reviewSummary:
A beautiful and welcoming church. The music was absolutely incredible, and the atmosphere was peaceful and inspiring. I especially loved how everyone was invited to be themselves and feel accepted. Thank you for such a meaningful and uplifting service. ❤️ As a Los Angeles wedding photographer, I recently had the pleasure of photographing a ceremony at this incredible church — and it was such a memorable experience. The space is LGBTQ+ friendly, warm, and welcoming to all couples, which makes it even more special.

The church itself is stunning, with beautiful gothic architecture, tall arches, and elegant details that give every photo a timeless look. The light inside is soft and atmospheric, creating a perfect mood for wedding ceremonies. For professional photographers, I’d recommend bringing some additional external lighting, especially near the front section of the church, where natural light can be limited.

Couples should keep in mind that the time allowed for photography inside is limited, since the venue charges per hour spent there. In my case, we didn’t have much extra time for portraits inside, but we still captured some incredible moments before heading outdoors.

Overall, I truly enjoyed shooting here — it’s a one-of-a-kind location that blends classic architecture with inclusivity and heart. Highly recommend it for couples looking for a Los Angeles church wedding venue that’s both elegant and welcoming.

— Nem, Wedding Photographer | NZ Wedding Studio Attended Roger Sayer's Organ recital.  Incredible church and has the world's second largest pipe organ.  Unforgettable experience We came here tonight for a show. Such a beautiful building and acoustics. The organ is a masterpiece. I could stare into the stained glass panels for hours as well. Attended a family friend's wedding here and it was very solemn atmosphere. Great architecture, love the old craftsmanship of woodcarvings, pipe organ added substance to the occasion. Lots of parking, clean and we'll stocked facilities in several strategic places. Helpful, patient and friendly security staff. This is a good venue to consider for large gathering of same faith.

name: First Congregational Church of Oakland - Oakland Campus
reviewSummary:
East Bay Children's Book Project is a small community based organization that works to put good books into the hands of children in need.  We rent space in the First Congregational Church of Oakland where our clients, who are teachers, social workers, medical providers and other nonprofits, come to choose books for the children they serve.  We have been renting our space for 9almost  years and our experience here has been excellent.  It is a beautiful, historic building, our rent is very reasonable, our space works very well for our needs. Ronnie, the building coordinator, is very easy to communicate with and is responsive to our needs.  He makes an effort to get to know us and supports our mission.

We highly recommend the First Congregational Church of Oakland as a space for any community organization to rent.  It is welcoming and has many types of spaces that can accommodate a wide variety of needs. My nonprofit organization, Genesis Interfaith Organizing, has been a tenant of First Congregational for nearly a decade. The event space has a good amount of free (safe) parking, many good options for large and small gathering and a great staff that will support your event. The location is near public transit (a few blocks from BART, many AC Transit options). I recommend the space as it centrally located and a nice communal vibe. FCCO is an amazing community space that charges very reasonable rates for hosting events. It was a pleasure meeting and working with Ronnie and Brian to find a space to record some music in. They are both so kind, warm and attentive and helped me immensely in getting my recording project completed.

If you need a venue to host your next event don't hesitate to reach out to Ronnie today! I have been renting space for teaching classes at FCCO for seventeen years! 17 YEARS of excellent service and rapport.

* FCCO always has our room clean, organized and ready for us. I never have to worry if the room is going to be setup when I get there. This is so valuable in itself because it means NO STRESS for me. Something I cannot say for some of our other rentals. THANKS FCCO!

* Ronnie, who is in charge of bookings, is a pleasure to work with and a breath of fresh air. You can tell that he enjoys working with people and he truly cares about your experience at FCCO. He is professional, organized & friendly.

* Brian is also pretty darn awesome! He is in charge of setting up our class for us and is ALWAYS there if we ever need anything or help of any kind. We feel like we are in good hands with Brian every single night.

* Yes, the building is old and needs some repairs ... but honestly, this does not affect our experience at all. It is immaculately clean and the excellent service and welcoming attitude cancels that out!

THANK YOU FCCO. FCCO has hosted California Revels since 2019, giving us a home when we left the nearby Scottish Rites complex. They have provided wonderful support, and helped to save our organization with their gracious welcome and help over the years , especially through Covid and its effects-- and we are now in our 40th Anniversary year! We have our office there, we rehearse there and have performed there. Ronnie Casey and the staff are amazing. They extend the same welcome and professional assistance to all the groups that are lucky enough to share this historic space. As the Artistic Director of California Revels, I know how well they respond to every difficulty!

name: First Congregational Church of Palo Alto - Palo Alto Campus
reviewSummary:
We love the First Congregational Church. I was first exposed to FCCPA by attending their awesome Spring Musicals. (These are a must-see.) When our daughter was around five years of age, we decided to participate in one of the church services as we wanted a good wholesome, progressive environment to raise our daughter. We fell in love with the church, the pastors, and especially the community. First Congo is the place where we belong.

Although I never thought I would be a “church retreat goer,” I look forward to them every year and cherish the special bonds created during our gatherings. We’ve hosted fundraising events like wine tastings and Fondue parties and have participated in events like caroling down Christmas Tree Lane. There is Vacation Bible School, family camping trips, youth groups, and lots more for the kids.

I find myself looking forward to church and Dave’s weekly sermons. And the music is second to none! Each week we get to listen to Joe, our outstanding, talented organist and music director, to one-of-kind soloists, the church choir, and sometimes a Blues band.

I have made forever friendships from folks at First Congo and love this open and affirming environment that I’m proud to call my community. If you are looking for a unique church community, I’d give us a try and make sure to let people know that you are new so we can welcome you with open arms. First Congo church has been such a blessing for our family. My 3 boys enjoy going to church, the youth group, vacation bible school summer camp, family events, and the annual plays. Dave, our pastor, has done a wonderful job transitioning to virtual worship while still keeping it engaging. The music and choir is amazing. We are so lucky to have found this welcoming, family-friendly church that we all love. My husband and I have been members of this church for 25 years.  We have participated in many of the activities offered:  Board Membership Pick-a-Parties, Vacation Bible School, Youth Mission Trips,  Biblical Musical Plays, etc.

My favorite times are those spent with the children of the Congregation.  The children are given extraordinary opportunities to grow in spirit in a safe place where they can ask questions and get answers that make sense.

It is a great environment for the family to widen their spiritual life. I'm a celiac who has worked on staff at this church for a few years now. At a certain point I wanted to take communion but there were no safe options for gluten-free people. I spoke with the communion organizers and now they offer gluten free crackers and grape juice whenever communion happens! I educated them on the concept of cross-contact, and they were very attentive about it, so I definitely feel safe here. We have been members for five years. We shopped around for churches in the area for quite a while. When we came to FCCPA, we felt right at home. The community is welcoming, loving, warm, and supportive. This is a community that lives out its faith. The pastors encourage us to ask questions, be curious, and even explore our own doubts. They also inspire us to be the hands of Jesus in the world.  My spiritual cup is full when we are here. And, my children love going to church!

name: First Congregational Church Of Savannah - Savannah Campus
reviewSummary: My wife and I were married here in 1987 and we are still together! Lovely Church with a beautiful square out front, perfect, to take photographs with the wedding party and Bishop. Wonderful folks at the Church as well.

name: First Congregational Church of Winter Park - Winter Park Campus
reviewSummary:
I stopped by on Sunday morning to check out the service and get a feel for the community. The greeters were very helpful and pointed me exactly where I needed to go without making me feel pressured. And the staff clearly puts a lot of work into keeping the grounds looking sharp and inviting. I recently moved to WP and searching for a welcoming and progressive congregation. I’m a musician and vocalist, so I aim to engage/contribute my talents in a new Church home. I was the organist (sometimes pianist) for my previous church and served as a traveling evangelist ministering in music for more than 20 years -  I appointed church, organist, at the age of 12!

Most importantly, I need a church family that would welcome my tiny companion puppy. She is extremely well-behaved and would quietly sit on my lap, wrapped in swaddling clothes (blanket) for the duration of the service.

I look forward to your reply and thank you for your thoughtful consideration of my spiritual needs Delightful walk through Bethlehem experience. You could tell that the whole church had invested in preparing for this from the 2-year-old sheep to the lovely little dancing angels, the townspeople selling their wares, a scary Herod, a band of shepherds with a real fire, the holy family surrounded by real animals, a convincing angel Gabriel and a legion of elementary-age Roman soldiers. Costumes were fabulous. The scenery was very clever. Our favorite was a very pregnant, elderly Elizabeth who was very funny. This is a perfect event for families with young children and started our Christmas off on a joyful, meaningful note. Loved it! Could be better advertised - it's worth it. Come see for yourself, an open and affirming church, wherever you are in your spiritual walk, you're welcome. The rule is: there is no rule. We embrace diversity, we are routed in tradition, not stuck in it. We are a Christian church and we try to act in the way Jesus taught.
Sunday service at 10am, programs available, heck go to our web page. See you there? This church has changed my life. Loving caring people and Pastor. Incredible outreach, heavenly music, everyone is excepted,  it is open and affirming.  If you are looking for a spiritual family this is it!.

name: First Congregational Church, Bellevue
reviewSummary: I am brought to tears every time I listen to the sermons. Such great messages! I’m not usually a church person, I prefer to connect with God on my own, but my husband loves the music (organ & horns) and I feel welcome as I am. As a concert venue the acoustics are live and what you would expect from a high ceiling and shallow, wide sanctuary. Very comfortable seats and nice amenities. We’ve never felt more genuinely welcomed than by these wonderful folks.  The best thing was NOT having to leave our brains behind - thoughtful, relevant message and the music was superb! We went for Ash Wednesday service, and were very welcomed by other parishioners and the clergy. A nice atmosphere. Wish we could visit more! A welcoming place for believers, seekers, and doubters.

name: First Congregational Church, UCC - Atlanta Campus
reviewSummary: Wonderful place to visit and enjoy a nice concert. Visited with a friend and had an amazing time listening to the music of Hyrule. I was walking downtown Atlanta and saw this beautiful historic structure!  Read their amazing history!  And I saw a sign with  great encouraging words...hard to read because of the trees but encouraging words.  I hope to visit soon. Two brown men helped me and my son. They brought us a room at a very nice elegant motel for one night. Fed is! I came back three weeks after, and was mistreated by two of their staff members. We haven't been back since. Enjoyed the Sweet Lu quartet's performance at their setup called The Commons. Excellent show, and the food was good also. Wonderful renovations to the church. Delightful Pastor. Congregation quite old, not the building but the community of elders. Seriously needs young people. That said, totally enjoyed the homily and the old fashioned feel to that. Not asking for bells and whistles just more vigor. The group communion was unfamiliar to me and certain changes to the liturgy I found concerning but that’s just me I suppose. The church is historic and of great significance to free Black people in the US. The stained glass includes such “saints” as John Brown and images of “colored” children. The organist feels divinely inspired but the choir not so much. The Fisk Jubilee Singers first performed here in Atlanta and they’re returning soon for a concert. It’s the church of WEB DuBois talented tenth. Google that if you are not familiar with Black History.

name: First Congregational United Church of Christ - Portland
reviewSummary:
I attended a performance of Handel’s Messiah at First Congregational United Church of Christ, and the venue itself is genuinely beautiful. The church’s architecture, high ceilings, and historic character create a reverent and visually impressive atmosphere that feels very appropriate for sacred and classical music. The acoustics were strong, allowing the choir and orchestra to be heard clearly throughout the space.

One challenge for me was the seating. The wooden pews are quite hard and became uncomfortable over the course of the performance, especially for extended sitting. I later learned that seat cushions are available if requested, which would likely make a noticeable difference. Unfortunately, I wasn’t aware of this at the start of the concert, and it did impact my overall comfort.

As for the concert itself, the performance was well done and clearly involved a great deal of preparation and talent from the musicians and singers. Many audience members appeared deeply engaged and appreciative of the presentation. Personally, however, Handel’s Messiah just isn’t my particular style of music. While I respect its historical importance and the quality of the performance, I found it difficult to stay fully engaged throughout.

Overall, this is a beautiful and well-maintained venue that would be an excellent setting for those who enjoy classical or choral music. While the concert itself wasn’t quite my preference, the craftsmanship, setting, and professionalism of the performers were evident and appreciated. I had the pleasure of photographing a wedding in this historic church! I love it is a place that welcomes all couples and the staff was just a dream to work with.  I would recommend them for your downtown church wedding! Fun place. The choir was good. I went on a Sunday morning g at 10:30.  The architecture was really rad. Wonderful service! Congregation is well funded as they demolished the school and built the shinny new apartment building in gentrified Portland providing all the  funding for their mission. Very supportive of local Muslim community. Friday Muslim prayer (jummah) offered every Friday at 1:00pm upstairs. Visiting imams rotate to offer different styles and messages in their khutba (sermon). We thank the Church for being generous hosts!

name: First Covenant Church Oakland - Oakland Campus
reviewSummary:
Despite The hours posted on Google, Worship service is held on Sunday at 10am. Wednesday Community Nights are great for all ages. Lots going on all the time for connection and growth in faith in Christ and Community. The website is full of info. I love the authentic people and genuine love for God and People the is expressed, taught and modeled. This is most likely going to be the last feedback I ever give on a church. This church holds a special place in my heart. This is the first REAL church I went to. Just some trivia facts, when he was in High School, Tom Hanks went to church here, I wasn't here at the time.

The high school group at this church had a HUGE impact on my life, what a great High School group it was. I got involved with VBS...Vacation Bible School at this church, and Urban Outreach. A beautiful church building. Gorgeous stained glass windows. The time I spent here was primarily high school-college years.

Thank goodness I found this church, praise God for First Covenant Church. I first went to what was then the "Mission Covenant Church" in Oakland CA when it was down near what is now the Kaiser Auditorium.  At that time, the pastor was Rev. Edwin S. Johnson, a wonderful Christian man.  I believe the Nazarene Church later purchased that building.

Because my father was an immigrant from Sweden, he liked to listen to the church's radio program on Sunday mornings, even though he was NOT a Christian and did not believe in Jesus Christ.

The radio broadcast, came on with the pastor and a lady from the church singing in Swedish the song, "Guds Barns Trygghet".  At that time (in the 1940's), the entire broadcast was in Swedish.

Every year, we would go early Christmas morning to the Julotta service held at 6:00 A.M. at the Mission Covenant Church, even after they built the "new" church at 2100  5th Avenue in Oakland.

I can remember when they had the "Ground Breaking Service" for that new church.  I was about 8 years old (I am 86 now), and I sat on the hill as the service was conducted.

By the time I was a teenager, I met a family who also lived on the island of Alameda, who would drive two miles out of their way to pick me up for Sunday School and church.  Later, a wonderful young man who also lived in Alameda would take me.

We had a wonderful Sunday School teacher, Mrs. Herriott, when I was a teenager.  I loved the Young People's meetings and the activities they provided for Christian youth.  Rev. Harold Erickson was the Pastor of the church at that time.  He was a wonderful Bible teacher, who truly loved the Lord.

My parents sold our home in the Bay area and moved to San Jose, where I married a fine Christian man.  We later moved to Tucson AZ and eventually to Lanesville IN, where I have lived for the past 45 years.

Looking back,  am so thankful for the blessings that were mine during those years of my life.  I trust that you will continue to be a blessing to the young people of this generation also. Pastor Marco is an amazing pastor. I met him several years ago in a youth ministry and now he is growing First Cov at its best. I am honored to know him and call him a friend. They have a very beautiful chapel to relax in for contemplation, and the staff are incredibly warm hearted good people :) 👍🏻❤️

name: First Evangelical Free Church - Colorado Springs Campus
reviewSummary:
I love this church -  my church family.  From the very young to the very old,  we all minister to each other and enjoy lifting each other up in prayer.  What a privilege to be a part of this family.  Love in action happens here.  The truth is preached.  God's word is taught to young and old. We looked for a church in the Springs for about two months, visting 6 congregations. This church feels like home. Pastor Rob is knowledgeable and thoughtful, the sermons were on point and rock solid. Worship was nothing over-the-top, but unlike many loud churches, people actually sang and worshipped along! It was refreshing to hear everyone contributing and participating. It's a great mix of young and old and after the church picnic a week later, it was clear how warm and incredible this group of people is for new believers or those seeking a church. Highly recommended! Come and join us! Great place for family gatherings. They hold Awanas scripture memory classes here that are really fun and educational for kids. Good for weddings and receptions. The are planning to build an even larger facility soon closer to Coronado High School. I have only three requirements for a church I attend.  I found two of the most important at First Evangelical Free church.

1. Jesus must attend on a regular basis!  I felt HIs presence there.  The pastor and his wife and others were so caring of me as a new attendee even through my hospitalization. I also enjoyed the Tuesday evening Bible Study as well.

2. The songs sung should have His Name in them so I will know about Whom we are singing. I could even remember the words and sing them throughout the week.  The music director and his wife were wonderful additions to the worship service.

3. A bell choir! Sadly, it was missing, but even as a confirmed "Ding a Ling", I was able to overlook this one down-fall for the joy of the first two.  Praise His Holy Name!

I didn't join the church because I will be moving to Denver very soon where my son has a new job, but I was all the more impressed when I learned that my daughter-in-law's missionary parents were sponsored by a First Evangelical Free Church for their 18+ years working with the tribes in the jungles of Bolivia.

I am considering making a monthly trip to visit the people I have come to love.  May God continue to bless your ministry to His people. As a child, I grew up in this chruch, was married in this church, barried my father and will do the same for mother in this church.  Our doctrine is biblically solid!!  I have watched GOD working through the people of this church and it is wounderful to see. All our pastors throughout my experience here are men of the word and preach what GOD has instructed them.  Plenty of opportunities to grow and develop a relationship with our living GOD here.  I would envite everyone to join us as we celebrate all GOD is, and what his love is doing in our fallen world.  God  bless you.

name: First Evangelical Lutheran Church - Redlands Campus
reviewSummary: I would not recommend this church, or their future school/daycare to anyone.  The Pastor recently closed down the current school to children and staff in the middle of a school year, with 3 weeks or less notice.  They originally lied, stating "health and safety" reasons due to covid, despite the CDC recommending that kids go back to school because they were safe spaces. Then they let parents and staff in on the real reason, MONEY!  Their next plan is to make it a daycare.  Some of the teachers have worked there for over 20 years and are being let go with 3 weeks notice, no severance, and told they can apply if there are positions available. Its insane that you would have a teacher committed to the community's children for 20+ years and to throw that all away for money. Its heart breaking to watch my child cry about losing the one thing that has been consistent throughout the pandemic.  It's almost impossible to believe a Christian church would treat children, families and staff in this regard. 10/10 would not recommend this church or the new daycare to anyone So sad to have to write this. I attended this church on occasion and sent my children to their preschool but the administrative leaders in the form of the minister of the church and the church’s board are Godless people. As a Christian, I do not write this easily of anyone who seems to be doing God’s work. But, the church’s leaders have been planning for over a year to close the school but did not inform the staff, parents or congregation. Two weeks before they decided to close, when they had done all their planning, they decided to tell everyone. They made up a story that it was due to Covid and then later admitted it was a long time in the planning. The loyal staff were not given adequate time to prepare their families for this loss of income. The loyal parents, parishioners were not even given an audience. When staff and parents asked to speak with leadership they were denied. No true Christian would do this, much less without even offering an audience to the offended parties. Don’t go to this church, don’t send your kids to this school. This church is posing as Christian but is actually run by the Lost and do not seek to live their lives and run their church and businesses the pure Christian way. Would not recommend this church, or their future school/daycare to anyone.  The Pastor and church board is abruptly closing down the current school to children and beloved staff in the middle of a school year, with 3 weeks notice.  They originally blatantly lied and claimed it was due to "health and safety" regarding covid, but after being met with questions and anger, they let parents and staff in on the real reason: money.  They plan to "restructure" to make it a daycare.  AKA charging more and hiring less qualified staff to work for cheaper.  Some of the teachers have worked there for over 20 years and are being let go with 3 weeks notice, and told "they can apply if there are positions available."  Children who have already had so much of their lives disrupted by a pandemic, are being taken out of their routine and away from friends and loving teachers, so that the board has "more time to organize," according to an email sent to parents.  I cannot believe that a church would treat children, families and staff this way, and wonder what experience you could possibly get out of a church who's leaders are so obviously heartless. reviewSummary:
Founded in 1892, Historic First Lutheran is one of the oldest churches in Pasadena. It is also the San Gabriel Valley's oldest Lutheran congregation. The church building itself is over 75 years old and is designated a Pasadena City Landmark.
Through the churches which Historic First Lutheran founded, all other Lutheran Churches in Los Angeles and San Bernardino Counties have been started, making Historic First Lutheran the Mother/Grandmother/Great-Grandmother church of those counties.

The church is an excellent example of Mission Revival style architecture. The Church has obviously taken pride in the building and maintained the exterior appearances intact. The following features of the church are characteristic of the Mission Revival style: stucco walls, gable roofs covered with clay tiles, arcades with segmental arches, corner bell tower, balconets and iron railings on the tower, molded front entry surround, and deeply recessed windows.

Frederick Kennedy, Jr. and David Ogilvie were architects whose designs made significant contributions to the architectural heritage of Pasadena.

Frederick Kennedy designed several other major churches in Pasadena, including the Throop Memorial (300 S. Los Robles), First Baptist (with Carlton M. Winslow at 75 N. Marengo), Trinity Lutheran Church (with Quintin and Kerr at 997 E. Walnut), and Third Church of Christ Scientist (2801 E. Colorado, for which he received a California Honor Award). His commercial buildings include the seven-story Pasadena Furniture Co. Building (with Curlett and Beelman on Colorado Blvd. east of Oakland; now demolished), three auto showrooms in the 300 block of W. Colorado Blvd. (NR), and the Fish Building at 24-28 E. Colorado (NR contributor in Old Pasadena). Institutional projects include two Mayfield School buildings and the American Legion Building on N. Marengo (with Ed Maybury). In addition, his designs for houses in Pasadena were often featured in newspaper articles. His expertise in school buildings led to designs for Santa Paula High School, Baldwin Park High School, Mt. Sac Junior College, and four buildings at the University of La Verne, all designs that received California Honor Awards.

City records identify nearly 15 houses in the Pasadena area designed by David Ogilvie, most of them being large houses in the southern part of the city. His South Pasadena home at 2000 Ashbourne Drive won the second place prize in a national competition for the use of brick in homes. A commercial project of his is located at the northwest corner of Green and Madison (new site of Culinary Arts School) in the NR Playhouse District. His design for the Pasadena Golf Club’s Clubhouse in Altadena received numerous mentions in newspapers in the late 1920s.

The Church is the best local example of Mission Revival design in this property type.

They performed the dedication with efficiency of a military operation. Depending on the year. Orlando will either be 1 or 2 top tourist destination in the world. If you are in need of a religious service on a Sunday, I don't know their operation hours. I would recommend attendance. Beautiful campus, buildings and sound systems. name: First Presbyterian Church
reviewSummary: Am I seriously being asked to review a place of worship?  I don't exactly feel qualified for that.  But any time that I've been there, it seems like a nice welcoming place.  I've even voted there once.  And I believe there's an associated preschool, day care, or something like that.  But it's basically a Presbyterian church near downtown Durham (NC). This is a wedding review - I knew that I wanted to be married in a church, and I spent weeks trying to find one that didn't have ridiculous restrictions and rules. It was a very disappointing process. My own church was meeting in a high school, so that wasn't really an option. For most churches, if they don't have the rule that you have to be a member, they have rules about using their pastors, no photography at all, music restrictions, program restrictions, ridiculous pricing, etc. FINALLY, I found First Presbyterian Church in Durham, NC. This building is absolutely amazing - one of the most beautiful interiors I have ever seen. To make things more awesome, it didn't cost a ridiculous amount of money, and Alissa Miles is their designated wedding coordinator. She loves her job and is AMAZING at it. They did give me a somewhat intimidating rulebook at first, but once I actually talked with Alissa, I realized that they were extremely laid back and really wanted my day to be what I had envisioned. None of their rules got in my way at all. Alissa was there for the rehearsal, and she was there to direct everyone on the day of. There is also a sound coordinator, and he was on top of every detail - microphones, the mp3 for the recessional (which was a secular song - most churches wouldn't have allowed it), and anything else sound-related. I LOVED LOVED LOVED being married in this church. I recommend it to anyone looking for a ceremony venue in the Triangle. So wonderful!! I first started coming to First Pres in 2012 and joined in 2013.  It has been a wonderful faith home.  I love how involved and invested the First Pres family is in the future of downtown Durham.  The church is passionate about social justice and standing with those on the margins.  I'm a member of the young adults group which does a weekly Sunday school, monthly potlucks, and other fellowship and volunteer activities.  All great people!  And great companions as we learn, grow, and live in Christ. Full disclosure - I've been a member at First Pres for many years. At first glance, there are many things to like about it - its history, its downtown location, the interesting and thought-provoking programs, the gorgeous sanctuary (with sound so good it doubles as a music venue) and more. But the real beauty of this church is that everyone is welcome there - and I mean everyone. The only requirement (as I've experienced) is that you be open-minded and welcoming to others as well. It's definitely worth a look. Beautiful church with wonderful people. Big but still very friendly and welcoming to everyone. Their age-related groups are active and add to the experience, but new people have to want to participate to make the most of this fellowship.
