All traditions are beautiful and I respect them, I would have wanted to know what I was in for and have the option to choose a more traditional Catholic Church where the focus is purely on God, our lord and savior Jesus Christ and the gospel. The mass should be labeled English/Samoan mass. Gods bless everyone and always keep your focus on Jesus especially in Church. July 22nd 2023 - My 2nd time Capturing a wedding ceremony here and the Architecture is beautiful outside! Congratulations to Stephanie & Francisco. Nice little church in Downtown Santa Ana. Near the County Civic Center. Mass in English on Holy Days of Obligation at 12.15 pm. Plenty of seats and music and normally a good sermon. Parking is available close to the church. Beautiful church . Priests are helpful in family values and spiritual growth ❤️🙏

name: Saint Jude Melkite Greek Catholic Church - Miami (Downtown/Brickell) Campus
reviewSummary:
Beautiful church that brings me peace walking around! Spend 10 minutes sitting in the garden. It will help brighten your day! Very special church and the area where it is.
This church has a style that it seems like you are visiting a place from the 1930s.
Close to it there cafeterias, a border with the sea, etc.
I recommend it. Enjoy it. Truly shining the unity of the church, a place where latinos, americans and middle easterners can all worship together. In the heart of Miami. Beautiful mosaics and Icons. Rich history. This has always been my favorite Church in the entire Miami Dade County, one of the most beautiful and peaceful churches we have in town.  The Day of St. Jude on October 28 it used to be one of the most beautiful days, the church held the St. Jude Festival, the mass is so powerful, the church gets really crowded and you feel the energy, faith and devotion of the people, and the church chorus is just amazing, it really complements the whole spiritual experience.

There is a gift shop right by the main entrance of the church where you will find ll type of religious items like rosaries, little statues of St. Jude and jewelry, with really good prices.

Parking could be an inconvenience depending on the day and time of the visit as only street parking is available in the area.

When you visit Miami if you are in the Downtown area, Brickell is just a few mins away, so I highly recommend to visit this peaceful church!

Blessings 🙏 Historic beautiful Melkate Catholic Church,ancient rite. The house of the miraculous Saint Jude. 3 masses every Sunday. 9:00 (inglish)11:30(inglish-àrabe)6:00(español)

name: Saint Jude Shrine of the West - San Diego (Downtown) Campus
reviewSummary:
For personal reasons, this parish will always have a special place in my heart, and serves me an occasional visit. I attend Mass at another parish. That said, I deeply lament the fact that they added the vending machines for votive candles inside the church. It's very much irreverent and a lack of respect for the house of God. Vending machines have no place inside a church. While there praying, someone purchased a candle from the machine and the sound it made as the candle was dispensed was super loud. Again, a most disrespectful addition.

We were there recently for the St. Jude festival, and I felt they were pushing the donations hard. One big bin labeled "donations" would have been enough. But they added four bins around the St. Jude statue they bring out for the festival. Almost begging for it. It was a tacky look. View the attached image. I circled all the donation baskets. Between the vending machines and all the donation baskets, it comes off as if this church just cares about finding the most ways to get your money. On my quest to visit every church in San Diego county, I visited Saint Jude's Shrine for Sunday Mass.  4 stars only because there is almost no parking and ss of October 2022, they are still making everyone wear a face mask 😷. ♿ Parking available and access to church as well. Welcoming church. St.Jude in National City is one of the most peaceful, beautiful and incredibly spiritual churches I have ever been to. St. Jude is the parton saint of hopeless cases.....St. Jude is always ♥️ there for me. I’m very disappointed with the office staff at St. Jude’s Church. I was placed on hold for 30 minutes and no one ever came back to the line. Eventually, I had to hang up because no one answered. I never received a call back or any follow-up. This kind of experience makes it really hard to feel supported or welcomed when reaching out for help or information. I hope this can be addressed moving forward. Amazing church, I was fortunate to go to the relic of the St Jude tour.

name: Saint Judes Episcopal Church - Burbank Campus
reviewSummary: Recommend to anyone, who is looking for a solid church. Sincere and transparent! I have no idea what these people are, but they are in no wise Anglican. This is now The Gathering place!

name: Saint Judes Episcopal Church - Glendale Campus
reviewSummary: Recommend to anyone, who is looking for a solid church. Sincere and transparent! I have no idea what these people are, but they are in no wise Anglican. This is now The Gathering place!

name: Saint Justin Martyr Catholic Church - Anaheim Campus
reviewSummary:
It was nice. Reminds me of the 1970’s when growing up with guitar mass and non-judgmental parishioners. Very diverse and also very individualistic- and I’m good with that. It was reverent in a down to earth way. Just normal sinners hanging out with JC wondering if Mercy will come our way. The faith here seems about as real as you can get. Very nice congregation. Super quiet and very nice masses. Priests here are very good with their sermons... Beautiful Church nice service this morning. Lots of folks... One of my Favorite Places to go ol and stay for a very Long period of time🙏🙏🙏🙏♥️♥️♥️♥️♥️. Peacefully, joyful and specially when I  see Priest Sergio and Padre Chispita( Padre Guillermo).
Thanks God🙏🙏🕊🕊 First time visiting was a few years back the day after the mass shooting at the El Paso, TX Walmart.  We were actually driving up to Anaheim the day it took place.  I was able to have a very heartfelt moment with the Priest.  Just visited again today and it was so peaceful with the doors open and the breeze coming through the building.  Prayed and meditated for about 20 minutes.  I’ll visit every time we are back here.  Thank you for being open.

name: Saint Kateri Tekakwitha Catholic Church - Santa Clarita Campus
reviewSummary:
My recent experience at St. Kateri Catholic School was disappointing and left me feeling uncomfortable as a parent.

I was attending while my child was participating in a class and had initially been told that I could wait outside the classroom. After sitting quietly for a few minutes, a staff member approached me and asked that I leave the area and wait upstairs. I politely explained that I prefer not to leave my son alone in a building I am unfamiliar with, especially since another parent was seated nearby waiting as well.

Despite this, I was again asked to move. In an effort to cooperate, I relocated to the area near the school office and even began the fingerprint/background process they require for parents. While sitting there quietly and not interacting with any children or staff, I was approached again and told to go wait upstairs.

At no point was I disruptive or interfering with any activities—I was simply sitting and waiting for my child. The repeated requests to move, despite my cooperation, made the situation feel unnecessary and uncomfortable. Given that another parent was allowed to remain nearby and considering that I was wearing a tank top and have visible tattoos, the interaction unfortunately left me feeling as though I may have been unfairly profiled.

I fully respect the need for safety protocols in schools, but policies should be communicated clearly and applied consistently to all parents. My hope is that the school reviews how these situations are handled so that parents are treated with respect and made to feel welcome while supporting their children. Gabrielle and Cassandra we're very emphatic and contradicting to one another as one staff member told me I can sit in a certain area and wait they would come in and say I could not, a different staff member invited me in to sit in the classroom they came in and collected me and removed me very unwelcoming I've never felt so targeted based on my appearance especially at a church. St. Kateri Tekakwitha Catholic Church is such a beautiful and welcoming parish. From the moment you walk in, you can feel the warmth and kindness of the community. The church itself is stunning — with high ceilings, glass windows instead of walls, and plenty of natural light that fills the space with peace and harmony.

The priests are incredibly caring and always make time to support anyone who needs guidance or comfort. There are also so many wonderful ministries for both adults and children. One of our family’s favorite parts of the year is Vacation Bible School — my kids look forward to it all year long!

There are several Mass options throughout the week, making it easy for everyone to attend, and the Sunday 10:30 a.m. Children’s Mass is especially uplifting. Parking can get busy, but arriving a little early helps a lot.

Overall, St. Kateri is more than just a church — it’s a community filled with faith, love, and light. We feel so blessed to call it our parish home. 🙏💛 I loved attending masses in this church. The parish office however, in my opinion, needs improvement.  It will be so much better if the front desk people there would be more conscious of the fact that they work in a church office, not just any ordinary office.  Some parishioners go there because they just lost a loved one and would want to ask for prayers and mass intentions.  We understand that the schedule can be really packed since "we have over 5000 parishioners" but it will be really great if the office is staffed by compassionate people who are truly willing to help. I was visiting the area last Sunday and stopped in for mass. The church campus was beautiful and people were very nice! After church the priest told us about Saint Kateri, the first Native American saint. It was a wonderful experience. I would definitely go back! Saint Kateri Tekakwitha is a beautiful modern church in the north part of Santa Clarita off Copper Hill. Lots of parking and easy entry and exit. The church is spacious and the 5.30 pm Sunday mass was perfect with ample seating and enjoyable music. Deacon provided a captivating and relatable homily and the mass flowed nicely. Enjoyable visit to attend Sunday mass.

name: Saint Kilian Church - Mission Viejo Campus
reviewSummary:
A beautiful church and a good Catholic community. The priests, Fr. Angelos & Fr. Tuan, are very good and are helpful bringing those who worship here enrichment in their faith. I recently called for a friend who wanted a hot meal,,, The guy that answered was really stern and kind of rude,,, This is not a place you can get warm food so do not call them... Thank you anyway This is a beautiful Church. The services for saying farewell to our loved one were carried out  professionally. We had lunch on site in the facilities the offer. A nice large room that held our entire party. They had a screen to play our video they took care of tables, coverings, chairs our caterer. It was a very good experience during a very hard time in our lives. Beautiful church Through Sunday, breakfasts are amazing and going to miss father, Scott, we love you, we miss you and to your journey to Notre Dame, my friend, we all love you blessings. I love the happy go lucky friendly atmosphere that both priests bring to the community. They're one of the big reasons why I decided to stick to this church. Thanks to them and all those involved with the RCIA program, restoring my faith (journey) has been smoother then expect it.

I recommend this church for all that all looking to restore their faith, build relationships, as well as seeking a loving community. I thank the Saint Kilian Church for being open-minded, understanding, and patient with me.

God Bless all!

name: Saint Mark's Church
reviewSummary:
This beautiful, historic Episcopal church is an exemplar of the Gothic Revival style. Built between 1847-1848, the original design is attributed to English architect Richard Cromwell. The church maintains gardens, most noteworthy for its roses. The congregation is committed to serving the poor and needy. This is a stunning church. I'm glad to have discovered this church in the COVID age of streaming Masses when I was looking for a new church. I get a very warm and welcoming feeling from the clergy, and the sermons have been an inspiration during these dark days. "For although they knew God, they neither glorified him as God nor gave thanks to him".

With a heavy heart I say that this is not a God fearing church. I went to the Handel's Messiah Sing along. The choir director gave a small speech at the beginning, saying that we are gathered here because of a love of music. Not once did he mention God. Christians sing to give glory to God, not to ourselves. To say that our songs of praises are for ourselves and not for the glory of God is heretical. I pray that God warms their hearts to Him that they might turn to the Lord and receive mercy. An exceptional place to worship.  It is beautiful; beyond that it is welcoming. On any given day one is likely to find some of the most affluent and some of the poorest residents of Philadelphia in the same space. The clergy knows everyone. All are welcome.

name: Saint Mark's Episcopal Church - Van Nuys Campus
reviewSummary:
I visited St. Mark's on October 23. It was my home church from 1953 to 1970, and it was wonderful to be back. Of all the churches I've visited as a guest over the years. St. Mark's was easily the most welcoming, with a sincere warmth from all the people, without being overbearing and with no sense of falsity or just "surface politeness". The priest was accessible without stepping away from leadership. His sermon was memorable and to the point. The Mass was truly worshipful without being too stiff. There was a simple and deep genuineness in every part of my time there. Very unwelcoming church. Lady who claimed to be in charge 'Robin' and her office secretary/chihuahua are very rude. Office is usually always closed and 'Robin' trained the chihuahua to not give ANY information regarding the church. Its almost like they're hiding some kind of fraud or embezzlement. I do not recommend this place. This is an Episcopalian Church in the Diocese of Los Angeles; the current times for their Masses & Misa is on their website!

Everyone is welcome, their is Bus Service, however, it's tricky, but worth the hassle of the amount of time, it takes to visit Padre Vince &
no pricy auto rental for the out of Towner to worry about! & theirs UBER Cab as well!

I've  enjoy coming here; Padre Vince being the only friends in town; it's worth the Invesment.

Warm Hospitality;
Gracias mi Amingos Everyone is welcome here, and services are held in various languages.. the Luganda service happens every Sunday.. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

name: Saint Marks Mission Church - San Marcos Campus
reviewSummary: It would seem that the church now is indoors obviating the need for folding chairs for outdoor mass or services. The drive there is most scenic. The actual mission Church itself is very basic, but there is a definite feel of community here. The congregation is small since the actual physical building is relatively small. They are so kind and generous here. I took a friend that could use some help and they hooked him right up. Food stamps, medi-cal was applied for there, how convenient. Plus he got a huge box of fresh food and he needed it too! You can go back once a month for a box of free food. Also there is a thrift shop where nice clothes can be had for cheap Go there for the 10:30am mass in English. Mass in Spanish is at 1 pm. Very small but comfortable. Make sure to bring a chair, since most masses are outside. A small Roman Catholic Church where everyone is very friendly. Great alternative to a bigger Church. Friendly place to attend mass.  Visiting priest, Fr. Moses, is excellent.  Lits of parking and not crowded.  Very good location.

name: Saint Martin De Porres Church - Chino Hills Campus
reviewSummary:
Well had both my children baptized here in 1992 n 98 I do want to let it be know that when I was going through my divorce which was in 1993..I called the church to seek counseling n was told by the office receptionist very rudely that there was no place here since I was getting divorced...not only was she cold n quite mean..it really turned me off from being a catholic I didnt return back to saint Martin til 25 years later.Instead went to Calvary Christian churches where I was welcomed with open arms...but came back to Saint Martin due to growing up being a catholic and Italian It just felt right coming back.. I ATTEND pretty regularly however I do want to say some of the parishioners volunteering on Sundays are not only unfriendly if you are an attractive woman..but they barely smile its the most unbelievable thing I have ever seen in any church..I dont let that stop me from attending but I find it annoying to be met with such unfriendly faces when u greet them or smile..I just see that as people who are unhappy inside n really dont have the lord in their hearts ..and outwardly that shows.I suggest you visit n see how you feel yourself.
God bless🙏I do want to say the church is quite beautiful  and peaceful..other than my thoughts regarding the unfriendly few..most parishioners are friendly.The priest are friendly and mass is never boring because they have a sense of humor ...which I appreciate. Gorgeous place, with 24/7 Adoration!🙏🏻 please take a moment of your busy day to get some peace in His Presence, totally worth it!🙏🏻❤️ Choose another place of worship. This church does not welcome diversity and are hypocritical. They recently decided to host a Super Bowl watch party only to choose to watch the “All American half time show” but they have the nerve to host a yearly carnival where they sell food from various Non-American cultures. So which is it? You want vendors to donate Mexican food for your church so you can raise money but you don’t want to celebrate their culture when given the chance? Really beautiful church with great and strong Catholic community and young families. The community of service.  They're wonderful at making you feel welcome.  We love the 10:30am mass.  We learned to get there around 10:15am to not stress over parking.  We also learn to sit closer to the very front.  We can be so open to pray and have our 3 year old daughter see how we can participate in mass.  We are encouraged to confess and repent, and stay away from sin. The Lord hears the cry of the poor.

name: Saint Martin Lutheran Church (NALC) - Atlanta Campus
reviewSummary: Saint Martin Lutheran Church on Piedmont between Midtown and Buckhead in Atlanta is ideal for all those seeking to grow in their Christian faith maturity. Saint Martin Lutheran Church is truly a blessing.  In this day and time, when so many Churches are making a mockery of Holy Scripture, it is  both refreshing and renewing to have a Church still faithful to the Word. Here you will find a traditional, liturgical worship setting and you will leave Church with a sense of peace and well-being. Come visit us, you just may find your new Church home! Jack Kimmich I am happy to be a member of Saint Martin. We are a traditional, liturgical church that preaches the Gospel. It is a joy to attend the church service, and then join in the fellowship afterwards. Saint Martin is a welcoming community of traditional, liturgical Lutherans living out Christ's commandment to make disciples in his name.  The Gospel, and only the Gospel, is preached from the Saint Martin pulpit. What an amazing Church that teaches the scriptures!  It is warm and welcoming to everyone.  Come check it out for yourself on Sunday at 10:30 a.m.  Great coffee, food and fellowship after every service.

name: Saint Mary Catholic Church - Anaheim Campus
reviewSummary:
A great community church.
5 masses on Sundays accommodating both English and Spanish languages. Family and community church. Had our family Services here also. Very busy church so timing is important. Go early to find parking always or expect to stand up in the back. Finally Made a commitment to attend church since I haven't been for years and decided it was time to go and pray with God in my heart and spirit and reconnect with the church as I  was raised and went to school as a child especially by my mother who constantly urges me to stay wth God . That's amazing and beautiful Church I am loved it God bless My boss was on his dead bed and there was no one priest available to assist him. I try to arrange a Annoitement of the oil & no one answered, this was going on for 5 months. He eventually pass without the Holy Rite.
Chock of Cultural Backgrounds.
Nice stuff personal.
Lovable icon made by a Spanish Missionary Priest. Iconic backgrounds for any occasion.
I miss the Mass on line.
Please bring the back.
Love & +Peace!

name: Saint Mary's by the Sea Church - Huntington Beach Campus
reviewSummary: The best kept secret of Huntington Beach as far as Catholic Church's go. Please take time to appreciate their gorgeous altar reredos done by Granda Liturgical Arts ❤️👑🙏🏼 St. Mary's by the sea is a beautiful Roman Catholic Church to visit. There are several Masses to choose from on the weekend including the Latin High Mass at noon. They have Daily Mass with the Holy Rosary starting at 7:25 a.m. and the Divine Mercy Chaplet recited after daily mass. Fr. Chu and the local parishioners have done a great job keeping the devotions and prayer groups going including the Miraculous Medal Novena on Wednesday mornings and Adoration on Thursdays. Check online Bulletin for more details. A Holy Church to feel close to God. Receive graces and spiritual nourishment for mind, body and souls! Beautiful seaside church. Reminiscent of old sea town church. Very quaint and service great Beautiful and friendly little church. But I walked a long way from my hotel for the Latin Mass, only to find I had arrived on the first Sunday of its extinction. The priest told us to be grateful to God for the service being in English, which added insult to injury a long way from home. If the Faith hates the Faith, what is left? We visit this church some Sundays at noon to attend their Latin mass. If you have never attended a Latin mass, you must come to this one. The Father and the Altar boys are absolutely phenomenal.  It is a beautiful mass. One of the best masses I've ever seen. Soooo reverend. It fills your heart of joy.

name: Saint Matthew Ecumenical Catholic Church - Brea Campus
reviewSummary: Church advertised they would provide Ash services on Ash Wednesday from 1-6pm. Many at 4:30 were outside wandering with no clue and doors locked. I had called and the woman on the phone said they had closed at 5 (it wasn’t even 5 yet). She stated they closed it since no one had been coming to stop by. Many people showed up after 4 due to getting off of work and were left confused and saddened that they couldn’t recieve this reminder of mortality as they prepare their hearts for Easter. The Spirit of the Lord moves within St. Matthew's church. The community is very loving and welcoming to all! This is one place to come and feel great. You can feel the warmth as the people there greets you. Welcomes you like a family. Padre Arturo is an amazing leader. We couldn't be at a better place to teach our girls to love God and follow their lifes on the way to Gods. Saint Matthew Ecumenical "Catholic" Church is not really Catholic, they are not in communion with the Bishop of Orange or with the Pope and other bishops of the Catholic Church.  There are several friendly and welcoming Catholic Churches in the area (i.e. Saint Angela Merici, Our Lady of Guadalupe, Saint Mary's, Saint Martin de Porres, Saint Denis, etc) please do not go here thinking this is a Catholic Church even though some of the trappings and prayers are taken from the Catholic Church.  I pray that those running and attending this Church will come home to the One Holy Catholic and Apostolic Church founded by our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ that we may be one in Him and His Church as He commanded not separated by following our own ways instead of His.  Thanks be to God always This place is unlike any other church I have ever been to and that's a GOOD thing. The nicest, most genuine people you will ever meet. Zero judgement, casual attire and everyone is welcome.  I had been turned off by churches due to the hypocrites and fakes. This church is the exact opposite and I am beyond grateful to have found it. Seriously, check it out, you will be very happy you did.

name: Saint Nicholas Catholic Church - Irvine Campus
reviewSummary: I’m here from Salt Lake City for daily mass this week. I’ve enjoyed my “refocus “ on Jesus time here. It is a clean big spacious church in Laguna Woods, California! Check it out and don’t forget Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament chapel! St Nicholas is a beautiful church is there many times with my father and just recently for his funeral My niece is getting married this Saturday in Texas and she needed a form filled out and signed by me in presence of a deacon, priest. Jayne and Father Leo were the most kindest and caring people I ever thought I’d come across. I can’t describe how helpful, patient, diligent they were in getting this form out to my niece’s deacon in Texas. May GOD shower them with an abundance of blessings. I can’t thank them both enough for making it so easy for me to provide my niece with what she needs for her upcoming wedding. Very nice and beautiful church! Recently remodel to the altar and look pretty good and my cousin is a priest at this church! A wonderful church thanks to the loving shepherds(all the pastors) , the joyous and friendly congregation and one of the best choirs you will ever hear! Join us for the beautiful mass celebrations.

name: Saint Oscar Romero Catholic Community, Inc. - Ontario Campus
reviewSummary: I love our church!  Everyone is friendly, the priest is wonderful, and it's fun watching it grow.  The grounds around the church office are looking better and more beautiful all the time.  Everyone involved cares so much about our parish and wants to bring everyone and their families closer and closer to God. Have been part of this church for the past 3 years. Father Pat is very approachable and caring.  He makes mass personal and relevant.  I love the warmth that our church community has.  Even though our church takes place at a school it is so much more than an actual church building.  Father Pat has led us into becoming our own church which is so much more than just a building.   Can't wait to see how much more our church family grows. Priest is the ideal modern priest with still traditional Catholicism, he is a joy to listen too and laugh with. Not to mention the Amazing acoustic musician that plays great music ( John metering) relaxing and great atmosphere. Love to be in a church that I truely enjoy listening to the gospel ( it is so relevant to today World), he touches your hearts and you’ll never catch yourself falling asleep. Love it Father Pat is an awesome priest. No matter who the priest here is though, we are here to praise God and receive communion because "whoever eats my body and drinks my blood has life in them". The only reason I rated it a 4 stars , is that the church is being built. Currently, the Catholic community in this area is attending mass at a school on Harrison Ave. The wait for the new church is taking too long.

name: Saint Patrick Catholic Parish - San Diego (Downtown) Campus
reviewSummary:
On my pilgrimage to visit every Catholic Church in San Diego County, I found myself immersed in the beauty and history of this Church. As the seventh church built in San Diego (1921) and at one time considered to be San Diego’s cathedral, it exudes a special kind of grandeur. The Mass was truly inspiring, and the warm spirit of the parish added to the overall experience. Stepping into Saint Patrick Catholic Parish, I was instantly captivated by its old-world charm. The welcoming community made me feel connected to the rich history within these walls. A must-visit for any church explorer! A blessing for many learned who love all peoples and and a safe comforting home in which to pray to our Creator. The homily was to point and educational advice. The location wonderful, the attendees open armed in welcoming everyone, trying to get us all to be able to get to Eternity Beautiful church. Lot of beautiful stained glass. I love old architecture and this church is just the perfect kind; it's been around for just over a century. Mass was excellent, so far each priest there has shared some gem homilies. This is my new home parish. Worth it!  Yes, it is worth the time and effort to attend 8am daily Mass!  People smile at you!  They are kind and reverent!  Priests give clear, concise, and sobering homilies!  Shout out to Father Carlos and Father Phil!

Also, there is daily Rosary after daily Mass.

I feel joyful when great traditions of the Catholic Church continue.  So good for the soul!

name: Saint Paul Church of Sacramento - Sacramento Campus
reviewSummary: For those of us considering living nearby, does this church have a bell that goes off hourly or regularly? This is a quality of life issue and a prompt response would be appreciated. Thank you. I'll remove this after receiving a response but you should consider just putting that information somewhere people can see it. Some Sacramento churches are really oblivious to the fact that some people like to have peace in their home. Came for a funeral.  The service was beautiful and well organized.  The screens and sound system made a difference.  Very spacious seating. Sororities are welcome here. But do sororities pledge to greek god's and goddesses?  4th Sunday all 9 sororities were acknowledged.  Walked in, and walked out. Very sad to see Pastor Reece is caring on Dr. Ephraim Williams and his visions!  We are Blessed !!🙏🏽❣️❣️❣️ I reached out to the church for the first time about a sensitive issue and spoke with Sister Felicia. The tone and response I received was insensitive and left me very uncomfortable. This one star is strictly for her. I was hesitant to leave a review but I think the church needs to know.

name: Saint Paul the Apostle Catholic Community - Westwood Campus
reviewSummary: I basically grew up in this church and I am very thankful and fortunate for the Paul's fathers and the Catholic community ! I have very fun childhood memories my family has been associated with this church for a very long time we think the Paul's fathers for their thoughts and the prayers for their help and assistance over the years ! Please keep Phil Duncan your thoughts and your prayers especially during the holiday season I myself and my husband and our four dogs lost or one bedroom apartment from a fire in North Hollywood almost 3 months ago and we are just trying to get our lives back together it's been a financial emotional time for us thank you and God bless It’s Parish Hall for meetings & gatherings and faith development & faith formation programs are held here. It's ok.   Good parking. Father Gil Martinez needs to refrain from making political statements. Please stick to the Gospel, which transcends earthly politics.

name: Saint Paul the Apostle Church - Westwood Campus
reviewSummary: I never ever going to this church anymore. Today first time i saw you guys closed for private event and not letting the other people to come inside … this is bazaar i never ever seen this type of racism before and im going to let all my community to not show up their .. because of end of the day this is God place everyone can able to get in their. And u guys put security to not let people come in . I gave so much money in this church and i will make sure to tell everyone else who racism activist you guys are doing. Shame all of you… A very simple church yet the beauty of it takes your breath away.  When you walk in you can feel the presence there.  Very easy to get to and an amazing Priest who gave the service.  Made it very deep, yet light!! How ironic the ICU nurse recommended St. Paul's where I attended elementary school!   I was flooded with memories and realized my faith and tendency to chat with Creator started there in front of the statue of St. Joseph and the Virgen de Guadalupe.  🕊⛪😇 I was there for my mother's funeral and for Easter Mass and found it very comforting and welcoming. A place  of worship . Services are held at rhe parish hall while the church is undergoing renovation. We're visiting  & attending Mass  offer my son Jacob birthday 13yrs old. We're from Oakland  The Cathedral  of Christ the light

name: Saint Paul's Church - Augusta Campus
reviewSummary:
We've been coming here on and off again for a little while, and now with living closer have the privilege of attending regularly. It's a great church that is very welcoming to all, with traditions rooted in scripture, sermons that support and encourage faith, and activities that allow all church members to find a place.

They regularly do outreach that involves and helps out the community. I also can't forget to mention that the location is great, and the church itself is beautiful. I love the stained glass windows, and their 11am has a choir and organ that are both phenomenal!

Their hand out includes information on their weekly / monthly activities, and instructions on everything, so whether you're new to the church or not, you don't have to worry about not knowing what to do. Beautiful venue. Has outside area overlooking the river. Lovely looking church in a nice area. Never been inside. From the first day our family went to this church, it was warm, welcoming and accepting. We wanted to find a place where our son and his husband would be comfortable and St Paul's is the perfect place.

It's more than just a place to go to church. We love the music and the choir and it has a joyous feeling about it always. If you haven't been to St Paul's recently you really need to give it a try. We have two great reverends, Eric and Kimberly. And there are plenty of opportunities to get involved in the community and do some good works. You can help out anywhere from arranging flowers, to helping provide food to those in need, or even helping to welcome all the Iron Man participants that join us every year for a pasta dinner before the race.

Please consider joining us one Sunday and I promise you won't be disappointed. What a wonderful place this is really what I was doing was going for a run though. It has a beautiful graveyard it is old and well taken care of, many receptions that I've been there have been beautiful

name: Saint Paul's Lutheran Church - Irvine Campus
reviewSummary:
I have been a member of St Paul’s Irvine since I was baptized in 2002. Now being a young adult I have grown to love and cherish the Divine Service with its Liturgy and hymns. This church also provides wonderful teaching and preaching from Pastor Espinosa or Pastor Mueller. Come and visit on Sunday 9:30 am or early evening at 4 pm to receive the gifts that God has given to us in His Word and Sacraments. Also come on Wednesdays at 7 pm for a brief Service of the Word. The pastor is incredibly knowledgeable, sharing deep insights into the Bible and faith with wisdom and clarity. When I first arrived, I struggled with the language barrier, but despite that, I could deeply feel the power and mercy of God. His presence was undeniable, guiding me toward understanding and peace. Moved by His grace, I decided to be baptized. This church has become a place of spiritual growth, love, and faith for me, and I am forever grateful for the journey it has led me on. Extremely friendly. Serves communion both the common cup or the chalice.
If you’ll be kind enough to sign in, you’ll have a sticker with your name on it. When Pastor offers you the bread/body of Christ he will usually say your name it’s very personal. Great service & sermons that are biblical sound, friendly people and beautiful stain glass sanctuary!

name: Saint Peter Lutheran Church - Greenwood Village Campus
reviewSummary:
Our First Time to attend St Peter this Sunday. We googled to get an earlier church time close to home.
My husband is a Viking football  fan and this is game day.
So..off we went to worship and we sure got the 5 star morning.
The friendly energy was evident immediately.
Lots of smiles and greetings. We were gifted in participating in a
Traditional Service with Fine musicians and an amazing soloist.
When the congregation shared the peace, we noticed it was  most the  church members going all around.
Will Be Back.. Amen ! Never have I walked into a church and felt so welcomed as a newcomer. Pastor Dave and the St. Peter congregation have an awesome way of making you feel right at home. Since visiting that day a few years ago, my family and I have become members and Pastor Dave baptized our son. We're so happy to have found a church home to raise our little guy in, and we know it will be a wonderful and supportive community for our family for many, many years to come. The first time we walked in the front door at St. Peter Lutheran Church was a Sunday more than 25 years ago.  Valerie and I were looking for a new church then, and it has been a blessing ever since.  The people, the pastor, and the events have all be a major part of our lives since, and will be forever I’m sure.  What a pleasure it is to sit next to people every Sunday who care about what’s going on in my life just like I care about what’s going on in their lives, good or not so good.
Pastor Dave has been a wonderful pastor.  His sermons are memorable, to the point, and totally non-political.  Kids of all ages are always involved when possible and practical.  He oversees the activities of the church with close attention and points people in the right direction when necessary.  I can say from experience that he is there when you need him to be.
In addition to being on Church Council, teaching High School Sunday School, overseeing the Property Committee and being on numerous committees over the years, we have enjoyed the activities connected with the major holidays (Easter, Christmas, etc.).  Again, when you are working with people you care about, it makes a big difference.  Some of our friends at St. Peter we have known since we started going there.  In fact, some we have known before we started going there.  These people aren’t just friends, they are “family”.  What a blessing it is to sit next to friends/family every week who believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God and that everyone in the room is praying the same way you are and is there for the same reason you are…to develop their relationship with God. I've been a member of Saint Peter for my entire adult life. It's an extension of our family and is so welcoming (really!). The music is top-notch, the children's sermons and programs give my kids a sense of community and confidence that God loves them, the discussions are open and engaging, and the sermons make you think. Come check it out this Sunday! We have been going to Saint Peter for a few years and absolutely love it.  The people are super friendly and welcoming without being in your face about it.  The Sunday morning worship is always meaningful with wonderful music.  Pastor Dave does a great job of tying the weekly lessons into what is going on in the world.  He provides an opportunity to think about what it means to be people of faith and what God is calling us to do.  The Wednesday brown bag Bible Study is a great place to continue the conversation.  There are lots of activities for all ages, especially for the kids.

name: Saint Polycarp Catholic Church - Anaheim Campus
reviewSummary:
This Sunday's Mass was the best. Our parishoner Mr. Ramiro Lopez was introduced as our new Deacon. He has been a wonderful force in our church for decades. We are very proud of him. There is English mass at 6:30 daily, during holy Friday, they did a beautiful altar for the blessed sacrament.  Lovely. Attended a funeral mass on 2-13-23
It's a nice church. What a lovely church, inspiring music & homily, friendly people. Will return soon ❤️‍🔥 Loved it here! The band had very top tier performances. You could tell they put a lot of effort into the music, and they have a cute pianist

name: Saint Polycarp Catholic Church - Stanton Campus
reviewSummary:

name: Saint Stephen Lutheran Church - Long Beach Campus
Saint Therese Roman Catholic Church - Pasadena Campus
reviewSummary:
Very respectful
Clean
Organized
Original mass in latin
Not crowded
I recommend to come to mass at 1pm in latin every sunday St. Therese Church is a very lovely and spiritual community. The prist are very holy all of them, they always are helping people and you can feel very welcome here. I feel very blessed to be in this church. If you want or need the presence of God,come to St. Therese church.
They also have the perpetual adoration chapel 24 hours open. Exc church. Im a 15 year christian and besides catholics  praying to saints and as christians we all pray to GOD AND HIS ONLY SON JC...  but when i cant make it to my church i do the evening mass and its great.  Peace be with you. Traditional Latin Mass offered at 1pm Sundays. Beautiful, reverent. Priest comes from Saint Michael's Abbey. Also, Red missals provided, and women veil. Bring everyone! I feel at home here, like family. It's a beautiful, spacious church.  Everyone is very friendly.  I mean everyone.  From the clergy to the office staff, even the congregation. There is a chapel that you can visit any time of the day with a key card that can be purchased for $20.00.  Confession is held three times a week and mass is offered throughout the day on Sundays.

name: Saint Thomas Korean Catholic Center - Anaheim Campus
reviewSummary:
A vibrant and welcoming Korean community. I enjoyed Father Dominic Chai’s first mass on June 15. What a delight! This is the largest Korean Catholic Church in Southern California when considering the capacity of parishioners it can accommodate within its premises. They underwent renovations after my departure from California in 2000. Whenever I am in Orange County to visit family, I make it a point to attend Mass at this church. The church is splendid, roomy, and invokes a sense of devotion when praying before the tabernacle. The cantor's melodic voice adds to the reverent atmosphere during the Mass. Despite the circumstances in society, relationships among people, and church leadership, I believe it's crucial for us to continue attending church to worship the Lord. This practice fuels our spiritual growth, provides meaning to life, and paves the way for salvation, for Jesus is the way, the truth, and the life. Going there to participate in Table Tennis with other adults and take private 1/2 hour coaching lessons with a competent excellent and patient English/ German speaking coach used by many of the Korean players. The seats of the sanctuary are removed and tables take their place.  So ceilings are very high, the lighting is great and the room is air conditioned.

Play times are Tuesday 1pm-5pm and Sunday 2pm-6 pm. In addition, I pay an annual facility fee of $100. I do not know if lessons can be taken without paying the additional fee. But feel practice/play time is important. And the coach can also observe my technique between intervals of his coaching other players. Those things are important for me to speed along my progress. There is a ping-pong robot  and two other free to use tables each with a basket full of practice balls. Best korean Catholic church in U.S. Cinvenient access from I5 and 91 fway and parking lot is spacious. Provide a variety of programs for all generations year round. July 4th Bbq party and October Fest are real fun I am not too comfortable with fancy indoor decorations in catholic centers. But I still see some places to upgrade a bit... still not so comfortable 😕..

name: Saint Thomas More Catholic Church - Irvine Campus
reviewSummary:
I stopped attending after they kept asking for money to finish building the rest of the church EVERY MASS!! When this campaign first began, it was $4 million. Mind you, the land is already pitched, plumbing, electrical, septic, and ground prep have already been run to the spot. So it's pretty absurd. Well, not as absurd as them upping it within a couple years to $8 million. I didn't go for a while because I felt this was an underhanded money grab. But I went to a holiday service where they had grossly grown their pitch to $13 million!! Who the hell needs a $13 million chapel? Does the church know how many people that would feed? Does it care? Nope. It DOES care about the looks of the place and keeping up with modern non-denominational churches. Its a total waste of resources and screams of corruption from the inside. This parish is very different than many I’ve attended or called home. It’s large and modern, and has that feel.

The people are very welcoming, and the priests, including Fr Joe, are excellent.

The outside patio area is really nice, as is the walkway through the parking lot. As you walk you will fine signs that tell you various things about Saint Thomas More.

It’s a peaceful place to be. Recently moved to Tustin Ranch and I discovered this church. It is a real blessing. I love it and feel happy when I visit it STM hosts abundant opportunities for parishoner involvement, including Bible studies and a wonderful young adult community! We’re so blessed to have a beautiful church and clergy especially Father Eugene and Fr Thomas who are very compassionate about the church! We are also thankful for the many hard working ministries available to participate . Looking forward to the new building and development of St Thomas More which is so needed!

name: Saint Thomas of Canterbury E​piscopal Church​ & School - Temecula Campus
reviewSummary: I witnessed two ladies, one in a military uniform, yell at a woman who was trying to park in a handicapped spot. A little boy looking like 3 years old was running in front of the lady's black truck. The lady asked if they can get their little boy and the two black ladies went off on the lady in the truck. Calling the lady names. Another woman who claimed to work in the preschool began defending the lafies. How is a stranger More concerned for a toddler than the mother???  Very sad.  Unsurprising actually. This is our episcopal church that we have been going to since the covid-19 epidemic. It is small but the atmosphere is very welcoming. Everyone is very down to earth. The church service on Sunday is unassuming and the choir is very nice. It will be worthwhile for someone who is searching for spiritual needs. Great newer facility; new vicar due in a couple of weeks. Great congregation. Bless this wonderful, welcoming church, the main Episcopal church in the Temecula Valley! Excellent place of worship. Welcoming and easy to get involved.

name: Saint Timothy Church - Laguna Niguel Campus
reviewSummary:
I’ve had the pleasure of photographing two weddings at this beautiful church, and each experience has been wonderful. The architecture and natural light provide a stunning backdrop for capturing meaningful moments, and the peaceful atmosphere really adds to the reverence of the day.
The staff and clergy have always been welcoming, organized, and respectful—not just to the couples and guests, but also to vendors like myself. Their professionalism and kindness help everything flow smoothly, allowing everyone to focus on the celebration. Saint Timothy's Catholic Church seems to be a great spiritual home. From the moment you arrive on the beautiful, peaceful grounds, there's a sense of peace and welcome that's truly special.

The church itself is architecturally beautiful with its modern yet reverent design. The worship space feels both intimate and grand at the same time, with excellent acoustics that enhance both the music ministry and the priests' homilies.

There was an Asian priest when I attended that delivered a thoughtful, humorous , relevant homily that connected scripture to daily life in ways that stay with people. It struck that perfect balance of being spiritually nourishing without being overly lengthy or preachy.

What really seems to set Saint Timothy's shine is its vibrant community. The parishioners are genuinely welcoming to newcomers.

Whether you're looking for a new parish home or just visiting the area, Saint Timothy's welcomes all with open arms. The 8:30 AM Morning Mass was especially vibrant. They also offer convenient confession times and adoration hours for those seeking those sacraments.

Saint Timothy's truly embodies what a parish community should be - a place of worship, growth, service, and connection. I'm sorry been a while since I went to a mass. This was granddaughter's first Communion. Very nice. They did not have big screen TVs in my previous churches haha. I guess that's the new way The love for the Lord Jesus is infecting and contagious. Be on time and attend for it will be uplifting and your worthwhile precious time will thank you for it! 1st time on St. Timothy church during Easter Sunday mass & very festive celebration.

name: Saint Vincent de Paul Rectory - Petaluma Campus
reviewSummary: I stopped during my day visit to Pentaluma. I was surprised it was open and felt so welcoming to everyone. I lit a candle for my loved ones and had time to sit and pray in peace. I appreciate the time I was able to share with God in this of holiest of places. I attended midnight mass at this church many years ago. My wife and I returned for a Saturday Mass yesterday. I am much older and only here because the Lord has chosen to allow me to stay after some serious health issues. You are closer to God here. The Church is overwhelming beautiful. My goal now is not to let the Lord down, and to make a difference with the time I have left. It's an amazing Church! I had have a great time for Christmas there!! Merry Christmas to everyone ❤️ God bless 🙌 🙏 us!! Beautiful and great Catholic Church!  Beautiful sounding music!  The priest had a great homily!  Without doubt worth going to!  Know Our Savior Jesus loves you!  Know Our Father and Creator God loves you!  And have a great day!❤️✝️⚓️🙏😃 I did my confirmation here, many many many years ago, really beautiful church, thanks God for letting us have this nice place.

name: Saints Community Church - Metairie Campus
reviewSummary: This church has been nothing but welcoming from the very beginning. The love, kindness, and genuine sense of community here have made such a difference in my life. Every time I walk through the doors, it truly feels like coming home. I'm so grateful to be part of a church family where everyone is welcomed with open arms. Saints Community has been my home since 2020. I was very all over the place and they were so patient over the years as I asked hard questions, volunteered on different teams until i found what was right, and took a while to decide on if this was my home. I have no regrets, and love so much about this place. It’s small enough to feel like family but big enough to make new connections and not feel clique-y. The messages are phenomenal, and Pastor Wayne, Kristi, Daniel and all the rest of the staff have such servants hearts. There are thriving small groups for all ages,  kids programs, a growing youth, and growing young adults programming. Check it out if you can, 9am or 11am service! my first time attending i was 14 for a baptism & then i attended again at 16. i started to attend regularly at 18 years old. I am now 21 years old and can truly say i love this church. i am a young adult just trying to serve the Lord & i have grown so much spiritually over the few years because of the family i became apart of. my spirit is always fed throughout every service. i have served on multiple teams and can truly say that this church has became a home for me. i love the people, i love the messages, i love the growth opportunities & the discipleship that comes with being apart of this community. This church makes you feel like family. You create a bond with the church family and the music just captivates you into worship. They have everyone of all ages and you’ll fall in love with SCC Great atmosphere great place to worship friendly people I highly recommend it

name: Saints Felicitas & Perpetua Church - Pasadena Campus
reviewSummary: We attended a funeral mass for a friend and it was very solemn.  Fr. John, the pastor gave a very nice homily/eulogy. The cantor was great and it made the celebration of life very solemn & meaningful. Only issue is parking when you have about 300-400 people attending. The walk to a residential parking spot will cover your daily exercise. Good school and great church.  It's a peaceful sanctuary and they have a really fun fair in the Spring. They're in a beautiful neighborhood in San Marino and the parking there is terrific and Fr. Paul is an amazing, inspirational priest. Went in to St Felicitas Catholic Church. In San Marino. Stopped in with an elder friend I work for. We went to light a candle and say a few prayers for all this confusing  days and times.  She, however is a long time member of this  Church. I belong to the San Gabriel Mission Parish.  Born and raised in the thee adjacent neighborhood as a child growing up. St. Felicitas Church is beautiful and like all Catholic churches in thee area have some history.                      Very peaceful and relaxing to walk in and feel blessed and safe. I do Co+Sign for This place of a safe haven. A place to go to if feeling a little over whelmed with the madness in the streets, and everyday life?. photos to follow. This is Chuy Vara Viramontes signing off for now from a Small City that they call Alhambra Town,. Gateway to the San Gabriel Valley, SGV AKA SG,. With Respectt Father John is great. Really comes prepared with his homily. Great cantors. We are Saturday churchgoers. Also, Their lectors are well trained. Wonderful church. While visiting from Santa Rosa ca I attended Sunday mass here. That was about a year ago. Now I’m back and looking forward to joining service again in this most beautiful church.

name: Saints Simon & Jude Catholic Church - Huntington Beach Campus
reviewSummary:
💕❤ We appreciate the little ones! Cheerleaders!
Summer Kick Off barbecue night is a blast! With Live band too! 💕❤ I attended Mass at this church on my recent visit to California. It is a large and easy to access church with plenty of parking. Although I did not take advantage of it, there was a "meet and greet" before Mass. The congregation was friendly and welcoming. The musicians were excellent - I suspect most are professionals. The celebrant was easy to understand and I greatly enjoyed his homily on the Pentecost. Beautiful location for my Aunts funeral service. I wasn't sure what would happen after the Franciscans left, but the priests have been great. Active men's club. Solid high school youth program, grade school, sermons, and social justice outreach. Generally welcoming. A few people could be a little more LGBTQIA+ friendly. Friendly parishioners. Newly remodeled. Kind Priest

name: Salem Baptist Church - Winston-Salem Campus
reviewSummary:
I am sharing this post on behalf of my husband, Barkev.

I was born in an Armenian Christian home in Aleppo, Syria.  My dad was the assistant editor of a Christian magazine.  I was led to the Lord by my Christian school teacher when I was seven years old.

When I joined Piedmont Baptist College in 2005, my wife's and my priority was to join a local church.  We joined Salem Baptist Church because it met most of our spiritual needs:  worshipping, studying God's Word, sharing the love of Jesus, soul-winning, missionary outreach, Christian growth, and service as needed.

Salem is a spiritual home for us.  We share our prayer burdens, soul-winning opportunities, studying God's Word, and Christian service.  The Holy Spirit is fulfilling our spiritual needs.

I have had the privilege of serving as a deacon and in various other opportunities.  We are now enjoying retirement from our professions.  Life in Christ is rewarding. Salem Baptist Church is helping us to continue enjoying life.

The Bible is our manual.  Augustine said, "Where Scripture speaks, God speaks." We appreciate the priority of Bible exposition as basic for our pulpit.  We look forward to what God has to say to us.  The Bible is a Christ-centered book.  Our aim is to exalt Christ.

In Matthew 7:24-27, Jesus confronts us with the truth that each of us is building a life.  He wants each of us to build a life according to the truth of God's Word.  Jesus said.  "Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man which built his house upon a rock."  Matt. 7:24

Barkev S, Trachian, Ph.D. Salem Baptist Church , on Broad Street in Winston-Salem, NC , is my Home Church. I call it Home Church , because my whole life has been centered around this church family. I grew up in the church, got married in the church, raised my children and grand children in the church. I grew closer to God in the preaching and teaching in this church under the sound doctrine of many fine preachers . First and foremost is the Bibical Principles exercised in our church  .  The God honoring and awe inspiring Word of God taught in every area of ministry. God has blessed our church with ministries of a school, and Camp Merriwood, with missions and missionaries we support. I have confidence in the Pastor , Elders, Deacons and leadership that God has gifted to lead our church , knowing the Truth of God’s Word is being taught and exercised! I invite anyone seeking to know God more fully and willing and ready to study God’s word intently, will be blessed in joining with us . You will be loved! name: San Carlos Cathedral - Monterey Campus
reviewSummary:
Great historical cathedral in the heart of Monterey. It’s been beautifully renovated and was originally the military chapel founded by St. Junipero Serra. My review is not for the active San Carlos Cathedral church services. Instead it's for the Royal Presidio Chapel historic federal landmark. They are both the same building. Currently the San Carlos Cathedral Catholic Church uses the Presidio Chapel.  When services are not occurring, visitors can explore the interior and outside facade. There is no charge to walk about, it's free.

The present sandstone chapel construction was completed in 1795. The native Americans labors built the chapel. The Monterey Presidio was founded in 1770 as the second of four Spanish Presidios.  At that time, the presidio's chapel served for the Spanish soldiers and dignitaries. It's the oldest stone building in California.

When walking about the exterior of the chapel take note of the marked lines to the  right of the building. Those lines indicate chapel construction (where, what, and when). Directly in the back there is a plaque memorializing where the Oak tree stood in 1770 where Father Junipero Serra broke ground for the chapel construction. The tree was removed in 1905 when it was damaged. But the tree holds important place in Monterey history. In 1602, it is said that Spanish explorer Vizcaíno followed the creek from the Bay and noticed this majestic oak tree. Under that tree he and with the friars, traveling in his expedition, held Mass under the tree and claimed the area for Spain. Father Serra followed Vizcaino's directions to the site in 1770 to establish a mission and presidio. But a year or two later he decided to build the mission in Carmel instead. But the presidio continued with building the chapel. Pieces of the grand tree have been preserved and are located in various local museums.

Now let's talk about out the interior. The church doors are left open during the day welcoming all inside. Inside there are paintings and statues including  are originals such as the Stations of the Cross, St John, Sorrowful Mother, and Spanish Madonna. As you enter the church, look up and the exterior and take notice of  the Our Lady of Guadalupe statue; it's still the original making it the oldest non-indigenous statue in California.

Also throwing it out there that there are  cameras all over and everything is monitored.  So don't be a doofus. Just enjoy and soak in the history. Spanish architecture and area history.  Beautiful and peaceful This Cathedral was a treat to visit. It reminded me of European travels. It is amazing to have something of such age and significance in the United States. I'm grateful that it has been preserved in the Monterey Community. There are several benches outside and beautiful statues. Such a beautiful historic church. The grotto and surrounding prayer gardens were so awesome.  We were able to enter for a daily rosary. Highly recommend this outing if you're visiting.

name: San Francisco Bible Church - San Francisco Campus
reviewSummary:
A great church! During my first time here, they welcomed me warmly! Everyone is nice and welcoming! Don’t be afraid because no one will judge you as a new member! Warn God's flock. This is a once visible church that had become a dangerous cult, and it will harm you emotionally, spiritually, and financially.

1. There is an immature young pastor of bad fruit, greed, and self-indulgence (Matthew 23:5-13, 23, 25 and 28, 3 John, and 2 Peter 2): fighting and insulting people, making pathetic, pointless, and immature arguments, babbling non-stop disrespectful gibberish, refusing to apply basic Biblical teachings to his own life, falsely accusing people, falsely accusing people of things that he is doing, speaks very insolently, disrespectfully, and foolishly, lies constantly to deny what he did, has terrible, very childish, man-centered and non-biblical sermons, brags constantly (Jude 1:16 and Matthew 6:2-4; 16-18), dominating the Sunday services as just an associate pastor, has little to no decorum, and manipulating people to give him money and join the membership of his church.

2. There is no accountability. The young pastor can never be corrected, rebuked, or disciplined. After I moved on, the immature younger pastor was scared I would begin telling friends who go to SFBC the truth about him, so he slandered me through email to everyone on SFBC's membership list making up a bizarre lie that I "slandered" him and then he told them not to talk to me. Nothing was done and he continued to dominate services and gain more and more influence with the church leaders' support (e.g. a board member announced his "special accelerated membership class" during their service).

3. This church lies, slanders, and makes up false evidence against people to preserve their reputation. One board member wrote lying emails to friends about me. He made up complete nonsense and said I "continued to malign" the young pastor, when I was very patient and kind with him and only went into specifics with one board member. After that, I moved forward with telling the truth about him in detail to people through email and in real life. I do thank the board member who wrote this lying nonsense to friends who go to his church or are members of this church, because it opened the door to warn the community further up to this point.

4. This church brainwashes people into blindly following them instead of being obedient to Christ (Matthew 15:14). Former friends who once were determined not to be manipulated by that church became very badly brainwashed. One of them actually warned me about abuse and libel from that church, but betrayed me and ended contact. A second friend who was less likely to be blinded by them began going out of his way to start arguments to defend SFBC. Then he ended contact too even though I tried to hold on to him without talking about SFBC anymore. They began worshiping SFBC instead of Jesus.

5. SFBC is a money-making business always pressuring people to give more and more money and making people feel guilty for not going to enough of their ministry meetings and social events and not donating enough.

6. In general, the sermons are spiritually dead, shallow, and superficial. Every week, they ask the same spiritually dead questions: "How can I grow in my love for God? How can I know more about the Bible?"

However, the last true pastor, an older man, has some good sermons preached out of honest desire to edify believers. He literally told his audience to go home and listen to sermons online if he is just speaking his own truth. That is humility.

At best, SFBC is a very controversial church. Once the good pastor leaves, it is a cult. I stopped going in 2023, but I know little has changed. This church has faithfully taught God's word for almost 50 years. I've been part of this church family for 37 years. We have English and Cantonese services. Various fellowship groups meet here on Sunday afternoons, Wednesday's and many groups meet Friday night. Hope to see you here on Sunday. English services are at 8:00am & 11:10am, Cantonese services at 9:30am. This is a very friendly and welcoming Church.  As a 3X visitor I've felt very comfortable attending the Sunday, 11:15am Service. I truly enjoy the worship and the Expository Teaching of God's Word. When I can't attend I watch on-line. They have many ministries aimed for all ages, and a very nice Childrens ministry. The most friendliest church I’ve been to

reviewSummary: I believe I found my new church home. This place is open to all. There is a sense of calm here. There is an inviting sense of Faith here. name: San patrick - Mill Valley Campus
San Ramon Valley Bible Church - San Ramon Campus
reviewSummary:
As a child I fell in love with the Lord. In my thirties, my ex husband and I along with our three young children joined SRVBC. For the first few years the experience was amazing.  I felt alive in the Word and in the Lord. After a while, it seemed that those who tithed "higher" $, were the ones chosen for certain tasks as well as 'seating assignments'. The leadership thrived on money given to the church and at once you were feeling like you were sidelined.

A very close relative who had been a Pastor for over 30+ years visited SRVBC. He was asked to speak several different times. My relative took my ex husband and I out to lunch one Sunday after service and very humbly told us we needed to leave the church. He had seen what we had suspected.

I left years and years ago and I'm still to this day dealing with what I went through and I'm scared to be involved in another church. I praise God for San Ramon bible church. I’m incredibly thankful for the teaching of the word of God so powerful and clear and easy to understand.  The leadership is amazing ( loving, kind, always available to take a call to help me  in anyway that I might need and also my entire family.  I’m eternally grateful! I heard the way of salvation at SRVBC and gave my life to Jesus Christ the best decision I’ve ever made. If you’re looking for eternal security, support, encouragement, love and fellowship with other believers from young people to older people look no further San Ramon valley bible church has great Sunday sermons and fellowship plus Wednesday night women’s bible study and men’s prayer meeting and different age groups of Friday night youth groups and older single groups. There is something for everyone. Thank you Jesus for bring me here and my family ❤️ I have attended SRVBC since 1992 (28 yrs). Was married in this Church  and raised two children in the truth of the Word. If it wasn't for teaching the truth straight from the Bible, and most importantly, Leadership living it out in their daily lives, I know that I would not have the transformed life that I have today. Living for Christ daily and having a true compassion for the well being of others, living a godly life, being an encourager, and a light to those struggling or needing to know the Savior... is what life is all about... You will find that here. The community at this church is like a family.  It's a very welcoming environment and a place to connect with others for support and worship. I appreciate the music, the message and pastor Adel.  It's so amazing to see how everyone supports and prays for one another.  I was raised Catholic but I visit regularly to get my "dose" of family as well as a message with bible-based foundation. Our family attended this church for 29 years. Terrible lies were told about our family and insults about our children and our marriage. We were told we had the worst marriage in the church, ( we have been married for 44 years) we were told our children went to inferior schools (U.C Santa Cruz and the U.S Air Force Academy) and we were maligned to others behind our backs. When we left, people still at the church refused to speak to us or our sons. The church FALSELY accused us of suing the church and FALSELY accused us of attempting to fire the pastor's son from Oracle. None of these false statements have been retracted by SRVBC.
