St. Denis Catholic Church - Chino Hills Campus
reviewSummary:
An absolutely stunning church, easily one of the most beautiful I have ever seen. The architecture and atmosphere are incredible, and it was an absolute honor to be able to shoot inside. Originally built in the pre-Vatican II style but since reconfigured to allow for more participation by parishioners, St Denis is a beautiful church, featuring lots of marble and stone. The courtyard is ample enough for large gatherings. The Eucharistic chapel is breathtaking and quiet. St. Denis Catholic Church is a true spiritual home, and it has earned my heartfelt five-star review. From the dedicated priests to the beautiful liturgy, it’s a place that genuinely nurtures the soul.

I’m especially grateful for the consistent access to the Sacrament of Reconciliation, with daily confessions offered Monday through Saturday (noting only occasional exceptions on Saturdays). This commitment is a tremendous gift to the community.

The priests are a remarkable blessing. Father John is wonderfully detail-oriented and has a constant, positive vision for improving the church grounds and parish life. Father Dennis provides a perfect balance—he is a profoundly warm and calming presence with a true gift for hospitality, even remembering the names of those who attend regularly.

The music ministry elevates the worship experience beautifully. The Sunday 11:00 AM choir is excellent, and the Young Adult choir at the 5:30 PM Mass is both skilled and spiritually moving to listen to.

Overall, St. Denis is a parish that clearly cares for its people through prayer, service, and a very welcoming atmosphere. I highly recommend it to anyone seeking a faithful and vibrant church community. Beautiful church ⛪️ not a local here & went here for Mass closer to place we were staying. Love my church father Denis is an amazing person ❤️ We just had my daughter's 16 . Connie was our singer and she had such a beautiful voice. It was amazing  what a blessing.

name: St. Didacus Catholic Church - San Diego (Downtown) Campus
reviewSummary:
My husband and I have been attending this church as members for a couple of years. When we got engaged, we enrolled in the parish's marriage preparation program and their Rite of Christian Initiation of Adults (RCIA) program to finish some of our missing sacraments. Deacon Dino Serafini prepared us and officiated our rite of marriage, and Elena Platas and Roman Becerra led our preparation to become fully initiated Catholics. All of them are some of the kindest and wisest people I've had the pleasure to meet. They are very welcoming and genuinely care about the people attending our parish.

We had ~160 guests on our wedding day, with lots of space for up to ~200 guests in the parish. We also had a live mariachi band play at our wedding. We opted for very minimal decorations, as the church is beautiful already. In all, we are very happy to have married at St. Didacus, and we look forward to continuing to attend this parish for years to come. I recently attended Mass at a church in San Diego County as part of my goal to visit different churches in the area. While I found it challenging to understand the priest at times, I appreciated the opportunity to experience the service and learn more about the church community. The community seemed very close-knit and welcoming. St. Didacus Church is a beautiful church with an outstanding staff. They scheduled my father's funeral mass on the first Friday of lent when no other Catholic church in San Diego would. The priest also volunteered to come to the burial site after the mass to bless the final resting place.
My mother still talks about how blessed we were to find St. Didacus. Thank you and God bless you. I had such a beautiful Christmas meditation at this shrine. I'm so grateful to the Church community for offering such a devotional and inspiring place. I was a parishioners of this church and attended regular mass. Their choir would sing an uplifting hym about community and family that kept me returning almost every Sunday just to hear them and learn more about the faith under Pastor Mike Senior.

reviewSummary:
I'm from Michigan and have visited St. Edmund's Anglican Church.  I loved the service each time.  It felt very familiar and comfortable to me as someone who became Anglican 35 years ago.  The worship is reverent and beautiful, the teaching powerful and sound, the Sacrament rightly administered.

And the downtown neighborhood is beautiful and very walkable!

I plan to visit St. Edmund's every time I come to Milwaukee! Our family attended a beautiful service on Easter Sunday.  St. Edmund’s fosters a wonderful sense of community.  They have a welcoming and kind congregation.  For anyone looking for a traditional Anglican service, St. Edmund’s would be a lovely choice. We were members of St. Edmund's for about a year during a time of transition, and Fr. Eric baptized one of our children. The congregation was just what we needed for a high-church, yet not overstimulating, experience. St. Edmund’s Anglican Church is a warm and welcoming community. The sermons are inspiring, and the traditional hymnal music adds a beautiful and meaningful touch to each service. My husband and I moved to Milwaukee last June and heard about St. Edmund’s through a mutual friend. Everyone was so welcoming, friendly, and genuinely wanted to get to know us after the service.

name: St. Edward the Confessor Catholic Church - Dana Point Campus
reviewSummary:
My visit to Saint Edward the Confessor Catholic Church was truly uplifting. The Sunday Mass was celebrated in a sanctuary filled with a vibrant, engaged congregation that clearly forms the heart of this parish community.

The church grounds are absolutely breathtaking, with carefully maintained gardens that complement the stunning ocean views. Standing in the courtyard after Mass, watching the Pacific shimmer in the distance, provided a moment of peaceful reflection that perfectly extended the spiritual experience.

The Father's homily was thoughtfully crafted and delivered with genuine passion. He masterfully connected scripture to everyday life in a way that had the entire congregation truly reflecting on the message. You could tell he puts great effort into engaging with his parishioners, addressing real concerns while offering hope and guidance.

The warmth of the community was evident in how parishioners greeted each other before and after the service. This is clearly not just a place of worship but a true spiritual family.

Whether you're a longtime parishioner or just visiting Laguna, Saint Edward the Confessor offers both spiritual nourishment and natural beauty that feeds the soul. Highly recommended for anyone seeking connection to faith in a stunning setting.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ My favorite church hands down and of course I am biased. name: St. Ignatius Parish - San Francisco Campus
reviewSummary:
Incredible Church.  Like a cathedral.  I had the opportunity to officiate/witness a wedding here.  I was astonished that this is a parish in the SF Diocese.  I am not sure how old it is but the architecture was very old school European, if that is a thing.  The sacristans, coordinators and musicians were all very welcoming to me and the wedding party.  Thank you Don and Patrick. San Francisco is a city of tectonic impermanence, a place where the ground routinely threatens to erase the skyline. But stepping into St. Ignatius Parish is an exercise in monumental defiance. It doesn’t just occupy space; it commands it.
Built in 1914 by architect Charles J.I. Devlin—after the 1906 earthquake rudely leveled its predecessor—the building is a masterclass in an eclectic style known as "Jesuit Baroque." From the outside, the twin spires loom over the city like a pair of unyielding sentries. But the real narrative is inside.
Observe the photographic record. The sheer volume of the nave is staggering, an architectural sleight of hand that uses poured concrete masquerading as classical Roman grandeur. Your eyes are immediately drawn upward by the towering, fluted columns crowned with heavy, gilded Corinthian capitals. They shoulder the weight of a massive, coffered ceiling and a central dome that feels less like a structural necessity and more like an artificial sky.
The decoration is unapologetically intricate, a calculated sensory overload. Yet, what strikes you isn't the gold leaf or the carved plaster—it's the light. The immense stained glass windows act as a theater prism, bleeding saturated, neon reds and blues directly onto the upper walls and the stone arches. Look at the way the colored light pools in the upper galleries in the photos. It’s pure drama. Down below, a long strip of crimson carpet cuts through the symmetry of the dark timber pews like a velvet artery, leading the eye straight down the cavernous hall.
There is a quiet, heavy gravity to the space. You don't need to be searching for anything abstract to appreciate the scale of the endeavor. It is a structural masterpiece, an acoustically pristine vault designed to make the individual feel incredibly small while simultaneously showcasing the sheer, stubborn heights of human design.
Five stars. It is an echoing, beautifully over-engineered landmark of survival and classical proportions. The only thing missing is a stiff drink, but you can’t have everything. The interior decoration for Palm Sunday mass on March 29, 2026, was simply breathtaking. The majestic palms lining the aisle created an enchanting ambiance.

St. Ignatius Church stands as one of the most stunning churches in San Francisco. Its architectural grandeur, exquisite stained glass windows, and picturesque surroundings make it a must-visit destination for both visitors and locals. My daughter saw the church from across the city and asked what was that my wife said? It's a church so we drove across town and went to the church beautiful church. We walked right in and were able to walk up to the altar, beautiful stained glass windows, incredible architecture, very peaceful church. And lovely fresco's. The use of a catholic church for this type of venue is amazing.  You are able to take in the architecture, art, and details.  The space also lends itself to a rich acoustic sound.

reviewSummary:

I breathe heavy metal, but I'm also a sucker for baroque and the human voice and everything in-between. I thought to myself, "I've spent worse Sundays than being in La Jolla. Why not?" Traffic...is, but the more South you go, towards the church, the parking gets much easier, especially late afternoon.

Groups better be good to sing there because nothing slips by and nothing gets lost in there. NOTE: There are pipe organ concerts there as well. If you ask me, I think every music-loving San Diegan should try something completely different on a Sunday afternoon / evening and check this place out sometime. I think a lot of people will be really surprised. I shot a wedding here this past weekend. It's a very beautiful church, but there are a lot of restrictions for photography during wedding service. Outside of that, the staff and clergy are kind and polite. Very home-y.  A beautiful interior and a rich history.  Stanford men's choir sings here every year, among other frequent events brought held. I called this church a while back over the phone, and spoke with one of the male receptionist, and from what I gathered through our conversation, no compassion, no fruit of the spirit, very disappointed. I thought to myself, this is a bad representation of what followers of the word are displaying in these times!!!👎🏻 The Assembly of Daughters of the King held on May 21, 2016 was beautifully arranged and executed by Elena Luz, D.O.K. Chapter President
and her friendly assistants!  It was a lovely event from the food to the flowers and the inspiring speaker, the Rev. Monica Mainwaring.  Thank you everyone!

name: St. James Cathedral
reviewSummary:
This is a beautiful cathedral. It is lightened airy with a stunning oculus above the altar which has red and yellow sways dropped from the ceiling. It is close to the.Frye Art gallery and both buildings are free to enter and Worth visiting. In a world that can feel overwhelming and isolating, I always find peace in the beauty and majesty of St. James. Both as a place and a people, the Cathedral is warm and welcoming to all. I would encourage believers and non-believers to visit. God has surprised me more than once with community and contentment at the Cathedral. The liturgies are rich and beautiful and the homilies are thought provoker and usually have a call to action "Faith without works is dead" (James 2:26). Shout out to Fathers Ryan and Lazzeroni, they are among the best. Amazing cathedral! Even has an accessible entrance which is hard to find in houses of worship this old. Simply gorgeous. INCREDIBLE experience. We visited Seattle for the first time and one of the things was to go and visit some Cathedrals around the area. This one is above them all let me just say that. The workers/volunteers are all very kind and welcoming, the stained glass is beautiful, and the little rooms throughout the church are wonderful to walk in. And if you walk outside into this little courtyard there is a bookshop. I wish I knew her name but the kindest lady was in there working, she talked to us for about 45 minutes and has been at this church for 50 years! It was an amazing experience and I would love to return to a mass one day in the future! St. James Cathedral is truly one of the most beautiful and welcoming places in Seattle. The church itself is peaceful, stunning, and full of history, but what really stands out is the sense of community and kindness from the people there.

I’ve had a very positive experience attending Mass and learning more about the Catholic faith through their programs. The atmosphere is calm, respectful, and uplifting, and the music and architecture make every visit feel meaningful.

Whether you are deeply religious, exploring your faith, or just visiting Seattle, St. James Cathedral is absolutely worth experiencing.

name: St. James Cathedral, Chicago
reviewSummary:
The choir’s harmonies carried the entire nave, and the organ’s sound filled every corner—truly a concert for the soul. The deacon welcomed us with a warm smile and handed out a hand‑crafted faith guide that felt personal and thoughtful. Every corner of the sanctuary, from the stained‑glass to the oak pews, seemed lovingly maintained, making the visit feel like stepping into a living museum and a quiet retreat at once. This is one of the first churches to be rebuilt after the fire. The tower actually is prefire. The Cathedral has been exquisitely restored.
I’m a cradle Episcopalian. I love the spirituality and beauty of the service.
A new Dean was recently installed. Dean Lisa is literally a gift from God.
Perhaps more importantly, the grace, love and welcoming spirit of Christ lives here. A refuge for us all in these strange times.
Peace in Christ,
Greg Everyone is welcome. This charming, historic church is open to visitors on most days. They offer a personal tour brochure. We attended their Easter service and were really impressed. Their service is very personal, and people seem genuinely friendly vs. a "Sunday smile." The pastor involves the congregation and speaks in a manner that can resonate with anyone from a weekly church goer to people like us who are not frequent attendees. Beautiful interior, I'm not religious but I appreciate that it's a beautiful building inside and out, well worth a visit.

name: St. James Episcopal Church - Main Campus
St. James Episcopal Church - Newport Beach Campus
reviewSummary:
St. James Episcopal Church is an incredibly warm and welcoming place. From our very first visit, we felt genuine kindness, acceptance, and the true spirit of Christian love.

The church and grounds are beautiful, peaceful, and thoughtfully cared for. Every detail — from seasonal decorations to the quiet spaces inside — reflects reverence, tradition, and heartfelt dedication.

But what makes this place truly special is the people. The clergy, volunteers, and parish members welcome you as if you’ve always belonged here. Their kindness has meant so much to our family.

We are deeply grateful to God for leading us here, and we are happy to be part of this community.

If you are looking for a church where you can feel peace, connection, and sincere faith — this is the place. Everyone at St. James Episcopal Church in Newport Beach is warm and welcoming. I was the DJ and line dance instructor at their annual hoedown. Not only did everyone participate in the line dancing and have a great time, but there was so much pie! I think every congregant must have brought a pie because there were so many to choose from. I settled on the key lime! An incredible place of worship with an incredible group of people! I have been coming here for 2 years and have never felt this way about a particular church before. This is my spiritual home. I’m so glad I found St. James Episcopal Church! It’s a welcoming and inclusive community where everyone feels at home. The choir is outstanding, with professional singers who truly elevate the service. There’s always something new to celebrate, making every visit special. Reverend Cindy and her staff are wonderful people who genuinely care about the congregation. I highly recommend this church to anyone looking for a friendly and inspiring place to worship! I am very grateful to be a member at St. James. It is truly a faith community both welcoming and affirming. There are lots of activities, discussion groups and musical programs. I am a regular participant in the Ignatian Spirituality Group. That has become an important part of my journey. All are welcome at St. James and the parking is really good.

name: St. Jane Frances de Chantal Catholic Church - Van Nuys Campus
reviewSummary: Visited this church today with our son. Mass was 11.30 am (Family mass). The ushers were very welcoming, our son loved it. I enjoyed how the priest had the children in front asking questions about the Homily, and how they were so eager to answer the questions and share. Also for the children who didn't make first communion, they were allowed to come up and the Priest gave a blessing.  Also today, had a gentleman Tony and his son Joseph selling some lovely items. Don't know which church they would be heading to but really good quality. Would definitely visit again, God's will if in the area. It’s a lovely and welcoming community. The Blessed Sacrament is exposed 7 days a week and 24h a day. It’s a great blessing to be there. A few weeks ago my husband and I came to this church for the food giveaway and there were a lot of issues and a lot of problems you definitely need like security or somebody in charge of people are cutting lines saving spaces for people there became a problem a couple weeks ago and you really need somebody out there early because I'm so disorganized and a lot of people that were there so they're not ever coming back because of these women who were in the front of the line saving spots for people that weren't even These are very special priests, always available to help the community, very friendly, and with great charisma. We also have the blessing of the chapel for adoration of the Blessed Sacrament. Love the atmosphere here wonderful service grate community

name: St. Joan of Arc - Chagrin Falls Campus
reviewSummary: A wonderful, tight-knit Catholic community. Truly a fantastic church and school! This parish is a sleeping giant in the Cleveland diocese. The people are wonderful, the Mary Garden is beautiful, and the Catholic school is excellent. Highly recommend St Joan of Arc in Chagrin! SJA Catholic School has been an exceptional experience for my daughter. I have been very impressed by SJA’s curriculum and teaching  methods. The Teacher’s are very kind, understanding, and are truly invested in the children’s education. The amazing staff is very supportive and genuinely cares about each and every students success both in and out of the classroom. There is a wide variety of school events, activities, and sports to participate in. SJA is a warm and kind community that feels like family! We love it here and highly recommend this school which has exceeded all of our expectations! St. Joan of Arc School provides an excellent academic and religious education.  The administration, faculty, staff, and students are very warm and welcoming. My family and I have been attending St Joan's for over twenty-five years. My children attended the elementary school here before going to Gilmour Academy. Bishop Pilla referred to the parish as a jewel in the greater Cleveland area, and he was certainly accurate in that description. The school, the teachers, the church,  and staff and are top notch people.

name: St. John Apostle and Evangelist
reviewSummary:
Almost hidden by other city buildings, this church is a beautiful place of worship.  The congregation is very welcoming, and on my first time attending, greeters made sure that I was comfortable. The music is amazing.  There is an accessible entrance and accessible parking lot. The apse artwork is amazing. I highly recommend stopping in here. Put your damn Private Property sign in a better spot so it's easier to see and help prevent people from having their car towed/possibly towed...

And no, I'm being serious. Literally almost had my car towed because the sign is not in an open area. And saw a few other people have a huge sticker slapped on their window. The church it self is amazing, just beautiful. The only problem was the coordinator didn't seem very helpful when having a wedding. Over heard her say that she didn't want to do a Mexican wedding again. Beautiful church, very personable pastor Monsignor Delaney.  Had a nice brief conversation with him after 10am Sunday mass.

name: St. John Chaldean Catholic Church - El Cajon Campus
reviewSummary: Blessed church there a presence of the holy spirt and god waving at the whole church I feel so blessed to be around this church and the saints of blessed monks love this church and the staff are very welcoming can’t wait for every Sunday and mass to be there It is a great church! I enjoy coming here. Especially with the new remodel. It looks very nice. They have the best times for Mass. 12pm in English is perfect in case we don’t make it to 10am at St. Peter’s. The priest there, Father Ankido, is a very nice and humble man. He has the best homilies too! All the Monks, servers, and people there are very nice! I really enjoy coming here! One most beautiful churches in san diego...my father's service was there Nice church, super clean, staff very welcoming and friendly. Easy to make an appointment. Father Ankido was very pleasant and helpful so was the manager (I assume, the lady who met us at the church office). We sat at the church while we were waiting for our appointment. The atmosphere was so peaceful, and relaxing. Fr Ankido provided us with some information and even though he couldn’t help us with what we needed but he was very open and genuinely cared. Highly recommended I went to this church last night with my fiance and co worker. Services was amazing. It reminded me if services back home in the Philippines. The message was good. Without love you gain nothing. I'm glad we found a church that is literally around the corner from our house & I won't have to miss mass since they have English services at 7pm. Cant wait to hear next Sunday's word.

name: St. John Church - Oceanside Campus
reviewSummary: Mother Watson and Carolyn G made sure to bless Vintage Pointe 1 seniors. Thank you 🙏 for always thinking about us and making the club house over flow with God’s blessings. Carolyn G. and mother Ollie W. continue to bless our seniors at Vintage Pointe 1. We appreciate you and it helps my seniors to socialize and have treats in their clubhouse. Thank you Reverend Dr. Kadri Web. The word is being preached by a true man of God that has committed his life to serve the people of God. I've experienced true presents of the spirit of God  here. The people that attend are friendly and welcoming. When you come to this church be ready for an experience that fills your soul and a word that teaches how to serve our Lord & Savior Jesus Christ. Are you looking to be spiritually feed?  Do you want to give praise, sing, and dance for our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ?  Do you want to have a hallelujah good time with like-minded people?  Then, this is the place to be yourself.  Come on out and have a joyful time in the Word with us! Awesome holy ghost-filled church awesome Pastor nice people Bible teaching. A well-rounded church youth program senior program. It's a well-rounded church for families.

name: St. John Henry Newman Catholic Church - Irvine Campus
reviewSummary:
Wonderful place to worship. I attended Mass at 11:30am in Sunday and it was packed. I love the English hymns with the Roman Liturgy. The parish members are welcoming. I’d like to take my family again when we visit Irvine. Mass is done here in the Anglican Use of the Roman Rite. Despite being in the Diocese of Orange, it falls under the jurisdiction of the Ordinariate of the Chair of St. Peter. Very small location, but its Mass is much more reverent than those found in larger Catholic Churches. Father Glenn is a very good homilist and defends the honor of the liturgy, and the music is very conducive to proper worship. Deacon Christopher was only ordained a year ago. Very personable church. Small and close-knit congregation. Part of the Ordinariate of the Catholic Church. Anglicans and Episcopalians thinking of converting to Catholicism would feel very at home here. I would probably feel like I needed confession if I rated a Catholic Church less than five stars; the primary purpose of this review is to highlight some things that I know people care about when looking for a Mass or a parish.

- This church is part of the Ordinariate of the Chair of St. Peter, not the Diocese of Orange. The Ordinariate was set up for Anglican converts, and answers directly to the Pope. It is a legit Catholic Church authorized to use an Anglican-style liturgy. The priest is an Anglican convert.

- The priest here faces the altar during the Mass and communion is received kneeling and on the tongue. The Mass is not in Latin, but parts of it are different if you are used to a regular Roman mass.

- This church is inside a larger building, a law firm that has a Catholic chapel attached. This sounds weird, but it is very nice inside. St JHN is a wonderful, small Catholic Church.  Seating is very limited, but the setting is intimate.  No microphones needed.  The singing was very solemn and respectful.  I attended during a Prinicipal Mass which covered a lot of ritual and liturgy.  The homily was tremendously mature and informative.  I wish my own church offered the depth of spiritual understanding and instruction.  Great Sunday!

name: St. John Maron Maronite Catholic Church - Orange Campus
reviewSummary:
St. John Maron Maronite Catholic Church is truly a gem in our community and has become a place I hold very dear. The church property itself is beautifully maintained and provides a peaceful, inviting space that feels like home every time I visit. There’s something very special about walking onto the grounds, surrounded by the warmth of fellow parishioners and the beauty of our shared faith.

Being part of this church has allowed me to connect deeply with my Maronite Catholic roots. The rich traditions, meaningful liturgies, and sense of heritage here are like no other. Each visit offers not just spiritual fulfillment but also a profound sense of connection to my Lebanese culture and the community that celebrates it.

The people at St. John Maron are welcoming and kind, and there’s a strong sense of unity that radiates from every corner of the church. Whether it's during Mass, community events, or even just a friendly conversation, I always leave feeling uplifted and proud of my heritage.

If you’re looking for a church where you can feel connected, spiritually enriched, and embraced by a wonderful community, St. John Maron Maronite Catholic Church is the place to be. If you’re seeking an incredible spiritual experience, this church hosts several beautiful masses each week. It is led by a Monsignor and two nuns who are very humble and close to God. It is a very family oriented church and the leader ship are open to questions and conversations. I highly recommend this church where the masses are combined in English, Arabic, and Syriac. There are TVs that have translations of the entire mass. Super friendly people. You feel the holy spirit in this church. I am not a Maronite, yet I still visit this curch frequently..I really enjoy their mass. Beautiful worship space and inspiring services! The hospitality that they showed when I went to see the St Jude Relic was wonderful may God bless them all and may my Saint Jude watch over them and keep them safe amen

name: St. John Missionary Baptist Church - Long Beach Campus
reviewSummary: It's like home. Where everyone knows everyone. Where a hug is your greeting and a smile is your assurance of love in the place. There is a continuous atmosphere of caring and, no matter where you go you aleays want to return. You are always welcomed here at St John's. From the Pastor to the congregants and little ones,  you will find the love of Jesus throughout the building! Come join us! I have an amazing Church a great pastor and a first lady that is so wonderful and they are a blessing and they will be missed I Debbie Miller it's a great church and proud to a member of and a senior Usher there, a great pastor too. Always give the Great word from God along with good music that increase our soul 🙌 ❤

name: St. John Neumann Catholic Church - Irvine Campus
reviewSummary:
Have recently began attending this church, which is located in the Woodbridge village, when they began having masses indoors. The mission statement is: Guided by the Holy Spirit, St John Neumann Parish of Irvine shares the Good News of Jesus Christ with people of all ages, diverse faiths and cultures, forming a welcoming, worshiping Catholic community. Been here since 2005. Warm and welcoming community. Many Pastors have retired but many young Priests are new and bring life to the church. Each new season; Advent, Lent, Epiphany, Easter and Ordinary time tell the story of Christ’s life through the readings of old, New Testaments. The Bible is the book of the church not the other way around. Volunteered for many years as I was raising my son until HS. I would recommend their confirmation classes, as well. Lots of room to grow deeper into your faith through Bible study, books, volunteerism, helping the poor, pilgrimages, etc. Thriving Filipino, Chinese, Vietnamese, Italian, Irish communities as well. Come join us!!! Staff is very helpful, office is open 7 days a week, and they have the best choir I've ever heard (10:30). A great church in Irvine area. The parishioners and priests are great. Very welcoming community. I used to attend the daily morning mass.
Recently they stopped the 6.40 am mass on Monday and Wednesday.
Also the church is small compared to the number of families assigned to this parish. So it is always crowded. Iam not Catholic but Iam a Christian who loves the Lord and love my catholic brothers and sisters at Saint Neumann. I love going to Mass several days wèek. All the fathers preach a Real Gospel about Jesus Christ,to love our neighbors like The Christ did🙏🏾

name: St. John of the Cross - El Cajon Campus
reviewSummary:
On Sunday, Jan 18, I came back to my church for the first time in over 10 years. I’m usually disheartened by the number of attendees who go for the aesthetic rather than to truly follow Christ’s message. Unfortunately today felt no different. Someone abandoned two puppies at the church around 6pm. We tried to notify services and anyone coming in and out of the church to find them a home. We even let the father know before the 7pm spanish mass. We barely got an acknowledgement. It’s not anyone’s responsibility but it’s disheartening that in two hours no one could offer tangible help. I went home and brought them a blanket and placed them in this box for others to watch. We’ll find a way but I’m posting in hopes we learn to come together as a community and focus on practicing what we’re preaching. Blessings to the few people who stayed and watched them.

Proverbs 22:9 (New King James Version) Attended the 10 am Sunday service here on my quest to visit all San Diego County churches. It was a basic Catholic service experience. Finding parking was easy... Plenty of parking spots available here. Vibrant parish, the music was well done, the homily challenged us in a lovingly way. The sermon was tedious; sounding like the priest hadn't cared enough to rehearse it sufficiently. He probably said 'you must fear god in a healthy way' close to 15 times. I found the fellow parishioners to be eagerly seeking direction and comfort and perhaps finding it in themselves while attilributing it to the service. All that gold. What a waste. Nice windows though. First time here to go to church as i visit San Diego.

name: St. John the Baptist Catholic Church
reviewSummary: The Norbertine priests are outstanding confessors and homilists. Reverent Latin and English Masses.

name: St. John the Baptist Greek Orthodox Church - Anaheim Campus
reviewSummary:
St. John the Baptist Greek
Orthodox Church & Greek Festival is a truly exceptional community event. Nestled in a beautiful church adorned with intricate mosaic art of Mary and Jesus, this festival is a vibrant celebration of Greek culture. Rows of shops offer authentic clothing, jewelry, and crafts, while the food is a standout—from savory grilled meats and dolmas to decadent Greek desserts. The atmosphere is warm and family-friendly, with traditional Greek singing, guitar performances, and lively dance shows. Safety and accessibility are top priorities, with police presence ensuring a secure and organized environment, and designated parking for those with disabilities. This is more than a festival; it’s a rich, immersive experience that leaves a lasting impression on all who attend. We went to Greek Fest and had a great time. It’s well organized and the lines moved fast. The food was delicious! There’s parking and a shuttle to take you to the church. The wait was about 10 minutes. We will be back! Geek Festival ever is fun to enjoy Greek food, music, and shopping items. This is a beautiful Orthodox Christian Church with a wonderful and caring Christian community.

I find it odd that people are evaluating the quality of a religious institution based on the price of a food item at a church fundraiser.  That's pretty shameful.  Regardless, I've had nothing but wonderful experiences here. I'm an Inquirer. But truly,

☦︎ Come and See!

name: St. John the Evangelist Catholic Church - San Diego (Downtown) Campus
reviewSummary:
All church servers are helpful & smiling. The church emphasizes acceptance of all as children of God.  The lead singer is so good as well as the entire choir.  The ministers & volunteers are welcoming.  Daily 5pm Mass everyday for those like me who cannot wake up early  :) --- plus other morning Mass schedules. On my quest to attend mass in every church in San Diego County, I went to St. John yesterday. Nestled amidst the bustle of the city, St. John radiates a quiet warmth that draws you in like a gentle hug. Stepping into its threshold is like stepping back in time, not to a bygone era, but to a space where kindness and community reign supreme.
The first thing that strikes you is the abundance of friendly faces. A vibrant tapestry of silver hair and laughter lines, etched with the wisdom of years well-lived, greets you with genuine smiles and open arms. Gone is the anonymity of larger churches; here, everyone seems to know each other, and a newcomer is welcomed like a long-lost friend. The service itself is a testament to the church's dedication to its congregation. The pace is deliberate, allowing time for quiet reflection and mindful participation. The pastor's message is delivered with warmth, offering words of comfort and guidance that resonate deeply with the life experiences of his flock. And then there's the parking. Oh, the glorious parking! In a world where finding a spot near a church can feel like winning the lottery, St. John's boasts a vast, well-maintained lot that eliminates the pre-service stress. No more circling endlessly, no more hurried walks from distant streets. Just pull in, park with ease, and join the warm embrace of this welcoming community. St. John the Evangelist is a powerful and inspiring Catholic church in San Diego. Its beautifully performed hymns, the joy it imparts, and the spiritual inspiration it provides make it a place of profound significance. Attending mass here is a spiritual journey that enriches the soul and leaves you feeling closer to God. Very welcoming and friendly community! The priest gave a wonderful homily on faith and hope. The music was uplifting and included Latin responses. I enjoyed visiting. The church was beautiful, the hymns thoughtfully chosen, the scripture and homily were insightful and applicable to life. A welcoming and inclusive community.

name: St. John United Church of Christ - Louisville Campus
reviewSummary: Great service and friendly congregants. Glad to have visited. Oldest church in Louisville. Beautiful old church building. Only saw from the outside on a Saturday afternoon. The volunteers are wonderful here, very helpful and nice This is a beautiful church with a wonderful sense of community. This is a place of genuine positivity, support, and acceptance. This is everything a church in louisville should be. The sermons always leave you thinking and feeling closer to god. It is the perfect mix of tradition and progressiveness. Highly recommend! Questioning your faith? Looking for a place full of good conversation and some answers to your questions? St. John’s is the place to be. My husband and I have been attending regularly since August of this year. The feeling of family in this church is wonderful! Congregation is a bit small but large in spirit!

name: St. John United Methodist Church - Main Campus
St. John Vianney Catholic Church
reviewSummary: A traditional Catholic parish in west Houston with reverent liturgical worship and active parish community.

name: St. John's Cathedral - Jacksonville (Downtown) Campus
reviewSummary:
I love The Cathedral. Everyone is do welcoming. It offers so much and does so much good in our community. Everyone is Welcome and it is a wonderful place to spend time with God. Such positive uplifting messages and I would recommend it to everyone looking for a church home or in town visiting. Very Inclusive and accepting of all people. Come for a Visit. Ancient Being. Antique Surroundings. Heritage Place. Cathedral Hill Neighborhood. Congregation. Theological Seminary. Permanent Art Collection. Music Hall. Events: Concerts. Every year, St. John's Cathedral hosts amazing pipe organ concerts as part of The Beaches Fine Arts Series. These free concerts are open to the general public and show case some of the world's most accomplished pipe organists. Listening to the mighty pipe organ in the beautiful church sanctuary is one of the most moving and amazing experiences to be had in Jacksonville! Thank you for opening your church to the larger community for these much appreciated, deeply enjoyed and memorable performances! My husband and I have been members of the choir at St. John's Cathedral since 1981. My husband and I love the music program there. Both our former choirmaster/organist, John Barry, and our current one, Tim Tuller, are amazing musicians. It has been and is a privilege to work with both of them. We love the Anglican style choral music. I love to play my cello in the services from time to time. Our choir has made two pilgrimages to England, singing services at Ely Cathedral, Westminster Cathedral and Canterbury Cathedral. We also went on a pilgrimage trip to Washington DC where we were in residence at the National Cathedral. The congregation at St. John's contains some of the nicest people around and we always welcome newcomers. Hope you'll visit. Warm & inviting. Although I'm Baptist by birth, I couldn't have felt more welcomed.  The minister, Rev. Mark Anderson, delivered a very encouraging & worthy message that inspires hope!

Rev. Anderson shared an unforgettable story about two particular groups who were stranded out in the Arctic.  One resorted to crude means of survival & only 3 survived.

However, the other group cleverly appointed tasks based on ingenuity of the individuals, even assigning a minister.  This bonding teamwork provided a better outcome of survival for the two groups.

name: St. John's Episcopal Church

name: St. John's Evangelical Lutheran Church - El Cajon Campus
reviewSummary:

Good venue overall. This church and the members are nice and I really feel the Lord and his holy spirit is with us all when I sit in the chapel at this church. My family and I also love the time of year to have our animals Blessed by the Pastor. Our grandson attends preschool at St. John's and they are absolutely wonderful.  Would give 10 stars if possible. St. John's Lutheran Church & School - Main Campus
St. John's Lutheran Church Business Office - Orange Campus
St. John's Lutheran Church of Orange - Orange Campus
reviewSummary:
It's a peaceful and joy-filled church service. I love the Bible teachings during service and the hymns we sang were classic that transports my soul uplifted and renewed. Such an amazing place of worship and history dedicated to the Triune God! The music program and the pastors are some of the best we have ever heard!  The people are very welcoming and the church and school do so many things for the local community and missions around the world!  Stop in for one of their concerts! Beutiful Church located just East of Old Town Orange. If you're already in Orange just take the walk down to Almond & Center. Haven't been in years but it is a beautiful church with heart. In early 2024, I went here for a funeral of one of my former high school teachers who did on Thanksgiving Day. It was really sad.

Parking was good and I even got the chance to meet former faculty members and some of my teachers.

The interior is very beautiful especially when it comes to Christmas decorations. The place is very clean and well-taken care of. There were people who were generous with each other.

name: St. John's Lutheran School of Orange - Orange Campus
St. John's Metropolitan Community Church - Raleigh Campus
reviewSummary:
Love this place! As a millennial parent, I was looking for a church that was loving towards all and would teach my kids the same thing. I really enjoy coming to church each week, something I’ve struggled with in the past. Come check it out.

You’re welcome if you’re straight, gay, cis, trans, queer, young, old, and everyone in between. This was the first time I have went to church in a long time. I’m just now getting more In touch with God and this group is very supportive and friendly. Looks at the Bible but also it’s okay to be who you’re. Would recommended this place for new beginnings. Planning on visiting again. Hope this helps someone who is lost like I am. A church, a community center and a resource center all in one building. A very convenient location. The church, which is very unchurch-like, has programs for teens, toddlers and nursery care. All are welcome here ... just as you are. A Awesome church that helps people in need and supports the lgbtq community My home away from home. I  love Pastor Vance!!!

name: St. Joseph Cathedral - Downtown Columbus
St. Joseph Catholic Church - Fullerton Campus
reviewSummary:
My review will be a little long. It comes with love/ heart, honesty, and faith. Born catholic; would attend mass Sundays and a few events here and there.. not very involved. My love for Jesus started 4 years ago. Living testimony of Gods love and mercy: that’s another story. My miracle made me search for events in different churches. Did not want to commit to any. I will attend anything from worship nights, Holy Spirit nights, special healing masses, monthly priest talks, adoration, prayer, book readings, etc. In search of spiritual, emotional and physical healing and strength. That strength that Jesus gives me to overcome any life challenges and obstacles aimed my way was my miracle motivation and promise to attend 1 hour mass or pray.

One night Jesus had a plan for me; You can say a life lesson or purpose. I ended in an event hosted by St. Joseph Catholic Church. 3 days of that event and then after the event a light fellowship for the community. I purchased the guest book. Church volunteers were very welcoming and that’s where Jesus made his way. I attended a few group meetings. name: St. Joseph Catholic Church - Los Angeles (Downtown) Campus
reviewSummary:
I was asked to leave my own brother’s funeral service at church because my son, who has autism, was making noise. Being removed during such a painful moment made an already heartbreaking day even more difficult.
A so called priest asked us to leave.

Autism awareness matters everywhere, including in churches.

!
* Mark 10:14–16: Jesus became indignant when disciples turned children away, stating the kingdom belongs to them, then embraced and blessed them. Bells ringing eight times every weekend morning at odd hours is not tradition, it’s a nuisance to every neighbor within earshot. A little self-awareness goes a long way. It's absolutely not appropriate to remove a child from a church service simply for being noisy. We are often encouraged to help out in our congregation, but what are we supposed to do with our little ones in those moments? The church itself is very beautiful and the priest Rafael is amazing. He is speaks clearly also for the kids to understand the mass, he gives them examples. And what can I say he has everybody attentive during the mass due to his knowledge and he helping us get closer to god. Padre Rafael also goes for the Chivas de Guadalajara!  😊 Beautiful church, their Sunday mass has mariachis for music! Really fantastic! Also, father Rafael is a hoot. Gives great sermons and has a great sense of humor.

name: St. Joseph Catholic Church - Main Campus
reviewSummary: Beautiful historical church in Santa Ana. The community is very welcoming and the priest gives wonderful homilies in both English and Spanish. A cornerstone of the Downtown Santa Ana community. Very peaceful atmosphere and great parish support for families.

name: St. Joseph Catholic Church. - Pomona / Claremont Campus
St. Joseph Chaldean Catholic Church - El Cajon Campus
reviewSummary:
Let me start by saying this review is not about the church itself but specifically about the school and its staff.

My son started attending St. Joseph Preschool at the beginning of January. The first week went well but by the second week I started receiving complaints that he was “too active” and didn’t listen. Five weeks later the director Suzy asked me to reduce his schedule from five days to three because the teachers were unable to do the bare minimum and manage him. I declined due to my work as I occasionally help my husband and was also preparing to start a new job. The very next day they began sending me videos of my son running around while his teacher, Ms. Rita sat and did nothing and the TA Lindsey recorded him instead of redirecting him. I responded respectfully saying I would talk to my son but reducing his days was not an option.
Right after I sent that message she replied back saying that he was “not a good fit” and given two weeks for reevaluation. I was even told I should inform my new job “never mind” in case he couldn’t remain at the school. When I met with Suzy in person and asked what I could do to help she was not willing to work with me. When I asked what would happen if he improved during those two weeks (which he did) she sarcastically laughed in my face and said “maybe in the miracle of St. Joseph” instead of giving me some hope. During those 2 weeks 3 different teachers worked with my son and all of them told me he was doing well, listening, and behaving well. They did mention that he is active but also said that this is normal for kids his age and have kids who act worse than him in that school and specifically
in that class. These teachers were kind, professional, and clearly cared about the children. (You know who you are) I later found out from staff that Lindsey the TA  had been taking unnecessary pictures of my son and sending them to Suzy claiming he wasn’t cooperating even on days he was doing well. One teacher even confronted her about how unnecessary that was after it happened in front of her. What’s most frustrating is that the school refused to make any accommodations for my son, yet made adjustments for another child within just one week, even moving that child to a different class. Suzy and Roseann were extremely rude throughout this entire process. I reached out to Roseann and never received a response. On his last day she told me that he’s really not a good fit and was speaking to me with such a bad attitude as if I or my son did something bad to her. She also told me if I provided a doctor’s note explaining how to “handle” my son, they might consider taking him back. despite the fact that he is completely normal and simply active. They offended me in so many way on so many levels but I kept it calm just for my son to stay.  On his last day after they gave me all his stuff I also noticed that his pull-ups were barely used which shows that he wasn’t being properly changed throughout the day. It became very clear that this school is inconsistent and very very unprofessional. These people are in for the money. If you donate money for them they will take care of your child. It’s all about hookups!! There seems to be favoritism, and not all children are treated equally. After this happened I found out that a few parents have argued with Suzy and left because of her nasty attitude. My son was essentially removed for behaving like a typical 3 year old. Now my son is attending another school where he is thriving and receiving ZERO complaints. Sending my son to St. Joseph was the worst decision I made. I strongly recommend that parents reconsider enrolling their children here until major improvements are made in staff training, communication, and overall care. Otherwise, stay away from this place. This church new name is Saint Joseph Chaldean Catholic Church
Mass Times:

8:30 AM - Chaldean
10 AM - Arabic
12 PM - English I am giving them 4stars for this only reason which is: the secretary is an awesome person, very friendly and helpful and unusual in the Chaldean Catholic Churches!

Praying for this lady to be blessing for others🙏
Future projects: might build a charter school Amazing church.  Perish cancel members are amazing.  The priest father Philip is very friendly with the community. This was my meeting house when I was a kid. I think from 1995 to 2002. Always had a fond memory of the sacrament room, and the rock wall behind the pulpit.

name: St. Joseph Maronite Catholic Mission - Riverside Campus
reviewSummary:
Beautiful church and outstanding mass celebration. The priest was very friendly and welcoming to us, as it was our first time attending mass here. They have mass in Syriac and English on Tuesdays & Thursdays, and it was so easy to follow along. They have the liturgy in a book where you could follow along word for word. Definitely want to re-visit this beautiful church. And they’re in communion with Rome 🙏🏻 Mass every every morning at 9:00, Saturday at 5:30 pm and Sunday at 11:00 am
They have a gorgeous banquet hall available for rent any day of the week for great prices!! Honestly, everything here just feels right, you can feel God’s presence. It is very beautiful. God bless! Wonderful Church and wonderful people :) Father Fadi and his beautiful ❤️ wife Nicole are very welcoming as well as all the community at this lovely Church. The mass here is mixed English and Lebanese/Arabic. Come over and introduce yourself, get to know the parishioners and enjoy some of the food they prepare and sell after mass, delicious.. The Church ladies also cater Lebanese Mediterranean food, And u can rent out the hall for your special occasions and events. See you soon in God's will at this beautiful Church of Jesus 🙏🙏😍 Wonderful new church with a very friendly congregation of mosty Lebanese, Syrian, Jordanian, Iraqi, and Egyptian families. Mass is Sundays at 11 and lasts for 1 hour, everyone is welcome to join and discover this beautifully diverse community.  They host an exciting Lebanese cultural festival every year with great music and dancing, delicious Mediterranean/Lebanese food, and all kinds of activities. It's nice to have a church like this in Riverside so we don't have to drive to Orange county or LA or San Diego to gather with other Christian Arabs

name: St. Joseph’s Cathedral - San Diego (Downtown) Campus
reviewSummary:
Very beautiful, very holy, and very faithful church!  The priest had a great homily!  The parish is very active!  Without doubt I strongly recommend going to Saint Joseph’s Cathedral!  Know our Savior Jesus loves you and have a great day!❤️✝️🙏⚓️🕊️⛪️😃 Be careful walking down the stairs off of 3rd Ave entrance.  They are steep and numerous for the elderly. If you're not familiar with this church, you'll have no other choice but to use them.  Please know that there is a flat entrance on the 4th Ave side with  wheelchair access as well.

This is a beautiful, enormous cathedral! How sad. Visiting the area and wanted to stop in the church. I had not been back in 25 years. I paid for parking walked up to the front doors and found them locked at 2 o’clock in the afternoon. A man painting out front said that the church was closed. No signage indicating church hours. So I called the office and the recording said that the church was open Tuesday through Friday from 9 AM to 5 PM. I spoke to someone named father Peter Navarro and explained the situation and he really didn’t seem to care. All he said was where did you find out the information about the church hours and when I told him that it was on the recording all he said was that’s fine to know. Nothing else. Not exactly a very welcoming message to the faithful. It was a very beautiful Catholic cathedral. There are many  life size statues of many wonderful saints. There is also a new statue of Mother Teresa sank teresa and the Pope John it is gorgeous cathedral lovely lit and the acoustics are wonderful. For a mass today we had the I don't know how many pipes are in the Oregon but it's a big organ up in the loft and there was singing at the mass it was very spiritual. It reminded me of masses when I was a child absolutely lovely. There is a restroom and free parking. I love to come to mass here. It has the traditional church feeling. It's a beautiful church.

name: St. Kevork Armenian Church - Glendale Campus
reviewSummary: I have been going this church very long time, and I come here because I love this church, but the lady with black hair in the front who sells the candles, just insane. First of all, this is a church, anytime we enter there she either watching a serial or talking too loud that we cant even pray. This is a church, this not a place for entertainment. Beautiful and serene church ⛪️ I am sitting with my family and the lady with black hair is talking with people she knows and then when she went to next room she turned off the lights on us My favorite church the only church I go to I feel at peace over there it's a very nice and cozy spot very heartwarming people there and it's open every single p doors are wide open you could just walk in light a candle make a prayer very respectable place parking lot not too big but all right The best not the biggest but it's where I got married . Baptized both kids . God willing I will see there waddings in the same church & even my departure in the my end

name: St. Kieran Catholic Church - El Cajon Campus
reviewSummary:
I recently started attending St. Kieran, and I must say it is a wonderful place for prayer and reflection. The Mass is truly beautiful and conducted with great reverence, which creates a very peaceful and spiritual atmosphere.
The church itself is lovely and well-maintained. What I appreciate the most is the welcoming and serene environment—it's a perfect place for anyone looking for a quiet, holy space to connect with God. I highly recommend this parish to anyone in the El Cajon area looking for a meaningful and peaceful liturgical experience. My Family's church for many years, actually following the Word of God. Saint Kieran’s Catholic School is an amazing school. The principle Dr. Belcher and her staff are top notch. I highly recommend and commend their diligent effort towards the children’s progress from grades K- 8. This is a safe and caring environment where the kids are always number one! Beautiful service, nice church, great leadership in Father Ben and Deacon Frank.  That said, it is a clicky community and some people are treated like outsiders. We actually went for the open house for their school.  It was very nice, very clean and had some of the nicest people I have ever met.

name: St. Kilian Catholic Church
reviewSummary: A traditional Catholic parish in Mission Viejo offering liturgical worship and strong sacramental community.

name: St. Kilian Church
reviewSummary: A wonderful, warm, and highly supportive Catholic church. Mass is extremely reverent. Beautiful parish with fantastic priests and highly involved youth programs.

name: St. Lawrence Martyr Church - Redondo Beach Campus
reviewSummary:
Very welcoming and warm parish. We love celebrating Mass with this faith community. Beautiful cantors, inspiring sermons, friendly community. I’m visiting from the Caribbean and found this church and decided to attend Christmas Eve mass at 10pm. It was such an amazing experience. The choir was immaculate especially that hallelujah chorus sung at recessional. Beautiful pipe organ also. Homily was very well done. Just an overall amazing was to celebrate the miracle of Jesus’ birth. Large & beautiful Roman Catholic church located in Southwest Torrance (Prospect just north of PCH). Attended midnight (starts early @ 10 pm) Christmas Eve mass. Concelebrated service including full choir with instrumental accompaniment, thought provoking sermon and friendly congregation. A lovely way to celebrate the miracle of Christmas Lovely Mass, hospitable and friendly church members Beautiful neighborhood church and school with perpetual adoration chappel.
Very involved community that's welcoming. Monsignor Dotson knows everyone by name.
Come, be still with God in gratitude. The more you live in gratitude, the more you will be blessed with reasons to be grateful.

name: St. Lucy Catholic Church - Long Beach Campus
reviewSummary: This is a very nice community and modest looking church. Plenty of seating, clear sound amplification, bright lighting. Staff is friendly and accommodating. Rude!  I was looking for a church for my daughter’s quince and they completely shut me down because she didn’t have all her sacraments. I couldn’t enroll her ans honestly I wasn’t asking for anything for free and I know it’s a business so I’ll take my business elsewhere. Everyone went the extra mile, took the extra time and extra thought that really made the difference on our special day Great catholic church. Very welcoming to new comers. Great place to go and attend mass. A lot of Filipinos attend this church, they used to have Tagalog masses but not anymore. There are also Spanish masses, but most people generally attend English masses. They have indoor and outdoor mass, depends on the weather and restrictions of the state regarding COVID. People are respectful, they have different kinds of pastors, not just one. Sometimes they give out free hand sanitizers or free hand wipes. A lot of donations go to special charities. The church also is a school, so you know its a great church. 4/5 star rating.

name: St. Luke Lutheran Church - Woodland Hills Campus
reviewSummary: Such a amazing church. Great place to come to. Walk around it or just take a seat. A warm and welcoming congregation! The people are friendly, helpful and feel like family right away.  The pastor preaches beautifully, the music is truly gifted and the church sancutuary itself is a sweet peaceful place.  Classic all around. A welcoming church emphasizing love for people. Good meeting place with multiple rooms for groups. Kept very clean. The heater works very well in the winter though air circulation in summer is sort of poor. Boy Scout Troup has been having their meetings at thus church for 75 years! This church has been perfect hosts and we sincerely appreciate it.

name: St. Luke Lutheran Church, Claremont, CA - Pomona / Claremont Campus
reviewSummary:
Went here on Monday evening for a blood drive. This place is very faithful to allow the red Cross to come in and do blood drive so often. Lovely, small church with traditional service.  The sermons given by the pastor are very good, reflects his intelligence and compassion. A wonderful church. The pastor's sermons are truly inspiring! The members are welcoming and kind. The words of the Lord taught beautifully.    A beautiful small church.
The people are all warm and friendly. Warm caring church.  Gifted head pastor.

name: St. Luke Worship & Word Church - Long Beach Campus
reviewSummary:
My Paster is the best!!!!!
He has brought St. Luke a long way
I like his preaching because he takes the time to explain to where you walk away with understanding, he teaches the word.  Very approachable and kind the church is small but atmosphere is beautiful with friendly members I am a deacon at St Luke Holy Baptist Church. I enjoy the learnings and preaching of Dr. E. M. Williams!  He is a great minister to follow!   Continue to pray for him and come to our church to hear the word of the LORD! I had my dad homegoing Services here it's a beautiful church that has plenty of seating. A Home going was the occasion, the facility and its Attendees were Great. Very clean and we were well received by the Pastor and the Church Family. 💗 Blessed day and Awesome service 🙏

name: St. Luke's Anglican Church - Glendale Campus
reviewSummary: St. Luke’s Anglican Church is a community of faithful believers who hold fast to and faithfully teach the truth of scripture, while honoring the traditions and history of the church. At the same time, members there open their arms to welcome and bless those who enter their doors. Though my wife and I are active in another congregation, we always look forward to visiting St. Luke’s. If you do not have a church home, you might consider visiting and experiencing there what God will have for you. Well staffed, friendly, and easy to find Anglican (ACNA) congregation. Great musicians and accessible, knowledgeable, and personable priests. I came here for the first time, growing up Catholic. Everyone is very welcoming and wonderful, beyond belief. The service was also great, and the sermon very insightful. I like to think deeply about the scripture, and the pastor here certainly does. The Bible is very dense and he does a very good job dissecting the meaning, interpretation and translations of the words. Apart from that, everyone was great to meet and easy to get along with! Wonderful church, will return. Intimate, prayerful, come as you are  community took my family in and welcomed us as members immediately. So thankful for this group of faithful Christ followers. We found St. Luke’s to be such a warm and friendly congregation. We enjoy the embodied worship. The liturgy nourishes us each week. The climax of each service is Holy Communion (Eucharist)and it’s such a beautiful time to celebrate our union in Christ. So grateful to have found a church home.

name: St. Luke's Episcopal Church - Long Beach Campus
reviewSummary:
I was walking one night a few years ago around this neighborhood and this non drunk lady who was speeding at like 4 in the morning, SMASHED right into a parked car...

She apparently had a seizure, which is a spirit trying to renter it's original body by use of its supernatural teeth.

Since it was born in its body, it wants it back.

So it's trying to exile or exercise the demon that has replaced it.

Unfortunately, the demon didn't care about the laws of this land and decided that the other person's car wasn't of interest to her.

Some guy helped her push the car into action, and she "got away".
I would like four tacos, two piecea of yesterday's dinner look good though!

Go 99 cent store! This church is a terrible disappointment. My brother went here for a number of years and they let him down badly; he wanted purpose and they denied it to him. Then when he died I wanted help and they were utterly indifferent and didn’t give it to me; and not one person including a friend of his gave condolences when I told them of his death. This is the same church where I offered to design and pay for a sprinkler system for their neglected community garden about 3-4 years ago and was ignored. That whole church is rotten people. I use to go to a catholic church in Lomita, the catholic church itself does not align with any of my beliefs at all so I found this episcopal church on Google map and me leaving the catholic church permanently to become an Episcopalian was the best decision I've ever made, unlike catholicism, the episcopal church preaches about real life societal issues, and the Episcopal church (especially this church) is very inclusive, welcoming, loving, and caring towards everyone especially to the LGBTQIA+ community St Luke's is the best church I've been to. God bless you all Fantastic place for community, spirituality, and social activism. St. Luke's is blessed with two wonderful priests who make one dynamic duo. Love it! This is a place where EVERYONE is welcomed, and it's not just a nice line. Our Spanish service is growing and consolidating every month.

name: St. Luke's Episcopal Church - San Diego (Downtown) Campus
reviewSummary: We love St Luke's! It has a great community and support for whatever you're going through! Priests are very kind and welcoming and this is a good experience! Thursday food giveaway, amazing people and very clean. St. Luke's has been solace and inspiration to my friend David. I do not belong to this church, but if they ever need supporters to stand by them, I will do so. This is a church that walks the walk. Bless them. Very friendly and helpful. There is also an outreach site here for homeless people who have fallen in the hard times. They provide services such as a mailing address where you can pick up your mail, food and clothing distributed, several computers for use there. Many resources to help people get back on their feet. OPEN 9:00am till 1:00pm Monday THRU Friday. Best LIVE A.A. meeting open all week and I secretary weekends! Social distance in affect come share YOUR EXPERIENCE, Strength, and Hope, so others may benefit... Thanks and stay sober whatever it takes!..B.W.

name: St. Madeleine Catholic Church - Pomona / Claremont Campus
reviewSummary: St. Madeleine is full of peace. Father Manuel is a great priest. Love the worship during Sunday mass. God bless our church. If you mexican and grew up mexican in my opnion spanish session feels authentic more than english. Feeling peaceful whenever I come to this small church. Not too crowded as usual. I love this church, and the chapel 💓 it’s so peaceful 🙏🏼 Great church. We got married here. Deacon John, Father Bravo, Father Lima are caring for their community.

name: St. Margaret Mary Catholic Church - Chino Hills Campus
reviewSummary:
We attended the Saint Margaret Mary Catholic Church Car show today and had a great time-and what great cars! Friendly staff,beautiful location and lots of great people make this event a true blessing!

name: St. Mark's Episcopal Church - Glendale Campus
reviewSummary:
This Sunday, I was blessed to worship at Saint Mark’s Episcopal Church in Glendale (1020 N. Brand Blvd, Glendale, CA 91202). The morning sunlight poured gently through the stained glass, painting the sanctuary in hues of gold and rose. The choir lifted their voices in a harmony that felt angelic, drawing every heart into the presence of the Holy.

There’s something profoundly sacred about Saint Mark’s — a sense that generations of prayer still linger in the walls, that faith has been spoken and sung here long before us. Saint Mark, the Evangelist, reminds us that the Gospel is not just a story to be read, but a calling to be lived — to proclaim hope, to serve with love, and to move with urgency toward what is good and true.

My prayer this Sunday is for clarity and courage — that the Holy One would reveal truth where confusion reigns, and light where shadows still linger. I pray for all who labor quietly for justice, for those who refuse to hate even when hated, and for every soul longing to be seen and loved as they are. Especially, I lift up the LGBTQ+ community — may Gods protection and peace surround them always, and may every heart learn to see Their divine image in one another. Great, Welcoming Entrance.

There’s a little sign says come in light a candle have peace. That was very touching. The architecture is amazing high ceilings and amazing decorations. Very active with weekly programs. The style looks more like Scandinavian style but I’ve seen few pictures with Armenian writings which made me more welcomed. Great church to have in Glendale. I like this church so much it makes me feel in peace that's why I always visit it Fantastic church that is friendly and open to anyone without being too pushy. Beautiful and reverent Sunday services and many many opportunities to be involved in the community! Super creepy joker-looking, greasy haired guy clinging to the property who likes to hover and essentially promote negative energies if you're parked outside.
I wouldn't go inside if they keep something like that around, and allow it to feel the way it's showing itself off to be.

name: St. Martha Catholic Church - Murrieta Campus
reviewSummary:
Such a beautiful and welcoming church. The atmosphere feels very calm and meaningful, which makes every ceremony feel even more special. From a photographer’s perspective, the lighting and space are absolutely lovely to work with. Truly a great place for memorable moments. I first visited this church about nine years ago when I attended a wedding, and even then, it left a lasting impression on me. The atmosphere was warm, welcoming, and deeply reverent—perfect for such a meaningful occasion. The beauty of the church, both inside and out, added to the solemnity and joy of the ceremony.

Just this past Sunday, I had the opportunity to attend Mass there again, and I was reminded of how special this place truly is. The church continues to be well-maintained, organized, and inviting. The service was uplifting, and the message was delivered in a way that was both inspiring and easy to reflect on. The choir and overall sound during the Mass made the experience even more pleasant and engaging.

What stood out to me most is how consistent the church has remained over the years. It still provides a peaceful environment where people can come together, pray, and feel spiritually renewed. It’s clear that great care is taken in preserving not just the building, but also the sense of community and reverence that defines it.

I’m grateful to have returned and would highly recommend this church to anyone looking for a meaningful and enriching worship experience. This Church has lovely grounds and the people were great. The service was nice. I have to admit my bias for my love of traditional Church architecture. There is something awesome about hearing the choir above and beyond me during worship. Having said that, the worship was of a high caliber and you will not be disappointed. St. Martha. Is a beautiful church.

name: St. Mel Catholic Church - Woodland Hills Campus
reviewSummary: Just amazing 10/10 the Father is very good at explaining. Overall always an amazing mass. Glory to God! Proverbs 3:5 Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding; in all your ways acknowledge him and he will set your paths straight. Virgin Mary pray for us sinners As a wedding photo booth vendor in San Fernando Valley (Annnd...Action! Photo Booth), we had the pleasure to provide services to a bride and groom who got married in the church, then held their reception in the Msgr. Michael J. O'Connor Activities Hall. The hall is a large auditorium with a stage, canteen and large lobby. Triple sets of doors allow for excellent traffic flow and a way to create ambience with all doors open, or just the middle, or sides.  There are doors to the outside of the auditorium space making it very functional for all types of activities and vendors. Also, multiple ramps for ADA (or load-in) access. Lots of parking for your guests. Security on site is friendly and watchful. The space was clean and had natural light. Tons of potential!  Last, Julian at the church was lovely to deal with and answered all of our pre-event questions. We look forward to an opportunity to attend another event at St. Mel's and see how other brides and grooms will use the space. Where everyone is welcome. The people here are lovely and very welcoming. They have friendship Sunday Every week after the 9:00 and 11:00am service with donuts and coffee to help people network and meet others. This parish is clean, well maintained with several active ministries including a Knights of Columbus Council (pictured). Those I encountered here were friendly. I would definitely attend Mass here again if in the area. Best Church in the valley.  Everything about this place is beautiful; the church, the choir, the liturgy.  This place feels like home and you can tell the presence of God is here.  Father Steve’s homilies are always touching and thoughtful. I look forward to coming here every Sunday! Do be advised that depending on what time you go you will get a different experience when it comes to music.  Saturday nights and Sunday at 8 and 9:30am don’t have a choir and will have more modern music.  The 11am mass has the traditional hymns and a choir.  If you’re like me and prefer the traditional music you will want to go at 11am. Either way though you will be blessed by coming here! They also have a daily afternoon mass at 5:30pm which most parishes do not have.

Among the most revered of New Orleans historic landmarks is Old St. Patrick’s Church, a stunning example of the arts and crafts of another era. It stands in the heart of the business district and is one of the treasures that remains from early 19th century days when the city began moving outside the boundaries of Bienville’s original settlement, the French Quarter.It has been declared a National Historic Landmark by the Department of the Interior, setting it apart as a special American edifice of importance.Old St. Patrick’s lies in the 700 block of Camp Street in what was known as the American sector. It is one of the few historic and architecturally significant structures in and around Lafayette Square, once a grand park for residents and businessmen in the uptown side of the city across Canal Street from the Quarter. It was in this section that Americans built their homes and business establishments and distinguised their lifestyles from those of the Creoles residing in the original city limits.

At this tree-shaded patch of green (that remains today a respected urban open space in the Central Business District) cotton merchants, politicians and residents chatted. American ladies rested on benches, or strolled beneath their parasols pushing their baby buggies in much the same manner as the Creoles did along their Promenade Publique (now called Esplanade Ave.) in the Vieux Carre.

Aside from the magnificent Gallier Hall which served as City Hall until recent years, Old St. Patrick’s is the onlyearly landmark of distinction in the square area that still remains much as it did originally.

The church dates to 1840, but the parish was established in 1833, the first outside the boundaries of the original city. The first structure was a small wooden building at the site the church occupies today. Now the church is in the midst of a section in the business area that is surrounded by what was once a neighborhood of grand mansions and fine mercantile stores that were outfitted with the finest appointments. This whole area now is regaining its significance as an in-town area for housing and shopping rows. In the old days the section was known as Faubourg (suburb) St. Mary. It was here that St. Patrick’s was born out of necessity, and from an Irish determination to worship in the splendor and magnificence equal to the French in their grand St. Louis Cathedral.

For too long, they thought, good Catholic Irish immigrants squirmed in the rear pews of the Cathedral on Jackson Square where God appeared to speak only in French. Bishop Antoine Blanc observed this and he encouraged the construction of a small wooden church on Camp Street for the Irish. In a short time it was filled to overflowing at every Sunday Mass. The Irish then began building a grand church, one that would rival the Cathedral. And indeed, it did.

The Irish hired noted architects Charles and James Dakin to plan it. Construction began around the existing wooden church which was dismantled and carried out when the new edifice was completed.

The new church was of Gothic style in elegant details, with a ceiling imitating Exeter Cathedral. The tower is 185 feet high, the vestibule 40 feet, the nave 85 feet. It was a triumph in Gothic comparable to any parochial structure of its kind in Europe.

But there were construction problems in the swampy area. The foundation was found to be defective in part. So the church hired James Gallier, an Irish architect who came here in 1834, to complete the building. The walls of the tower were settling at one side. Gallier accomplished a remarkable feat of engineering skill. He removed the old foundation, replacing it with a new one, without pulling down the walls. This lovely historic cathedral is easily accessible from Canal Street and the French Quarter. Beautiful church inside and out. We went Sunday for the Latin mass.
