Several amenities and hosptiable services are available, even a coffee bar for those who into that kinda thing. Come ine, come all. You are welcome! I spent multiple years at Walnut Creek Church. It was the church that God used to reveal the Gospel to me and save my soul a little more than 2 years ago! Although I'm no longer in Des Moines, I truly miss this church! The community there, the Biblically sound teaching, and EVERY aspect of what this church does truly shows the Gospel! I started attending Walnut Creek Church when I came to Grand View University, and it’s been a huge part of my faith journey. Over the past three years, I’ve grown so much in my walk with the Lord thanks to the solid biblical teaching, strong community, and focus on discipleship. The people here are welcoming, and the leadership is passionate about helping others grow in their faith. So thankful for this church! We attended one of their services. Our son, who is gay and 32 years old, told me during the sermon, you do understand they are preaching hate. I told him I was sorry and that we would never attend this church again I was so embarrassed and felt so bad for him. I got connected to Walnut Creek Church Downtown seven years ago while my brother was attending. I then began attending Drake University and immediately knew that Walnut Creek and their college ministry Campus Fellowship was the right fit for me. Walnut Creek values students in their church and certainly will make any future college student  feel right at home!

Straight from the BIBLE Great place to worship Enjoyed the visit

name: Walnut Creek Presbyterian Church - Walnut Creek Campus
reviewSummary:
The spirit is definitely felt here. For those that want to increase their faith in Jesus should definitely give this church a visit. Also a great school to send your little ones. Very disappointing.  We were in the process of looking for a new church home closer to where we live.   We'd attended WCPC multiple times over the past 30 years so were familiar with it.  I had hoped that after they had left the Presbyterian Church USA that they would return to being more biblical rather than worldly.   Unfortunately this isn't the case.  Durning a recent service the associate pastor started the service by expressing her political views, which were predictably based only on what the media told her to believe.  The lead pastor followed suit expressing views likewise based on the popular press rather than biblical truths, let alone any serious attempt to even the learn actual facts. They should remember that Jesus himself did not  advocate 'revolution' against the ruling Romans, violent protest, or in fact any opposition to the occupying Romans.  In fact one reason the Jews of the time rejected him was his refusal to engage in opposition to Roman rule.

Many people want to church to reinforce their worldly views at chuch.  The simple fact is that much of what modern culture exhalts is in conflict with God's teachings.  Churches are there to guide you on God's unchanging, unerring, intended path; not to support or follow the world's ever shifting beliefs.

The only reason I don't give them zero is that they have nice facilities and the people attending are nice. I honestly do not know what to make of our current churches, who calibrate their theology and level of immersion into the world, leaving us to shop around for the perfect permutation.  We try one on and move on when things don't fit just right.  With so many Presbyterian denominations, it seems we will never run out of choices.

I do miss the mainline PC(USA) denomination and what it represented in years past.  What a magnificent institution it was, and what a deep history it carried.  We were told that the Presbyterian Church was a large tent when sinfulness came and was given a place at the table.  Some stayed.  Conservative congregations made the difficult decision to leave.

This church left.  To what end, however?  I read the comments from the review written 3 months ago and many of the points resonate.  A heavy cost was paid to leave the denomination. PC(USA) does not make it easy for congregations who want to leave the denomination but also want to worship in the same building as they always have.  What was the point of schism and the financial sacrifice of the faithful, only to see this church on a parallel path to the trajectory of the PC(USA)?

I do wonder if God's will is in this fragmentation and with our local churches mirroring the city.  Was the judgment upon Babel also its blessing?  Tim Keller's notion of our call to the city was an appealing one, especially among the young and accomplished.  I thought it should have had an equal counterbalance of a call to the wilderness.  Do we go into the city to conquer and to serve, or do we go to there to seek the comfort offered within its walls and to fill up our stores of resources and memories of good times?  Life in Walnut Creek stirs us to do the latter.  We like a nice sunny afternoon to walk through Nordstrom's and have a nice lunch at an outside table, don't we?

As much as we can be critical of Walnut Creek Presbyterian Church, do other churches do better?  The cynic in me says all churches are flawed, and it is simply the age we live in.  These institutions may not carry the full and fearsome voice of the Word, but they serve the purpose of carrying the embers forward.  I think of the centuries between books of the Bible, and even in the books themselves, where He seems silent but where His plan is clearly present.  Maybe we, in this present time, need to just keep things as steady as we can, and Presbyterians of another age, with lamps full of oil, will do the work we could not.

On some Sundays, it does look like some manner of elaborate cosplay.  Of the most banal type, in short sleeves and khakis, with rapturous descriptions of bourbon and Broadway musicals at the pulpit.  (To be fair, the pulpit may be in the storage room now.)  I offer the critique of one atheist: Grown men and women should not carry on having imaginary friends.  Who among us will leave the make-believe of our creation and step forward with fear and trembling?  Who? I absolutely loved the sermon. Pastor Bart was really strait forward and made every part of his works count thanks Pastor Bart. I couldn't be happier with the preschool here. My daughter loves going and the teachers are top notch and passionate about teaching and caring for the kids. The classrooms are modern, clean, and well supplied. I haven't yet attended a church service here but definitely look forward to it in the near future!

name: Washington National Cathedral - Washington Campus
reviewSummary:
Stunning stained glass! It's worth going to see the architecture and stained glass. Go on a tour if you can to get insider information. The 7th floor observatory was worth it as there are great views. I went during the week, and in between school tours, it was quiet. I was dropped off my an Uber at a round a out and had to go to the right for the main entrance, which was clearly marked from where I was. The gardens outside were also nice. Of all the places we've been on vacation, this one tops the list. Even if you're not religious, there's something here for you, physically, spiritually. It's an awe inspiring place, that truly stirs the soul. The craftsmanship that went into building and maintaining this space is impressive. Every nook and cranny has some story to tell out a little secret to be revealed, if you're just willing to look for it. This is a place for EVERYONE, regardless of what you look like, where you come from, or whom you love. I only wish more places embodied that same spirit. After-hours tour (June-August).  Take a guided tour of the bell tower, 333 steps.  Informed guides and interesting facts.  Beautiful overlook of the city. A view of the Nave and Bishop's Garden is also worth visiting. Absolutely beautiful, tons of history, terrific tour guide (Chris who has worked there 31 years!). I reminded my family that this is a privately funded facility and the Cathedral is an Episcopal church.  Then everything made sense.  We are Roman Catholic and so, my kids asked some questions about the "pride flags".
We really enjoyed taking our time to look at all of the architecture, stained glass windows, sculptures, stone work, iron work, etc... We especially liked the different chapels, the information about the restoration of the organ, and extraordinary iron gate near the front of the cathedral with roses, other flowers, and the head of a butterfly. Washington National Cathedral is truly a wonderful place to visit.

Visiting here is a deeply rewarding experience. Every stone and architectural detail of the cathedral carries history and stories. For visitors who appreciate history or religion, it is absolutely worth exploring slowly and carefully.

From the observation level on the 7th floor, you can enjoy a stunning 360-degree panoramic view of Washington D.C., Virginia, and Maryland. Along the corridors, informational displays help explain what you are seeing, making the scenery more meaningful and engaging.

The gardens are beautifully and carefully maintained.

At sunset, the white stone exterior is softly covered with a golden glow, giving the cathedral an even more sacred and peaceful appearance.

Overall, it is a place that inspires both reflection and appreciation.

name: Washington, DC International Christian Church - Washington Campus
reviewSummary:
This church is an AMAZING place! Please do not let the bad reviews persuade you to not come! The church is SOOO good and the people are SOOO nice!  I can tell that God is fully in the spirit of the church and that they have great intentions! They love people so much and are willing to meet people no matter what they are going through to be a blessing! It is really hard finding places that encourage you and help you grow and take time eagerly out of their schedule to do it!

You will not regret going here! This church has changed my life A LOT! They love people like the love of the lord! I typically have a really busy schedule, and they are SOOO good that I wanted to create this review before I go to sleep! Please come. Please see for yourself what this church is like. We only live once on this earth. As some mentioned, please do some research on International Christian Church and its founder Thomas Wayne "Kip" McKean II. Very similar practices as Church of Christ. They put a lot of emphasis on the controversial doctrine of water baptism as a requirement for salvation. Their teachings make you believe they are the only church that is the true church and all other churches are false and congregation members cannot go to other churches. If you are already a Christian you will be taught to be all wrong in the past and must be baptized again in their church. If you are from a Christian family you will be taught to leave your family and previous church, otherwise you are not true Christian and will not be saved. Sounds like a cult practice. This is the best church EVER! Wonderful service with everyone singing along, powerful preaching from the bible, and awesome fellowship with people that are all truely giving their all to emulate Jesus' heart 100% of the time; not just on Sundays. I moved to DC region from central NY 9 years ago to start this wonderful church group and have been here ever since! If you come here, your life will change for the better, if you want to be changed and become a true disciple of Jesus Christ. This church not only saved my life 4 years ago but also restored to me the joy of my salvation, after choosing sin and drifting away from God for over a year! The family, the fellowship, the love, the evangelism, the world vision, the fun, the preaching, and especially the dynamic personal bible studies have all inspired me to love God with all my heart, soul, mind, and strength. I thank God for this church! This is a great church. The people are super friendly. The testimonies given during service are so powerful; they are so open and vulnerable about their lives. It helps me to know I’m not alone in my struggles. They teach solely from the Bible, not from their own personal opinions.

name: Water of Life Community Church - Ontario Campus
reviewSummary:
Been attending wol for about 10 years. It’s
Not the same with Dan gone. Shane tries but so many including myself feel lost when he preaches. It’s hard for me to say this because I know that’s Dan’s son. I pray it gets better. Bible teaching. Many other classes and Bible studies. I would send anyone new to the faith or needing a new church to give it a try. My personal tribute to Former Assistant Pastor Bob Bryant - Water of Life Church

Back around 2016 I had this kind of prophetic message to give to the Water of Life Community Church of Fontana, so I wrote it on a piece of paper and went to this church and ended up being met by Assistant Pastor Bob Bryant. I have only had a few of these messages in my life to give to churches and all other churches either kicked me out, locked their doors, sent security after me or yelled at me at the top of their lungs. Not Bob Bryant though. He was different. He heard me out, then he took out his phone and looked up some of the shared scriptures and said that he would keep my message in mind. I was actually surprised of how positive he was about it, as my church prophetic messages in the past have never been anything to be taken lightly, as they were always kind of chastising in a way, yet only by words, so don't worry.

Lately I have been talking to someone who is in the area of where the church is located, so I decided to see if I could give a recommendation of a local church in that area, since no churches are perfect, and the fact that Assistant Pastor Bob Bryant still made feel that if I ever chose to become a member of this church that I would still be welcome there.

Lyrics though on the radio as I just now find out of the death of former Assistant Pastor Bob Bryant, as I shed a few tears from hearing the news of his passing --- "I'm runnin' out of faith, I see the future I pictured slowly fade away, and when the tears of pain and heartache are pouring down my face, I find my peace in Jesus' name."

I decide to then find out more details regarding the circumstances surrounding his death back in 2020 and these next lyrics on the radio catch my attention:

"...Why are you crying?
Let me lift up your face
Just don't turn away..."

Someone on the radio just said - "My father passed away last year, so I went straight to Him and to the music for encouragement."

Lyrics on the radio as I nearly  finalize this review - "...everything is different nowadays. I lost a few ones along the way. I had to learn to trust it'll be okay, it'll be okay."

Then the next song - "He will come and wipe our tears away. No more fear. No more pain. No more sorrow, sin or shame. The King is coming back again. A reign of love that will never end."

I tried to see if any of the reviews here happened to mention him by name, yet nothing. Well here is a review for you Assistant Pastor Bob Bryant. 5 stars for the first impression that you gave. I'm sorry to hear of so much negativity found online regarding the circumstances of your death.

--- "Nobody is perfect, not a one is good. Only God is good. Rest in peace my friend." --- Google says: This message is highly biblically sound and rooted in key scriptures. It reflects the theological truth that all humans are sinful by nature (Romans 3:10, 3:23) and that God is the only absolute standard of goodness, as stated by Jesus in Mark 10:18, "No one is good—except God alone"

Google also says: This message is strongly rooted in Biblical theology, specifically regarding human nature and God's holiness. The statement aligns with scripture that emphasizes humanity's sinfulness and the unique, perfect goodness of God, primarily echoing Mark 10:18 (and Luke 18:19) where Jesus states, "No one is good—except God alone," and Romans 3:10, which says, "None is righteous, no, not one."

--- Keep the faith ---

In the Bible, "keeping the faith" means maintaining unwavering trust in God, adhering to biblical truth, and enduring spiritually despite challenges or persecution. It signifies holding fast to the gospel of Jesus Christ, as Paul did (2 Timothy 4:7), to finish one's spiritual journey with steadfast commitment and obedience.

Key Aspects of "Keep the Faith"

Perseverance & Endurance: It is a lifelong commitment to stay faithful, enduring hardships and not giving up on God’s promises.

Keeping the faith is viewed as a dynamic, "worked" response to God's love, aimed at enduring through the end of one's life. This church is the bees knees.
Big & beautiful.
I'm new round here but I use to come way back in the day & I luved & miss Pastor Dan.
Joel Sanchez is their best pastor now & I wished he was there more frequently. A lot to offer depending on what you are looking for. From kids programs, prayer, healing classes, adult ministry school and a k-8th school. Weekend services are excellent. Come early however as on-site parking fills up fast and then off-site parking is the place to go.

name: Water of Life Community Church - Rancho Cucamonga Campus
reviewSummary:
Been attending wol for about 10 years. It’s
Not the same with Dan gone. Shane tries but so many including myself feel lost when he preaches. It’s hard for me to say this because I know that’s Dan’s son. I pray it gets better. I wish like many others pastor Joel would preach more than just once a every other month or if lucky once a month. He is so good and really breaks the message down so well. It not only blesses me but also my teen boys who really stay engaged when he preaches. Please Shane let Pastor Joel have more opportunity. God will raise you up for doing so. Or maybe let him preach every Saturday night. Thanks for your consideration. Wonderful non denominational church. Loving staff and always holy spirit led. Message is always amazing and on point. Bible teaching. Many other classes and Bible studies. I would send anyone new to the faith or needing a new church to give it a try. name: Water of Life Community Church: Upland - Ontario Campus
reviewSummary:
No offense to any1 but this guy is the best pastor around.
Sure the Fontana campus is nice & big but if he ain't cooking then we ain't having a good church day.
On God fr fr I love this little church. I was introduced to the one in Fontana, which I love also but this one is just right down the street five minutes away. I really enjoyed coming to this church.❤️ They are never there to help their own.
They do have part of city link , which helps only uh fontana Residence.
And the upland facility it's only in video.
Because pastor Dan wants to keep all the MILLIONS HE MAKES within his family. If you want to lean, feel, and experience God, this is the church you been looking for.
Great community of believers, ready to partner with you in your journey. Lots of different ways to learn skills to grow in your knowledge of the word and God’s love for you. Yes God is crazy about you, that NONE should perish NONE.
Hope you can make it. There’s a seat always waiting For You!,,...and a brother or sister to embrace you and welcome you!! I have been a member of Water of Life for about 7 years. I love this Church because I feel welcomed, loved, encouraged,  and blessed to be a part of such an amazing group of God’s people! Pastor Dan is everything I want and and need in a Pastor! He is down to earth, honest, talks about the things that are going on in the real world and how to deal with that as Christians. He teaches from the Bible and makes it relevant to my life. Pastor Dan teaches me how to be a better Christian!! If you are looking for a place to worship give Water of Life a try; you have nothing to loose and so much to gain!!

name: Water's Edge Church - Encinitas Campus
reviewSummary: What a great church in so many ways! My family has visited many churches before happily settling in with Water’s Edge because it was easy to feel at home. It’s plain to see that the Lord is working through Andy during his talks. He has a way of getting to the heart of the Bible in a way listeners can relate. You’ll find vulnerability, challenging and stimulating talks, a sense of family and close community, openness and comfort. No judgments here, just people hungry for the Word. Kids ministry is also amazing with Deb’s wonderful age-appropriate talks about Jesus and the Bible. This is the first time my two kiddos have truly enjoyed church…and received sound teachings! Water's Edge Church is the house-church-family experience that is Jesus-led and Spirit-filled & less about the entertainment or special programs. This church balances being close-knit & doing "life-together" with being so welcoming and warm to new people coming in the doors. There is an honest heart for people who need authentic community, healing, mercy, or just a warm meal or help with their kids! I love that we have people of all ages and walks of life coming together for the sole purpose of hearing and responding to God's voice. It's a come-as-you-are kind of place. I love being part of Water's Edge! It is a strong community of people who share life together, who are real with each other. Kids are valued and welcomed into this community. They know they are loved. There is an honest heart of all of God's people, both inside and outside the church. You see this in how they serve each other and serve the community. My heart is full. This is a great place to belong! The Water’s Edge Church is not like any other church I’ve been apart of. They keep each week fresh by changing up the format of the gatherings. Water’s Edge Church and it’s members are like family and friends, they care for one another just like you would care for your family and dearest friends. There are many family’s with young children, and the way the church focuses on loving and ministering to the children is beautiful (and I love that they break up the youth program to developmentally appropriate segments for the children, my children look forward to going to church each week). Water's Edge church exhibits the best of what it means to be like Jesus. They love their community, both within the church walls and outside, so well. Andy, the lead pastor, brings the Word and is accesible to his WE Crew. Would recommend this church to anyone looking for home.

name: Watermark Community Church
reviewSummary: Famous for its 'Authentic' and high-commitment culture (Regeneration, Membership). Teaching is 'Expository' and 'Uncompromising'. A massive hub for 'Young Adults' and professionals in Dallas. The 'Porch' ministry is a frequent entry point.

name: Watermark Community Church - Dallas Campus
reviewSummary:
I am not shocked to know I was not the only believer rejected of being baptized in the name of Jesus because in their eyes I was a “sinner” living with my fiance before actually being married by the court of law. My new church in Cedar Hill named Trinity Church, welcomed me and my family with open arms and open hearts without judgment and sent all of 4 us (Husband, me and 2 children) an INVITATION to be baptized without a QUESTIONNAIRE nor an interrogation!! I’ve come to realize Watermark is not truly the welcoming, loving church they claim to be. They make it about their rules and qualifications instead of our One on One personal relationship with our Savior Jesus. Who are they to tell me I can’t be baptized because I am living in sin? Honestly not a place I would tend to leave a review but was in town for work and stopped here often as it was in close proximity. Beautiful well cared for grounds and architecture. Great work space and coffee shop. From staff to what they do I was all pleasant to surprised. If it’s not your thing don’t worry but worth a peak for sure! Cheers !! I enjoy this church a lot. Most of the pastors and what they teach are great; they make things understandable, relatable, and enjoyable. However, I wish there were fewer arrogant people and staff, but people like that are everywhere. But overall it’s a great place to learn and grow in faith as a Christian. My wife and I visited while we were in Dallas and we enjoyed worshiping God here. The Gospel was preached and I enjoyed hearing it. We spoke with someone at the welcome desk, but unfortunately I do not remember his name. He was very helpful and answered so many questions. This is likely to be our home church when we move to Dallas next summer. Yes, it's a mega church, BUT I always feel welcome. Their leadership is refreshing and God honoring; their messages will challenge you and encourage you; and their worship is Christ centered.

They have a connect center where you can get plugged into a small group and find community.

They also have a ministry for young adults called The Porch that meets every Tuesday night at 7pm.

They have a small "coffee shop" that's open throughout the week in the main lobby. Great place to hang out.

name: Watermark Fellowship Church - Chino Hills Campus
reviewSummary: I attended this church due to a friend of mine doing a sermon here on evangelism. Upon arrival I was greeted with friendly faces and a warmth I had never experienced at other churches. It has now been three years here and I am now a proud member of this church. It is a church that is focused on disciple-making, teaching, and solid biblical exegesis. It is a reformed Baptist church that teaches and applies the Bible to everyday life. We are small, but we have a children's ministry, youth ministry, and we host lifegroups as well. We host a BSF group here and we also allow two other churches to rent out our facilities. Pastor Alan is a great pastor who graduated from the Master's Seminary (associated with pastor John MacArthur). Being here is like being part of a family and I am so grateful to God that He led me here. Friendly! Nice !

name: Watermark South Dallas
Watershed Charlotte - Charlotte Campus
reviewSummary:
If your looking for a church of GOD this is not. Endured 20 minutes of their service and head them preach gods word once. Also learned this is a place for LBGQ and like minded individuals. If your seeking the lord this is not it. My child after leaving (mind you she is 9) told me they introduced themselves to the class they were in and were asked if they had any pronouns they went by. Look do what you will with my post just informing others so your not as surprised as I was because there was nothing there that made me feel like the lord was with us there. Cause I was praying!!! Watershed Charlotte is a Church for the sojourner. Wherever you are on your spiritual walk You are welcome in this community.
I said, when I left my last church, I would never join another church, but from the first moment I stepped in the building i've been drawn to this community. And for however long I am blessed to be with them I'm grateful to be here. a church for imperfect people trying to figure this whole thing out on this spinning rock. has made me think more about my faith journey these past 6 months than i have in a decade.

the cherry on top is how engaged they are in the community. can’t ask for a better spiritual home and people to share that with.

it’s unique, which is why we drive from concord to attend and volunteer! Attended a new church Watershed Charlotte today.

Let me begin with saying I have been searching for an intimate and smaller church that is dedicated to accept everyone with Grace and Compassion.

The praise team was excellent and the people welcoming me as a newcomer were very kind, gentle and loving!

Cedric Lundy was the speaker and the man spoke from his heart. I have been inspired because since finding my way back to our one true Shepherd I have endured pain and pray for broken relationships to heal. I just want to keep giving my heart to our God!

From giving my life back to the one true king I know with all my heart we are His people , the sheep of His Pasture. 🐑🙏 My family and I attended Watershed Church for the first time and we were instantly sure that we will be back. We’ve been searching for a church home since we moved to Charlotte last year and after our experience yesterday, I feel like we may have found it.

Every person we came in contact with was welcoming, kind, helpful, and seemed genuinely committed to making our first-time visit a good one. The sermon was so well done: engaging, conversational, authentic and exactly what I needed to hear in that moment. Our kids absolutely loved the children’s ministry; they made connections, had so much fun, and all 3 of them walked away begging to come back next week.

To be able to worship in a place that is not only progressive, but affirming and inclusive to ALL is exactly what we have been searching for and I feel so hopeful that Watershed is it. If you’re looking for a church where you can come as you are and feel not only accepted, but celebrated: then you’ve found it.

name: Waterway Christian Church - Bentonville Campus
reviewSummary: Awesome place and loving community, they let our group of 30youth crash on their floor and even fed. If you’re looking for community in Bentonville you should check them out. For anyone looking for a place to be affirmed and accepted with the Love of God, this is that place! Love the people. Inclusive atmosphere. Love this place! Great church!

name: Watson Grove Baptist Church - Nashville Campus
reviewSummary: I visited Watson Grove on Sunday (9/28) at the Nashville campus and I’m very glad I did. I arrived to service about 30 minutes late but I was still greeted with like an old friend or family member. The people are super friendly here. Pastor Faison is a phenomenal preacher and teacher! His voice reminds me of former BET News journalist Tavis Smiley but his preaching styles reminds me a lot of my pastor, Dr. Marcus D. Cosby. I was in Nashville to visit my daughter who is a student at Tennessee State University. We normally visit Mt. Zion MBC but I asked my daughter to plan the weekend for me and her Granny and she told me she wanted to go to Watson Grove. I was a little disappointed at first because I love Bishop Walker and the Mt. Zion family but I really enjoyed myself at the Grove!!! The men’s choir sang Victory is Mine by Commissioned. They had my attention right there. I will continue to follow The Grove online and can’t wait to worship them the next time I’m in Nashville. I’ve been a member of this church for almost a year now, the pastor is great, he does a good job explaining the word. This past Sunday it was a bit hard for me to focus due to a greeter asking for my water bottle and saying “You can not drink in the sanctuary.” I thought she was being funny so I laughed and walked passed her, she then came from behind me & repeated it and asked for my water bottle & told me I can get it after service. I was confused by this but continued to go inside for service. I’m not sure who the “No drinking in the sanctuary” applies to because the pastor had a water bottle on hand & a few others who sit behind him as well. This was just so weird to me, to basically get chased down for a bottle of water. Beautiful church! What a wonderful experience on my first visit to the Grove. The message was on time and much needed. I enjoyed the delivery and how the pastor walked through the scripture. I look forward to my next visit, but I will also tune in virtually. I definitely recommend this church to visitors and locals looking for a church home. We attended on Ugly Sweater Day.  The pastor recognized all of the 'UGLY' attendants. My Husband  and I were visiting our kids who are members of this Church and they invited us to  worship with them and It was Truly a Blessing  that We received!! I promise When ever we're visiting the kids we will most definitely be returning!! May God continue to Bless the Pastor and his Family !! I Pray your Strength in the Lord!!

name: Waxhaw Campus
reviewSummary: One of the most beautiful and welcoming Catholic parishes in the country. The liturgy is incredibly reverent. A wonderful faith family. Mass is always uplifting, especially the choir.

name: WAY CHURCH - Aliso Viejo Campus
reviewSummary:
Amazing church! Great people there. Awesome worship. Loved getting to experience a service here. Powerful leadership and preaching and the volunteers and staff were very friendly and welcoming. I highly recommend checking out this place if you are looking to get plugged into a local church. I have never felt so welcomed at a church! Everyone was so welcoming and went out of their way to introduce themselves and get to know me. The worship is amazing and the Holy spirit was moving in the space and through the Pastor as he spoke! I highly recommend coming to check out what they are doing! amazing church filled with amazing, loving, kind people who love to connect with others! From the moment my family and I walked in we felt welcomed.  The kids ministry is awesome! My 6yr old loves it! we love Resound OC and are so thankful to be apart of it!♥️ This church community is pretty special...they are totally our family! Authentic relationship is at the base of all they do...naturally their gatherings reflect that. Great worship and word based message every time but gee this congregation will genuinely walk with you! This church is phenomenal. Throughout my life I’ve explored multitudes of churches from all over the country. After being raised in the church from a very young age, I’d developed a certain amount of jaded expectations in association with certain places of worship. In my latter years, I shied entirely away from church because nearly every one I encountered gave off an impression of shallowness or insincerity which turned me off entirely from the idea of church.

On Christmas Eve, I attended my first Resound service, and I’ve been coming back ever since. There is something incredible and wholehearted about the manner and energy in which the Reid’s  conduct their services that for the first time since I was a little girl has me EXCITED about church and the people I will meet. The space they’ve facilitated, their personal story, and their gift of connecting with people is truly unlike any church I’ve been to before and I feel right at home with Resound. Highly highly recommend!!!

name: Way Church - Nashville Campus
reviewSummary:
My daughter and I came down from Ohio for a weekend in Nashville. She had heard about this church, so we attended this morning. It was the best thing about our trip! Excellent praise and worship music, and sound, Biblical preaching. Any future Sunday mornings we spend in Nashville will find us at Way Church! We visited Way Church on MLK wkend in Jan 2026 with our young friends and it was a wonderful experience!!  I LOVED the message from the young pastor and he can RELATE to the young folks of today and the unbelievable challenges that are faced with in today's  broken world.  I loved my visit so much that I found his previous sermons on YouTube and shared some of them with our local High School Principal as a possibility to show in the Chapel for their students. I then shared it with all of my own adult kids and their friends....his message is short & sweet and makes the point of what God has in store for them!!  I've also shared Way Church's info with some of my friends who have adult kids currently working and living in Nashville!  We will definitely be back!!! I tried this church out for the first time. Despite the fact there were signs saying put your car hazards on for first time guests, nobody helped me or told me where to go. The worship had blinding lights shining directly into my eyes for half of it, I just found myself looking down at the floor. Couldn’t focus on the music at all. There was also an uncomfortable amount of people with DSLRs walking around taking photos during worship and the sermon. I obviously know media team is a regular thing in modern church culture, however this felt like it was a movie set trying to get the right shots. Everything felt staged. Nothing felt genuine. Will probably not return. Way Church has been such an answer to prayer for my wife and I. We were new to Nashville with no community and were church hopping to try to find a home. When we found Way Church, we were welcomed by everyone we met and then made the decision to go to Way Track, start serving, and get plugged into a Way Group. Both of those decisions have changed our lives!

Pastor Noah preaches from the Bible and isn’t afraid to say the parts that others shrink from. Way Church is a place where you can find community, become more like Jesus, and help make Nashville look like Heaven! The worship is maybe one of the best I’ve experienced in my life. Really enjoyed a great gospel message. The people were so friendly and welcoming.

name: Way Family Church - Edmond Campus
reviewSummary:
"The Way" is a nondenominational Christian church which embraces people from every walk of life.
Pastors Josh and Lindsey are all about pointing people to Jesus, and hosting His presence.
We believe the bible is the inerrant Word of God. The Way Church people are welcoming, friendly, and caring.  The praise & worship is beautiful, and absolutely wonderful at leading us into the presence of The Lord.  The Holy Spirit is in this place!

If you are looking for a church home, you found it!  You don't have to believe to belong, and you don't have to "clean yourself up first"... everyone is welcome. Come as you are and see for yourself! This is truly a family of God. It is a place that focuses on Jesus.  Teaching scripture  by removing the falsehood that humans have put on teachings. The atmosphere is one of embrace and love no matter what walk of life you come from. You instantly feel welcomed and the Vail of hypocrisy is removed and no one expects anyone to be perfect rather working together through friendship and teamwork to build up. Doing life together is strong in this church and teaching how to do that not just on Sunday but even a fraction of each and every day and blooming from that start. We've been looking for a new Church family. We found that the mega style churches are not for us. Pastors who have no time and wouldn't be able to tell you apart from.any other stranger.  So as so many we just stopped attempting and slapping bandaids on with online services. I truly believe the Holy Spirit brought us here. I don't believe in coincidences so decided to go with it.
I can say we found our new Church family.
Thank you, see you next week. The Way Church is a rare gem. I immediately felt like family when I stepped through the doors! The worship is pure, and the true gospel is preached! If you’re looking for a place where Jesus is honored and the center of it all, this is the place for you!!! I’ll be back anytime I’m in the OKC vicinity. First time here seen a free haircut and school supplies sign it brought me right on in my son was well taking care of I did not have money cuz I'm moving and the moving expenses is breaking my pockets so this was a gift from God I love the energy here such sweet people I was also invited to the services sadly I have a home church but I am thinking of coming on Wednesday we will see what the future holds

name: Way Of Grace Bible Church - Rancho Cordova Campus
reviewSummary:
I have grown a lot at this Church, This church reflects the love of Christ in both word and action. People from different backgrounds, cultures, and ages, worshipping together in unity, and everyone is treated with dignity and respect. From the moment you walk in, you can feel genuine love—not judgment. There’s no perfect church but I can say Pastor Adrian and Elder Mike cares for the flock. I still think alot about the 1:30pm service.  I went to this church for about 7 year. I gained alot of bitterness being at this place but always hoped that because the preaching sounded good that some how that would make up the difference. At first it had a family vibe, but as time went on I started getting a different vibe. I was just someone to carry rules  and create distance. I felt more condemnation then love, and that I should not some how trust my own awareness of what was taken place at the time. I was building up my family, but the teaching ended up being to burdensome. My family is more of a mess now, and the people there would pray for us at a distance. True gospel preaching with no punches pulled, this isn't just a "Church" it's a family!  Food and fellowship after service on a Sunday, womens and mens hermeneutics classes, bibles studies, and they take special care of young ones!

People do come and go from the Church, and for all those who have left, when they visit it is with open arms and a happy heart to see them.  Way Of Grace, as with any true Church, will give you back in droves what you put into it.

Over the years these brothers and sisters are my friends, my family, my community.  If you want to hear true Gospel preaching that won't coddle you, won't belittle you, won't denigrate you, come and see us, break bread with us, worship Christ with us. Excellent bible teaching ministry! I feel so uplifted and educated from Gods word through this young preacher. Praying for the protection of this ministry, the minister and his family and the kind folks who attend. This congregation keeps it simple and powerful! For the best experience, bring a couple pieces of gum/candy, bring your bible and prepare to flip pages and respond to the ministers questions! Love the word here at Way of Grace. Pastor Adrian and Amber I miss you and the family. Although I'm in Texas I still enjoy receiving the word preached. Way of Grace is still my church home. May the Lord bless and prosper each one to grow spiritually, mentally, physically.  Much love in Jesus Christ.

name: Way of Life Church
reviewSummary:
Wow! About a year ago I was introduce to the most powerful church where I became a member & enjoyed every service. I love you Bishop Kelly & Ministers.  FYI due to personal circumstances I relocated to Texas with my family. God Bless You All & Love You All.

Betsy The total Worship experience is phenomenal as God's Word of Truth is always taught with an uncompromising commitment to seek after and serve the Lord with joy. The Love of God is shared with all people, the Lord Jesus Christ is lifted up and God is glorified. I have been to Way of Life many times.  Beautiful sanctuary, pleasant, kind people who make the visit very enjoyable. Excellent place to visit and definitely worthy of consideration for anyone seeking a home church. Very enjoyable. I felt like I was at a concert. Pastors message stirred my spirit. People are extremely welcoming. Great place to grow spiritually. People are extremely welcoming. If your seeking the truth this is where you want to go.

name: Ways Station Christian Church - Richmond Hill Campus
reviewSummary: When we first walked through the doors, we felt like we had come home. The wonderful, caring people here are warm and welcoming. The sermons are Bible based, the worship is meaningful, and the people are down to earth. Communion is served each week. Adult as well as Children Sunday school is offered. There are opportunities mid-week for further study and fellowship. Coastal Community church is an nice family church! The reception from church members is warm and inviting. They have a wonderful worship service and a the pastor is upbeat. We have loved being part of this church for over 10 years! Our church family welcomes and invites you to worship with us as we serve God and support our community. Great Bible teaching Christian Church! They have always welcomed me and treated me like family. Great small family church! Very friendly congregation, if you like personal connection this is the place for you!

name: Wayside Baptist Church - Pinecrest / South Miami Campus
reviewSummary:
This is the most Good News carrying, comfortable, and Fellowshipping live, laugh, and love type of experience to attend and especially becoming a member. So amazing and honorable. My family and I absolutely love this church! They make you feel like family from the start. We have seen so much growth in our relationship with the Lord and the body of Christ over the past 2 years of attending. Not the right church at all. The Pastor got upset because he and his wife wanted to pass by my house last Saturday in the morning and I had already made plans. They never called me again! I am glad. Because I don’t want to be at a church where people are odd! I believe you have God in your heart not a church. Thanks and God Bless You! Very warm and welcoming environment. Although this is a southern baptist church (SBA) , they don't really talk about the Blessed hope too much. Which is kind of a shame.

I've been going here for over a year now , I have met some wonderful people . This church is very active with its Outreach ministries, like it's visitations, its corporate prayer, and so much MORE. For instance, there is a beautiful animated movie called King of kings, coming out a week before Resurrection sunday, commonly known as Easter.

On the events page, they have a place where someone got a group rate to go watch this movie. Only $6. So I'm going to watch this movie with my church family. This is one of the nice things about this church. It's almost like we have a church within the church.

This is an updated review. I updated this in April of 2025. I don't know what the problem is, but they have been looking for a new pastor, because the other Pastor went to a church in Jacksonville Florida.

Apparently they had been through this before, I don't get into the church politics, because I just don't want to . But in order to get a pastor, they set up a pastor search committee. It has literally been OVER a year, and we have not had a new pastor yet. Why is this? We have an interim pastor, a man named Gary Johnson, he's a good pastor.

Although I personally prefer the preaching style of the one that left to JACKSONVILLE, FL more .

So let's get into the preaching, very near and dear to my heart because I want as many people to come to the Saving Grace and knowledge of Jesus the Messiah, because we all know the days that we are living in. And if anyone is reading their bibles, they would know what is coming right around the corner. But boy does the devil have people distracted. I wish they did more expository Style teaching. But they do have Bible study groups that meet before the 11 a.m. Worship On Sunday.

Worship music = AWESOME. Impressed with the Sound Stage setup, the musicians, I like the songs that they play. They try to mix it up as much as possible. It's not always contemporary Christian music, sometimes they just do acoustic sessions, sometimes the choir sings, they really mix it up a lot. There are no flashing lights, it doesn't look like a discotheque, so don't worry about that.

The only thing I find strange for a Baptist church, is that they DO NOT give out the elements for communion, in which we are TOLD to do in the scriptures. I've been to other Baptist churches who always have communion once a month at LEAST.

The other thing which I don't like, is I don't see public baptisms. Once in a blue moon, they'll bring up the topic about being baptized, but I have yet to see one here at Wayside.

I used to go to Pines Baptist Church, the one right across from the fire station. That was a wonderful Baptist church. True old school Baptist church, where they sing hymns instead of contemporary Christian music, I remember the pastor there didn't even allow drums. I miss that church.

Most Baptist Churches have one of those bathtubs right there behind the altar, in which you get baptized. That's the right way to do it. But not at Wayside. And they rarely stress getting baptized. 😔

As we all know, there is a great falling away, An apostasy that is going on throughout many churches, and I'm a little concerned about Wayside.

🚫Knowing Jesus Christ is a relationship, it has nothing to do with a religion.

And my friends, only the TRUTH will set you free. Run to Jesus the Christ as quickly as you can. The ONLY way to the Father is through the son.

"Look carefully then how you walk, not as unwise but as wise, making the best use of the time, because the days are evil. Therefore do not be foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is. And do not get drunk with wine, for that is debauchery, but be filled with the Spirit, addressing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody to the Lord with your heart, ...(Ephesians 5:15-21).

Time is literally running out. Read your Bibles ‼️ Shortly after relocating to the Miami area, my husband and I decided to begin looking for a new church home (knowing it would likely be trial and error for a bit until we felt we'd found a good fit
for us). I came across Wayside in an internet search and we joined an 11oclock worship service about 6 months ago. After our first Sunday service, we stopped our search and immediately felt this was the place God lead us to be in our time in Miami.

Wayside is a fairly large church with a two-story mezzanine and a congregation of all ages. On our first visit, pastor David, and his wife, Kelly personally greeted us as they recognized new faces and made it a point to welcome us. They were eager to introduce us to the leaders of a Sunday-school group for young adults, which has
cultivated relationships we intend to always keep. The messages we receive each week are biblical, relatable, and full of Godly wisdom in which we have been able to apply to our lives in the
past few months. We feel that God is working in a multitude of ways through Wayside and are blessed to be a part of it.

We would suggest and invite anyone to visit Wayside and see the great things that are happening here.

All of the people were  kind and welcoming. Good experience. The stage seems to be small but the atmosphere felt great. name: Wells Memorial Church of God in Christ - Greensboro Campus
reviewSummary: Was at the church for a repass. Funeral was held at funeral home but all attendees were fed at Wells memorial fellowship hall. Pastor Platt and wife and members treated us with great hospitality. Made us feel at home and fed us well. Great church great leadership. Wells Memorial is a very nice church to worship. The pastor and his colleagues are respectable and sharp. The sermons can be lengthy but deliver. You can tell God loves this church. Its apart of the Holiness C.O.G.I.C. churches. name: WellSpring Christian Church - Spring Hill Campus
reviewSummary:
Awesome atmosphere, vVery welcoming, The people are Great! it is 100% bible-based! All walks of life are welcome! This is the church that I I'm proud to call home! I was drawn to this church by a lawn sign I saw during my walk in my neighborhood. It said Love Everyone Always!  I came home and told my husband that it was a church I wanted to try and we have been going ever since. We find the sermons thought-provoking and the ministry staff is wonderful and helpful. We love our small group and feel like we have found family in this church. We moved from far away so this was important to us. We love our Wellspring Family! Wellspring is a welcoming and friendly church. There are people from all walks of life and upon entering you have people there to help you out. The youth program is amazing and Keith does such a good job making the kids feel loved and welcome. There are always fun activities for kids of all ages and I hear there will be some for adults and seniors coming soon. They have a great staff and  congregation that make you feel like you’re family, like you’re finally home. Having moved to TN to retire near our son and his family we have found the church address the needs of our whole family.  For Kay and I we have found study groups and friends at a similar life stage.  Sharing with friends similar joys and challenges is encouraging and supportive.  Our son with a young family has found activities the children ages 5, 9 and 12 in which they are eager to participate.  Our son and daughter-in-law are involved in church activities which they enjoy and have made many friendships.
The Sunday worship music is uplifting and the morning message has application to our lives.

If you are looking for a church I suggest attend a life group meeting or two as well as the worship service to become better acquainted with the life of the church. WellSpring was the church I had been looking for. My very first visit I was warmly greeted and I knew I was in the right place. name: Wellspring Church - Madison Campus
reviewSummary:
My family and I thoroughly enjoyed fellowshipping at Wellspring Church. We received an open invitation from the Dr. Larry Davis and his wife Cindy, and I’m so glad we accepted. The Pastor Matt delivered a powerful and impactful message, and the music and hospitality were truly top tier. From the moment we walked through the doors, we felt genuinely welcomed. There are many ways to become involved…women’s ministry options, men’s group options….and even more opportunities coming soon as we move into our new building! Exciting times ahead!

What a warm and wonderful group of Christians at Wellspring Church to kick start your week! I promise after the scripture filled sermons you will experience, your heart will be so full of love for Jesus and each other!
Come be a part~we saved a seat for you! Wellspring Church is a faithful, caring, and generous community of believers. Pastor Matt’s sermons are so engaging and are truly inspiring Biblical teaching. There are so many ways to get plugged in here. Come join our Methodist church. Wellspring is a great Methodist church! The sense of community here is incredible. Everyone is so welcoming and genuine cares for each other. The sermons are inspiring and thought-provoking, helping me grow in my faith every week.

Some have started other Churches some go to other Churches but my love ( and the Pastor ) for all of them is still there and always will be. The important thing is that everyone of them love and worship and love GOD.
I love this Church and everyone that goes here and has gone here. I actually love all of GOD’S children.
This is a great place to shown that love.
SPRING FIRST CHURCH. If you visit Spring First Church you will LOVE it. The singing and music is live, professional, and awesome. Most of all the Pastor and staff will bless your soul with love and anointed words from God. The congregation loves visitors and meeting new people so go in and you'll feel God's love.

name: Wellspring Community Church - Oxford Campus
reviewSummary: Make no mistake, this is the place you and your family wants to worship. The love of Christ is magnified and His name is glorified. We had a loving welcome and this church family believes in prayer and the power of the Holy Spirit. Pastor Rios and His wife are true lovers of Christ and are dedicated to spreading the Gospel. Sister Cynthia is a powerful worship leader and has a anointed voice. Thank you Wellspring for your love and hospitality. We will be back for sure next time we are in town. 🙏🏽🙏🏽. We pray God continues to guide and bless you. This church is so welcoming no matter who you are or where you come from! Pastor and his family are the best! Come let them love on you and show you how God can move and have HIS way! This is a loving church that welcomes all of oxford.ms to come and worship Jesus. The Pastor and his family work diligently to serve the community and share the Gospel of Christ. Services are @ 10 am Sunday and mid-week huddle @ 7 on Wednesdays. This church is the best! I enjoy going each service...if you are looking for a good fit for your family try Wellspring! Pastor Nathaniel Rios is authentic & genuine. If I lived in Oxford - Wellsprings would be my home church.

name: Wellspring Franklin (Formerly Grace Center) - Franklin Campus
reviewSummary: This place has hurt or betrayed a lot of people who once gave their all to this place. Still a lot of good people there. But it’s a repeated pattern that’s gone on through the lifetime of the church. Sad thing is, I guarantee you they think they’ve done nothing wrong. Guys… look at the fruit. I am not able to attend often, I watch it on TV.  I’m so thankful for the fact that I can watch church. One of my favorite things about visiting my friends in Nashville is getting to go to church at Grace Center. The Lord is always on the move and the people are passionate about Jesus. I injured my knee hiking several years back and had tremendous pain for a couple of weeks. Someone on the prayer team prayed for my knee and in an instant the Lord healed it. It has a special place in my heart for that alone. 10/10 would recommend. I thought that Grace Center was our church home family after Heidi Baker came to visit. GC was there for us after my grandmother passed in May'23. We had 3 children in diapers and more responsibility than we could well manage. We asked for childcare support in many ways, none was available. Our nearest family lived 420 mi away. This led to much frustration, exhaustion and critical attitudes in our marriage. Our GC small group is very spirit-filled and wonderful. Then, in October our 7 month old baby passed away in his sleep. And we needed prayer and support, nothing too demanding. Instead, "church leadership" informs our wonderful small group leader that I am "dismissed" bc I have more problems than the church "can provide help with"...🤨 And this is a church that "denies themselves, takes up their cross daily and follows Jesus"  correct? Luke 9:23 Our group leader was devastated being forced to dismiss me from the group (under pressure from leadership he said) and that I am "too much of a burden for the church". I do have a lot of enemies who have gossipped about me: former tenants and in-laws especially, who love to complain and judge rather than forgive. I am a servant of the gospel, sharing Jesus daily for my full-time driving job and my father was an ordained minister for 42 years. But, I would appreciate a call from church leadership so I can explain "that I am not too much to deal with" and hopefully we can cover our family in prayer instead of separating the family of God apart during tragedy when supporting each other is most important. I love my wife and I need to humble myself to her at the right time and ask her forgiveness for hurting her feelings in our marriage. GC Church and Pastor Jeff are 5 star people. Leadership gets 1 star. I hope we can be reconciled in the future. I am praying for GC. This church body truly just wants more of God and wants to do what He commissioned us to do here on earth. The staff and volunteers are genuine and warm. There are plenty of options for church services, conferences, and a consistently rotating Wednesday evening class. Theres a sweet Café to mingle inside or just grab a cup to bring to early morning service. The new children’s wing is a dream! With a quality check in and check out system your kids will be safe and will enjoy the creatively designed rooms and play structure. I love calling this place my home.

name: Wesley Church At Frederica - St. Simons Island Campus
reviewSummary:
Wesley Church in Frederica, Georgia is a beautiful and intimate venue that offers both character and functionality for events. While it’s not a massive church, that’s part of its appeal—the space feels warm, inviting, and well suited for gatherings where connection and atmosphere matter. The architecture stands out immediately, with impressive exposed wood beams and an abundance of natural light coming through large windows, creating a bright and uplifting setting.

Acoustically, the church performs extremely well. Whether for speaking or music, the sound carries clearly throughout the room, supported by a solid sound system that enhances the experience without being overwhelming. I served as the MC for a recent event there, and everything—from audio to flow—worked seamlessly.

This was our second event at Wesley Church in the past four years, and once again, it delivered. The staff was professional, attentive, and easy to work with, ensuring that every detail was handled efficiently.

If you’re in the St. Simons area and looking for a church venue for an event, Wesley Church in Frederica is a strong choice—well maintained, thoughtfully designed, and consistently reliable. Went for Maundy Thursday service where they had a live Last Supper. It was wonderful time of celebrating what the Lord did for us. Thank you for the hard work everyone put into this time of remembrance. Your church and grounds are beautiful. As a visitor, we  all felt welcomed. Very beautiful church Beautiful church filled with wonderful people. Beautiful church inside and outside. The choir walks in singing at the 10:45 service and the lesson from the sermon was great.

name: Wesley Monumental United Methodist Church - Savannah Campus
reviewSummary: This is a beautiful church right in the middle of historic Savannah, GA. The sanctuary has gorgeous stained glass windows with a huge pipe organ at the front. Was there for a family wedding and the pastor did a great job. Daughter went to preschool here at El's Place and it was the best experience. She's now moving up to public school but we will miss the teachers and staff there! Everyone was so friendly and showed love to my baby! She learned so much and always had a great time! A totally awesome worship of God experience.  Friendliness of members, outstanding traditional music, and thought-provoking, down-to-earth sermons.  You are blessed to have been a participant. Beautiful architecture and a wonderful church. John Wesley said “all the world is my parish” and this church named in he and his brother’s honor, serve Savannah housing, feeding, educating, and encouraging in the name of Jesus Christ.

name: West Anaheim United Methodist Church - Anaheim Campus
reviewSummary:
It's  been my church for 10 years. Bathrooms clean and a open space for children to play. One bench distance and 6' apart. Excellent place that takes very good care of their patients. Big, service in the morning every Monday, come and hear the God's word Need better traffic signs or directions for pick ups LOOKING TOWARDS THE PAST, PRESENT, AND FUTURE OF WEST ANAHEIM THEORY CHURCH

February 1956 - July 2025
West Anaheim Methodist Church (WAUMC) has a 70-year history. The church was founded on February 2, 1956, through the ministry of Pastor David Deshler. In its early years, the church purchased 2.5 acres of land at 2045 W. Ball Road, Anaheim, California.

The Chapel was the first building constructed in 1958. The chapel has a capacity of approximately 120 people. The main sanctuary was built in 1964 with a capacity of five hundred people. The first worship service at the church was held on January 3, 1965.

The church built three more buildings: an education center, a meeting hall, and an office building, and purchased a house at 306 Archer Street in Anaheim to serve as the pastor's family residence. In its first 15 years, WAUMC grew rapidly, reaching a peak membership of 1,700 in 1970.

Following the Vietnam War in 1975, many people left Vietnam to immigrate to the United States. In 1980, Pastor Nguyen Xuan Duc met with the WAUMC Board of Directors to express his desire to establish the first Methodist ministry for Vietnamese Americans in the United States. WAUMC welcomed him warmly, and in February 1980, Pastor Nguyen Xuan Son was appointed to begin ministry for the Vietnamese community there.

Therefore, WAUMC is the birthplace of the first Vietnamese Methodist Church in the world!

After 10 years of ministry, Pastor Nguyen Xuan Son dedicated his time to theological studies, now known as Union University of California. In January 1990, Pastor Tran Trong Luat was appointed the second pastor for the Vietnamese congregation at WAUMC. God abundantly blessed the church. Many Vietnamese families sponsored and assisted by the church accepted the Lord and became faithful and zealous believers.

On April 2, 2001, the Vietnamese congregation at WAUMC became an official church of the Methodist Church under the name "Anaheim Vietnamese United Methodist Church".

Over time, the number of American believers at WAUMC gradually changed for various reasons. By 2014, most of the English-speaking members were elderly, so they decided to merge with the Vietnamese Church, which at the time had about 150 members, to become a single church. On July 1, 2014, the two churches officially merged under the name "West Anaheim United Methodist Church."

After 27 years of dedicated service at WAUMC, Pastor Tran Trong Luat retired at the end of June 2017. Pastor Dang Thao Nhon (Esther) was appointed as his successor to serve the Vietnamese group; WAUMC still has an assistant pastor to serve the English-speaking group.

In September 2018, Pastor Thao Nhon was appointed to serve both the Vietnamese and American congregations.

After 27 years of dedicated service at WAUMC, Pastor Tran Trong Luat retired at the end of June 2017. Pastor Dang Thao Nhon (Esther) was appointed as his successor to serve the Vietnamese group; WAUMC still has an assistant pastor to serve the English-speaking group.

In September 2018, Pastor Thao Nhon was appointed to serve both the Vietnamese and American congregations.

name: West Campus
West Coast Baptist Church - Carlsbad Campus
reviewSummary:
Maturing is realizing this place is a cult guys! Because why is the pastor kinda weird? And they push the religion to extreme.. Like I've seen reviews of a people having weird experiences or this lady who got a flirtatious comment from pastor Clark! Gross? I know! Like talk about crazy. This is a church. They even believe females shouldn't work... And stay jobless! Gasppp, yeah. They will say weird comments to you most likely if you wear "too much makeup" Or "wearing shorts or pants" like this is where you worship God? Not where you care about what people are wearing. You may think these are the good guys but they aren't they have some drama too.. Like this is a church a place of God not a theatre class. Talk about embarrassing.. They try to force you perfect like crystal clear.. Well that's not happening.. Especially with this drama!!! And nobody's perfect. There's gonna be ups and downs obviously... Well whatever my point is don't go here if your not prepared for the weird pastor!  I have truly enjoyed attending this Independent Baptist church. The preaching is biblical, direct, and rooted firmly in the Word of God. This is not a “feel-good” ministry, and that is exactly what I appreciate about it. The messages are Scripture-based and focused on conviction, repentance, and holy living rather than entertainment or emotional hype.

Pastor Philip Clark is a faithful and bold preacher of the Bible. He does not water down the Word, and he does not shy away from difficult topics. The teaching is old-fashioned, biblical preaching that calls believers to examine themselves and grow spiritually.

This church stands on biblical principles, including modesty, holiness, and separation from worldliness not as man-made rules, but as convictions that flow from understanding Scripture. When you know better, you do better. The preaching challenges you, and at times conviction can feel uncomfortable, but that is the purpose of God’s Word. It is meant to refine us and draw us closer to Him.

If you are looking for a Bible-believing church that prioritizes truth over trend, Scripture over emotion, and conviction over comfort, this is a place where you will grow.

I am thankful for the clear teaching and the commitment to standing firmly on the Word of God. Hi, I'm Nathan. I'm a Marine on Camp Pendleton and I have been going to West Coast Baptist Church for 2 years now. I remember looking at the Google Maps for this church and seeing that they had reviews but never bothered to read them.  Today I read them. Before I started going to this church I was smoking, drinking, cursing, living for myself, living a life unpleasing to God.
Growing up, My church back home didn't know the gospel well, but by the grace of God, I was saved at a young age. I believed on Jesus Christ and repented. I believed God's Word. But my church back home never told me anything about baptism, which comes after salvation or about discipleship(going through God's word with another saved person that's been living out the christian life), which ought to be done with every newly saved Christian. I had little to no spiritual growth until I actually started reading my bible in about 10th grade. Through God's Word, I realized I wasn't living according to God's Word (I was worldly) and that my church was not following the Bible. My pastor couldn't even answer some of my questions. Over time these realizations lead me to have a strong desire to leave my church; and I believe this was the pull of the Holy Spirit on my life to bring me closer to God and to a strong Bible believing Church. That lead me to start technical school, which lead me to join the USMC which lead me into alcohol, cussing, and smoking at times. I was receiving the chastisement of God because of those actions and would ask God, "why am I going through these things?Why is my life so miserable?" But God lead me to this church. I was walking on a Sunday morning already dressed and going somewhere( I forget where), and I see someone From my shop walking in nice clothes, church clothes, and I ask him where he's going. He tells me he's going to church. I say, oh, I'm looking for a church. Can I come with? and he Says, sure. And I went there and realized, this is where I need to be. This is where I can Grow. Then I joined the church. I got discipled by one of the men at the church. I learned in their Bible institute. I went soul winning(going out with the church and telling people about Jesus Christ) for the first time in my life, and didn't stop going. I can now give an answer for the faith I hold. I can now actually present the Gospel Jesus Christ to anyone who asks. I never really had a problem with alcohol or smoking growing up, but after I joined this church two years ago, I haven't touched alcohol or smoked since then. I've submitted to be a preacher and to start churches. We preach the whole Bible, we preach Jesus Christ and Him crucified, we preach repentance toward God and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ. There are some negative comments here; and I wasn't at the church long enough to really know what was going on with those comments, but I hope that my short testimony can extinguish those fiery darts. God Bless. Take care. Great church that is faithful to the Word of God.  The people are very friendly and caring.  They preach the true gospel faithfully and boldly, worship God in spirit and in truth, and seek to live consistent Christian lives out of love for the resurrected Lord, Jesus Christ.  If we lived in the area (instead of, as we currently were, visiting it) we would gladly be members of this church and serve the Lord there. Joline Solomon left a review a year ago. A rebuking review with details of her experience. Sadly this is not the 1st time this type of incident has happened. My mother experienced the same experience when her and my dad met with Wesley Clark, at the time. He ran his eyes from top to bottom and made similar comments. In my own personal experience also, the Gossip in Leadership was so bad I decided to leave. After I did the next Sunday the Pastor got up in Church and excommunicated me and asked the church members to have nothing to do with me. Cult is a fitting word for this place.
